chapters.title: Chapter 701. The Underlayer Is No Longer the Prey. I Came to Make That Point Personally.
paragraphs: Rex didn’t wait for her to recover. He didn’t even wait for her to reach him. As Kaelira surged forward, a living comet of heat and will, Rex simply tightened the reins of reality.

He increased the gravity field around himself, creating a localized zone of crushing density. The air itself seemed to thicken, turning into a viscous, invisible liquid that resisted her every movement.
She hit the edge of his field at full speed. The collision was silent but violent.
The resistance was immediate and absolute. Kaelira’s expression shifted from fierce determination to a mask of sheer strain in a fraction of a second.
She managed two more steps, her boots grinding into the cracked stone, before the weight differential became too much to bear. She stopped, her body trembling under the unnatural load.

Her flames flickered, the heat dimming as her body diverted every ounce of energy just to keep her lungs expanding against the crushing pressure. Rex watched her through the haze of dust, his eyes gleaming with a predatory intellect.
"As usual... glad to see that you’re finally well and relevant again with that Berserker class," Rex stated, his voice cutting through the heavy air with a cocky, analytical precision.
He didn’t look at her like a warrior; he looked at her like a puzzle. "The designation amplifies rage conversion."
"The more damage you take, the more output you produce. It’s a fascinating loop."

Kaelira glared at him through the shimmering heat distortion, her teeth gritted so hard it sounded like stone grinding against stone. She didn’t speak; she simply breathed, each inhalation a battle against the gravity that wanted to collapse her ribcage.
"That is genuinely impressive," Rex continued, his tone dripping with a mocking admiration. "But it also means you improve as the fight gets worse."
"And the rational play, from a strategic perspective, is to never let the fight get worse."
"Funny," Kaelira spat, the word sounding like it was being squeezed out of her throat. "Coming from the man who just tore the plaza apart for fun."
"It wasn’t just for fun," Rex replied, a small, arrogant smirk playing on his lips. "Well. Not entirely."
In a sudden, violent motion, Rex expanded the field. He pushed the gravity radius out to a four-meter circle and slammed the intensity up to eight times standard gravity.
The effect was brutal. Kaelira’s knees buckled.
With a sound like a heavy weight hitting the earth, she dropped to one knee. The ground beneath her shattered, a spiderweb of cracks blooming outward from her impact.
A small trickle of blood escaped her lip, a crimson stain against the dust, as the pressure forced the very fluid in her body to strive against the weight.
"Kaelira!" Apollo’s voice roared, a sound of pure agony and fury.
Rex didn’t even blink. He stood there, the center of the storm, looking down at her with the calmness of a god watching an ant.
"Let her go!" Apollo commanded, his voice trembling with a controlled rage that was rapidly fraying.
He was stepping forward, his light flaring so bright it blinded the nearby soldiers.
"She is not in danger," Rex said, his voice flat and unyielding.
"She is on her knees under eight times gravity!" Apollo countered, his voice cracking with the strain of his emotions. "You are crushing her!
"She is on one knee," Rex corrected, his tone almost insulting in its casualness. "She is holding it, as you can see."
’Most combatants would have had their bones splintered and their organs ruptured by now. But she is performing exceptionally well."
Apollo’s energy signature spiked so violently the air itself seemed to vibrate. "You don’t get to decide what is ’well’ for my people!"
"I am not deciding for them," Rex replied, his eyes locking onto Apollo’s with a defiant, cocky glare. "I am telling you what the reality is."
"If you want to argue with the laws of physics, be my guest. But don’t mistake my observation for disrespect."
Apollo’s face contorted. The light radiating from him was no longer a warm glow; it was a blinding, white-hot radiance that threatened to consume the plaza.
The tension between them was a physical force, a coiled spring ready to snap.
"You think this is a game?" Apollo hissed, his voice low and dangerous. "You think you can just walk in here and treat our lives like variables in your calculations?"
"I think," Rex said, his voice dropping to a low, challenging thrum, "that you are reacting with emotion where you should be reacting with logic."
"And in a fight, emotion is just another way to die."

Apollo’s light intensified, a blinding explosion of pure willpower that seemed to drown out the sun itself. The battle was no longer just about the golems or the gravity; it was a collision of two unstoppable forces, and the world was caught in the middle.
The air in the plaza didn’t just vibrate; it screamed. As Apollo’s light expanded, the very atmosphere seemed to undergo a biological scale reversal.

It was a terrifyingly beautiful display of power, a radiance so pure it felt like the reversal of entropy itself. Where the light touched the ground, dust didn’t just settle; it re-energized, dancing in a frenzy of unnatural vitality.
Rex stood at the center of this storm, his eyes narrowed. He could feel it.
The light was not just light; it was the presence of a god-like force. It was the ultimate counter to the decay of the world.
To anyone else, this energy would have been a blessing, a surge of life that would have made their hearts race and their veins throb with a renewed strength. But Rex knew the truth.
To be caught in the maw of this light was to be overwhelmed by the sheer force of life itself. But Rex was not a man of flesh and blood alone.
He grounded himself. Through the armor of his suit, he established a connection to the very foundation of the island.
The Earthen Authority surged through him, a river of stone and granite. He wasn’t just a man standing in the light; he was an extension of the crust of the planet.
He anchored his existence to the unyielding mass of the substrata. The stone was his shield, and the stone was his soul.

While the light sought to revitalize and reorder the organic, Rex had made himself a monument of the inorganic. He was an anomaly in the flow of Apollo’s power, a dense, unmoving weight of pure mineral will.
"That’s new," Rex said, his voice cutting through the hum of the radiance with the casualness of a man discussing the weather.
He looked at the blinding glare of Apollo’s aura with the clinical gaze of a scholar examining a new specimen. "You’ve gotten stronger since the canyon.
"Considerably stronger, actually. I’d say congratulations, but the look on your face tells me you’re not in the mood."
Apollo’s light flared, a pulse of pure gold that seemed to shudder the very air. The tension was so thick it felt like it could be sliced with a blade.
"We are not going to resolve this by talking," Rex continued, his voice dropping into a register of unshakeable certainty. "You have made that clear, and I have made it clear."
"The situation has a momentum now that talking cannot redirect."
"Then what do you want?" Apollo demanded, his voice a low thrum of controlled fury.
The light around him was no longer a glow; it was a predator, waiting to strike.
"The same thing I wanted before this began," Rex replied, his posture as rigid as the stone he commanded. "I want the Apostle network to understand that the underlayer is no longer the prey."
"And I want every reincarnator on this island to have the choice that the network is currently stealing from them."
Apollo’s eyes burned with a fierce intensity. "And you think the way to do that is to fight me?"
Rex didn’t blink. He didn’t even flinch.
He simply looked at the man across the shattered plaza with a flat, unyielding honesty. "Yes."
The silence that followed was more violent than the clash of swords. It was a heavy silence, a void in which the world seemed to hold its breath, waiting to fill.
"That’s it?" Apollo asked, his voice laced with a bitter disbelief. "Just... yes?"
"No grand speech about the fate of the world? No philosophical justification about the balance of the cosmos? You just... decide to fight?"
"Would it change anything if I gave you one?" Rex countered, a trace of a smirk playing on his lips. It was a defiant, cocky expression that mocked the very gravity of the moment.
Apollo didn’t answer. He couldn’t.

The weight of his own power, the pressure of his resolve, and the sheer intensity of the moment seemed to choke the words from his throat. He merely stared, his jaw tight, his eyes burning with a light that could melt stone.
"Then let’s not waste time," Rex said, his voice turning as cold as the deep earth.
He shifted his weight, the armor of his body creaking with the anticipation of the clash. "I’ve got a busy day."
The challenge was thrown. The stage was set.
The very air seemed to shudder in anticipation of the collision that was about to shatter the world.

chapters.title: Chapter 702. He Made Me Work for It. That Is the Nicest Thing I Will Say About Him Today
paragraphs: The tension in the plaza didn’t just break; it shattered.

Apollo raised his hand, and the light that erupted from his palm was no longer the soothing, rejuvenating glow of a healer. It was a lance of compressed divinity, a concentrated beam of reality-warping force.
The strike slammed into Rex’s stone armor with the sound of a mountain splitting. The force was immense, enough to crater the ground beneath his feet and slide his heavy frame backward a half step.
Rex’s eyes narrowed behind his mask. He felt the vibration of the impact rattling his very marrow, but he didn’t even flinch.
The armor held and the anchor also held.
"Is that everything?" Rex asked, his voice dripping with a casual, almost insulting nonchalance.
The mask hid his expression, but the sheer arrogance of the question was palpable. "Because if so, this is going to be over a lot faster than I expected."
Then, the predator moved.
Rex surged forward, and the world seemed to groan under the sudden shift in momentum. When Apollo engaged, it wasn’t a fight of blades or fists; it was a collision of fundamental physics.

Apollo’s offense was a violent clash of realities. By reversing entropy in a localized zone, he created a ’boundary condition,’ a jagged, violent edge where the laws of physics simply refused to agree.
It was like slamming two different universes together.
The first forty seconds were a blur of destruction. The plaza, already scarred, was systematically dismantled.
Rex took three direct strikes, the impacts sounding like thunderclaps. The stone armor groaned, pitting and cracking under the pressure of Apollo’s divine output, but it held.
In retaliation, Rex unleashed a telekinetic surge of lethal precision. He caught Apollo in a grip of gravity, lifting him six meters into the air.
"Four seconds," Rex remarked, his voice cutting through the roar of the clash.
He was analyzing, calculating, his mind as cold as the stone he commanded. "Last time, you needed three."
"You’re slowing down, Apollo."
"Shut up and fight!" Apollo roared, his voice a commanding thunder.
He broke the hold with a burst of light that shattered the air itself.
As the two titans clashed, the battlefield became a meat grinder of elemental force. Nearby, Calivara, seeing the opening, moved with the lethal grace of a predator.
She didn’t target Rex; she knew her target was the golems. She understood the geometry of the chaos.
She unleashed her blood affinity, a visceral, terrifying power. Her first strike was a surge of corrosive energy that melted the stone of the first golem like acid on flesh.

The second golem, a massive construct of granite, was caught in a pressure differential. She forced the blood like energy into the seams of the stone, and with a sickening CRACK, the golem exploded from the inside out, its internal structure pulverized by the sudden expansion of pressure.
But the third golem was different. It wasn’t an autonomous construct; it was a vessel of Rex’s own will, a living extension of the Earthen Authority.
It moved with a purposeful, unyielding weight that the other golems lacked.
Calivara poured everything into her defense, her blood affinity forming a shimmering, viscous barrier. But the golem didn’t care about physics or logic.
It was a wall of pure mass, driven by the will of a god-like entity.
The collision was brutal. The golem smashed through her defensive field like a hammer through glass.

The impact sent her flying backward, a streak of motion across the shattered plaza. She slammed into the remnants of a decorative wall with a bone-jarring thud, the stone splintering around her as she was swallowed by the debris.

The dust settled for a fraction of a second, leaving only the sound of Rex and Apollo’s breathing and the smell of burnt ozone and crushed stone. The fight was far from over; it was only just beginning to bleed.
The air in the plaza didn’t just hum; it screamed with the friction of colliding realities.
As Eryndra, the astral summoner, began her work, the very fabric of the dimension seemed to shudder. Her energy didn’t strike the world like a hammer; it unraveled it like a thread.

Rex felt the sensation through his armor, not a physical impact, but a structural dissonance, a vibration that rattled his very essence. The golems near her began to lose their coherence, their stone-like forms blurring as the fundamental principle holding them together was stripped away.
Rex didn’t hesitate. He was a maestro of chaos.

He reasserted his authority, lacing the geological relay with his own will to stabilize the crumbling formations. But the cost was heavy. Managing the Apollo clash, the Kaelira gravity field, and now the astral instability was a mental drain that would have shattered a lesser man.
"Too many variables," Rex muttered, his voice a low growl of pure focus.
With a violent gesture, he tore seven new golems from the shattered rubble of the plaza. They rose like jagged monoliths, born of dust and fury.
He didn’t waste a second; he sent four of them screaming toward Eryndra.
She was swift—terrifyingly fast. Before the golems could crush her, she was already airborne, her body defying gravity through astral buoyancy.
She moved like a ghost in the wind, a shimmering afterimage of presence.
Rex saw his opening. He released the grip on Kaelira.
He didn’t let her up slowly; he dropped the gravity field instantly. The sudden release of eight times the pressure was like a vacuum snapping shut.
Kaelira, who had been bracing against the crushing weight, surged upward with a violent, uncontrolled force. She staggered, her balance momentarily shattered by the sudden void of resistance.
"Now," Rex hissed.
He was a blur of stone and intent. He ignored the distractions, his eyes locked on Apollo.
He moved across the thirty meters of broken rubble in a heartbeat, his boots thundering against the earth. He was a force of nature, a landslide given human form.
As he ran, he reached into the very substrate of the world, pulling compressed earth and stone into his momentum, augmenting his mass and power with every stride.
Apollo met him in the center of the carnage. The collision was a tectonic event.
Apollo unleashed a directed working of pure light, a lance of divine energy. Rex didn’t dodge.

He summoned a wall of compacted stone from the ground, a shield of granite that caught the impact. The shield shattered under the force, sending a spray of shrapnel and stone shards flying like bullets across the plaza, but the momentum was preserved.
Rex pushed through the debris. Apollo rolled, his movements fluid and desperate, launching a close-range strike.
Rex took the hit directly on his chest plate. The sound was like a mountain collapsing.
The armor cracked, a spiderweb of fractures blooming across the stone surface, but the inner layer held.
Rex didn’t even blink. He reached out.
His gauntleted hands, heavy with the weight of the Earthen Authority, clamped onto Apollo’s arm. It wasn’t a strike; it was a capture.
The grip was absolute, a lock of stone on flesh that felt like the closing of a tomb.

The tension in the air was suffocating. Apollo was straining, his muscles bulging, his breath coming in ragged gasps as he fought against the unyielding strength of the man who seemed to have the weight of the world in his fingers.

"You’re stronger up close than you let people believe," Apollo gritted out, his voice strained, his eyes burning with a mixture of exhaustion and respect. "All those matches... you were holding back."
Rex leaned in, his face inches from Apollo’s, his expression a mask of arrogant triumph. A dark, charismatic smirk pulled at the corner of his lips.
"Every single one," Rex replied, his voice a low, deadly rumble. "You should be flattered, Apollo."
"Most men would have been crushed by the weight of my presence alone. But you? You actually made me work for it."
He tightened his grip, the stone of his gauntlets grinding against the air itself.
"I gave you a fair fight," Rex added, his eyes gleaming with the pride of a predator. "But don’t mistake my mercy for weakness."
"In this arena, there is only one truth: the one who stands wins."

The shield shattered under the force, sending a spray of shrapnel and stone shards flying like bullets across the plaza, but the momentum was preserved.
Rex pushed through the debris.
Apollo rolled, his movements fluid and desperate, launching a close-range strike.
Rex took the hit directly on his chest plate.
The sound was like a mountain collapsing.
The armor cracked, a spiderweb of fractures blooming across the stone surface, but the inner layer held.
Rex didn’t even blink.
He reached out.
His gauntleted hands, heavy with the weight of the Earthen Authority, clamped onto Apollo’s arm.
It wasn’t a strike; it was a capture.
The grip was absolute, a lock of stone on flesh that felt like the closing of a tomb.
The tension in the air was suffocating.
Apollo was straining, his muscles bulging, his breath coming in ragged gasps as he fought against the unyielding strength of the man who seemed to have the weight of the world in his fingers.
"You’re stronger up close than you let people believe," Apollo gritted out, his voice strained, his eyes burning with a mixture of exhaustion and respect.
"All those matches... you were holding back."
Rex leaned in, his face inches from Apollo’s, his expression a mask of arrogant triumph.
A dark, charismatic smirk pulled at the corner of his lips.
"Every single one," Rex replied, his voice a low, deadly rumble.
"You should be flattered, Apollo."
"Most men would have been crushed by the weight of my presence alone.
But you?
You actually made me work for it."
He tightened his grip, the stone of his gauntlets grinding against the air itself.
"I gave you a fair fight," Rex added, his eyes gleaming with the pride of a predator.
"But don’t mistake my mercy for weakness."
"In this arena, there is only one truth: the one who stands wins."

chapters.title: Chapter 703. Watching You Work Through the Problem Is Interesting Than Just Winning.
paragraphs: The tension in the plaza was no longer just a feeling; it was a physical weight, a suffocating pressure that made the very air feel thick with the scent of ozone, pulverized stone, and the metallic tang of blood.

As Apollo transitioned into his close-range adaptation, the fight shifted from a clash of macro forces to a brutal, intimate struggle of physics and will. Rex felt the shift immediately. The life affinity wasn’t just a light source; it was a predatory force.
As his armored forearm pressed against Apollo’s chest, the stone armor began to react. The designation’s entropy reversal wasn’t just healing Apollo; it was actively reknitting the stone itself.
The cracks in the armor began to hiss and glow, the stone plates fusing back together as if the very matter were being commanded to remember its unbroken state.
"You heal fast," Rex grunted, his voice a low rumble of approval. "Faster than the canyon. I’m noting that down."
"Glad to be of service to your research," Apollo spat, his eyes burning with a ferocity that matched the heat of the clash.
"And it seems you really looked at me well enough!" He was already moving, a blur of motion that defied the heaviness of the atmosphere.
But Rex was not alone in the chaos. High above, Eryndra’s astral signature descended like a silent predator.

She unleashed an astral working, a frequency designed to shatter the very structure of his constructs. But Rex was a master of the field. With the calculated precision of a god, he didn’t just deflect it; he captured the frequency.
Using his energy manipulation, he mirrored her own signature, throwing her own weapon back at her with a three-second delay.
The result was a visceral catastrophe. The astral frequency hit Eryndra’s form, and the medium of her own power turned against her.
She fell from the sky like a broken bird, hitting the ground with a sickening thud that echoed through the plaza.
Before the dust could settle, Calivara was already there. She was a whirlwind of lethal intent.

She bypassed the golems and the stone, her eyes locked on the vulnerabilities of the man. She used a powerful attack that targeted the blood vessels of her living opponent, aiming to damage their internal fluids.
It was a strike meant to burst veins and shatter organs.
But it hit the unyielding wall of the earthen authority. The attack washed over the stone armor like water over a mountain.
Rex turned his head, his gaze cold and analytical.
"Blood pressure working," he observed, his voice devoid of strain. "Against a stone target."
Calivera didn’t flinch. Her face was a mask of intense focus, her breath coming in short, sharp bursts.
"That was a diagnostic," she countered, her voice tight with the adrenaline of the fight.
"What did you learn?" Rex asked, his tone almost teasing, as if he were testing a student rather than fighting for survival.
"You have biological material inside the armor," she replied, her hands still dancing through the air as she shaped her next attack. "The designation’s circulatory targeting found nothing to grip."
"Your internal systems are shielded.
"Correct," Rex said, a faintly arrogant smirk playing on his lips. "But the stone breaks."
"It does," Calivara snapped, her eyes flashing. "I saw the cracks, and the chest plate gave."
"And you’re walking me through this," Rex noted, his voice dripping with the swagger of a man who was entirely in control of the carnage. "Why?"
"Because you’re going to be wrong about what comes next!" she shouted, her voice a war cry.
Rex let out a short, dark laugh. "Because you’re going to be wrong about what comes next, regardless."
"And frankly, watching you work through the problem is more interesting than just winning."
The arrogance was staggering. He was standing in the middle of a warzone, surrounded by blood and shattered stone, and he was treating the entire engagement like a philosophical debate.
Calivara didn’t respond with words. She responded with violence.

She unleashed a new application of her power, a technique so unorthodox and so intense that it defied the standard taxonomy of her affinity. It wasn’t the crushing pressure of blood flow, nor was it the corrosive acid of her previous strike.
It was something else entirely, a visceral, bloody surge of energy that seemed to throb with a life of its own.

The air itself seemed to bleed as she poured everything into the strike, her eyes burning with the determination to shatter the man who dared to mock her intellect with his calmness. The clash was no longer just a fight; it was a collision of wills, a bloody dance of death and defiance.

The air in the plaza didn’t just vibrate; it groaned under the weight of a dimensional pressure. The atmosphere itself felt thin, as if the presence of the astral summons was sucking the very oxygen out of the lungs of the living.
Eryndra, sprawled in the dust and tasting the copper of her own blood, forced her spirit upward. She didn’t just summon; she tore the veil.

Seven massive, ethereal entities materialized at the boundary of reality, monstrous, translucent shapes that defied the laws of light and shadow. They were titans of the astral plane, looming over the battlefield like ghosts of gods.
But the unseen did not intimidate Rex.
He stood amidst the carnage, his eyes glowing with a predatory intellect. He didn’t even flinch.
He watched the seven entities with a cold, calculating gaze. Using the depths of his energy manipulation, he parsed their frequency, and he saw the rhythm of their existence.
"Too loud," Rex muttered, his voice a low thrumming growl.
He didn’t just counter them; he erased them. He channeled his elemental magic into a new frequency, a destructive interference pattern.
It wasn’t a strike; it was a mathematical execution. He unleashed a wave of cancellation resonance.
The seven entities didn’t explode; they simply ceased. One moment they were towering monsters of energy; the next, they were nothing but a flicker of starlight before dissolving into the void.
Eryndra let out a sound, a hollow gasp that was half sob and half exhale, as her essence was drained of its glory. She collapsed, her body limp, her spirit spent.
"You killed them," Kaelira whispered from the shadows, her eyes wide.
"They were fighting," Rex replied, his voice devoid of emotion, as if he were merely commenting on the weather.
He didn’t look back. He was already moving, his gaze fixed on the next target.
Apollo stepped forward, his face tight with a growing dread. "They are alive, but--"
"They are alive," Rex interrupted, his voice cutting like a blade. "Eryndra is depleted, and Calivara is making a choice."
"That is all that matters."
He began to walk toward Calivara. Every step he took sounded like the hammering of a blacksmith.
Calivara stood her ground, her breath ragged, her body coated in the dust of the plaza and the mist of her own blood. She looked at him with the eyes of a warrior who knew she was walking into a maw.
"You’re not going to give me an out," she said, her voice steady despite the tremor in her limbs.
Rex stopped exactly four meters away. The tension between them was a physical force, a cord stretched to the breaking point.
"You have been analyzing my defenses since the start," Rex said, his voice dripping with a dark charisma. "You found the vulnerability and you found the limitations."
"You are a lethal intelligence, Calivara."
He leaned forward slightly, his presence crushing. "But what comes next has nothing to do with your skill... It has everything to do with your debt."
"Everything has a cost," Calivara spat, her hands trembling as she began to weave the next working. "I knew that the moment I chose a side."
"Then you understand," Rex said, a cruel smirk playing on his lips. "The cost is coming."
"It is," she replied, her eyes burning with a defiant fire. "And I will pay it."
In that moment, the plaza went silent. The only sound was the hiss of escaping steam and the heavy thud of Rex’s heartbeat.

Calivara began to assemble her ultimate technique. It was a masterpiece of blood and will. She drew the very fluid from her veins, her skin turning a deathly pale as she channeled her life force into a concentrated surge of pure biological power.

The workings she built were a monstrosity of math and muscle, a shimmering vortex of crimson energy that ripped through the air with a whistling scream. It was the most sophisticated assault Rex had ever faced, a strike designed to shatter not just the armor but the man himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 704. Apollo Healed My Armor. I Genuinely Did Not See That Coming. (Well Played)
paragraphs: The air in the plaza didn’t just feel heavy; it felt thick, like breathing liquid lead. The tension was a physical cord stretched so tight it threatened to snap the very reality of the space around them.
Rex didn’t even move his feet. He simply raised his right hand, his fingers curling as if grasping the throat of the world itself.
"Gravity," he commanded.
The effect was instantaneous and brutal. The gravity field didn’t just increase; it slammed into Calivara like a falling mountain.
The force quadrupled, a crushing weight that demanded every ounce of her will to resist. She didn’t fly back; she was driven down.

Her knees hit the cracked stone with a sound like a hammer striking an anvil, the impact sending a shockwave of dust through the air. She went to her knees with the practiced, grim precision of a veteran, her body instinctively bracing for the load she knew was coming.
She attempted to fight back, her blood magic pulsing as she tried to generate internal pressure to counteract the external crush, but it was a losing battle.
"Blood working," Rex observed, his voice dripping with a terrifyingly calm arrogance. "It generates localized pressure."
"But gravity? Gravity is universal."
"It hits every atom of your mass simultaneously..." Rex laughed. "You’re trying to fight a tide with a spoon, Calivara."
She looked up at him, her eyes burning with a defiant intelligence. "Tch!"
"I know," she grunted through clenched teeth. "Just confirming... we’re on the same page."
"Good," Rex smirked, his eyes cold. "Some people get noisy when they’re about to break."
"I find the noise... tedious."
He didn’t wait for a rebuttal. He increased the pressure again.
The weight doubled, then tripled. Calivara was forced down, her face inches from the dust, her breath coming in ragged, stifled gasps.
She was no longer standing; she was a warrior pinned under the weight of a god.
But then, a new sound erupted from the periphery. A sound of pure, unadulterated fury.
Kaelira was coming.
She wasn’t just running; she was a streak of heat and rage, a living conflagration. The berserker designation had triggered.
The death of her companion, the collapse of Calivara, the sheer brutality of the fight—it all fed the flame. She was a walking explosion of biological fury.
Rex turned his head, a predatory grin spreading across his face.
"There it is," he muttered. "The ceiling breaker."
Kaelira hit him like a meteor. The impact was a cacophony of cracking stone and roaring flame.
Her first strike was a conflagration of eight hundred degrees, a heat so intense it seemed to melt the very air. The outer plates of his armor groaned, the stone shrieking under the stress.
CRACK.
She began to strike. Her fists were not just fists; they were hammers of fury.
Thud. Crack. Boom.
Each blow was a sledgehammer of flesh and force. The armor groaned, the Earthen Authority working feverishly to repair the fractures even as she created them.
The sound was a rhythmic violence: the crunch of stone, the hiss of steam, and the grunt of exertion.
Rex stood there, a monolith of calmness in the center of the storm. He let her strike and he let the heat burn. He let the rage wash over him.
"Go on," he taunted, his voice cutting through the roar of the flames. His face was inches from her fist as she swung. "This is the part where the rage is supposed to make you stronger."
"Show me the limit!"
"Shut... up!" Kaelira screamed, her voice a raw howl of pain and power.
She was pounding him, her body a blur of motion, her hits turning the armor into a grinding mill of shrapnel and dust. But Rex was counting.
He was watching the rhythm of her breath, the cadence of her strikes, the way her energy signature began to flicker like a dying candle.
He saw the moment the rhythm broke. The moment the exhaustion overrode the adrenaline.
"There it is," Rex said, his voice almost gentle, almost pitying. "The ceiling."
As the exhaustion threshold was crossed, Rex didn’t give her a second to recover. He didn’t give her a chance to breathe.
He unleashed the gravity again.
The weight slammed into her like a physical hammer. The momentum of her rage was shattered. Kaelira’s limbs, heavy as lead, were forced down.
She fell to her knees, her breath coming in ragged, wet sobs of exhaustion. The heat was still there, but the fire was dying, leaving only the smoldering embers of her will.
Rex stepped forward, his shadow looming over her like a tombstone.
"You’re done," he said, the words as final as a closing grave.

The air in the plaza didn’t just hum; it screamed. The tension had reached a fever pitch where the atmosphere itself felt brittle, like glass ready to shatter under the weight of the unspoken will of gods.
The punch didn’t just arrive; it detonated.
It wasn’t Kaelira’s fury this time. It was a calculated catastrophe.

Apollo had leveraged the debris of the eastern wall, using the shattered remains of the merchant district as a tactical shroud. The punch came from a blind spot in the geometry of the fight, a sudden, divine class impact that bypassed Rex’s perceived defenses.
CRACK BOOM!
The sound was like a mountain splitting in two. The force of the blow, a concentrated burst of divine output, slammed into Rex’s armored flank.

The stone plates didn’t just crack; they exploded into shrapnel, shards of granite and dust flying like lethal shrapnel. Rex was thrown sideways, his boots carving deep furrows into the plaza floor as he was launched backward.
He cleared fifteen meters of rubble in a single, violent arc, his body a blur of motion until he slammed into the ruins of a merchant’s ground floor. The wall buckled and the ceiling groaned.
He came to a halt amidst the splintered wood and crushed stone of a home turned grave.
Rex stood up, brushing a layer of dust from his shoulder. He didn’t look hurt; he looked annoyed.
He looked back across the plaza, his eyes narrowing as he analyzed the chaos.

Apollo stood there, his arm wrapped around Kaelira’s waist to support her exhausted frame. But they weren’t just standing; they were fusing. A radiant, golden light was flowing from Apollo into Kaelira, not the slow, healing drip of a spell but a violent, rapid surge of entropy reversal.
It was a biological overclocking. Apollo was feeding his very essence into her cells, rebuilding her stamina in real time.

Kaelira’s energy signature was rebuilding itself, her breath hitching as her body was forced back into a state of combat readiness. The rage conversion was still active, fueled by the life affinity surge.
It was a loop: Apollo gave her life, and her rage converted that life into pure, destructive output.
Rex watched them, and for the first time, a genuine spark of respect flickered in his eyes. "Hoh...?"
"That’s... new," he called out, his voice cutting through the dust like a blade. He stepped out from the wreckage, his presence commanding. "I take it back."
"That’s genuinely a fucking good idea, and you should have led with that."
"We were saving it," Apollo grunted, his voice strained, his face tight with the effort of the transfer.
The energy flow was a double-edged sword; it was rebuilding her, but it was draining him at a terrifying rate.
"Smart," Rex countered, his voice dripping with his usual arrogance. He began to walk forward, his gait steady. "But let’s be real."
"You’re advertising your limit right now, and I can see it," Rex crossed his arms. "The drain is visible."
"You’re bleeding energy faster than you can replenish it."
He paused, his eyes scanning the field with the precision of a predator. "You have four minutes max, and that’s your ceiling."
"You’re already halfway there."
But Rex’s gaze didn’t just stay on the people. He looked at the ground.
He looked at the way the life affinity field was bleeding into the environment. The entropy reversal wasn’t just healing Kaelira; it was rippling outward. It was touching the broken stone.
It was touching the debris.
And then, Rex realized.
A low, dark laugh bubbled up from his throat. It wasn’t the mocking laugh of a villain, nor the theatrical boast of a conqueror.
It was the laugh of a man who had just seen the punchline to a cosmic joke. It was a genuine, unfiltered burst of amusement.
He laughed because the very thing they were using to survive was changing the rules of the fight itself.
"You healed... the outer plates," Rex said, his voice booming across the plaza, his eyes shining with a manic, triumphant light. "You actually healed the armor."

The air in the plaza didn’t just hum; it screamed.
The tension had reached a fever pitch where the atmosphere itself felt brittle, like glass ready to shatter under the weight of the unspoken will of gods.
The punch didn’t just arrive; it detonated.
It wasn’t Kaelira’s fury this time.
It was a calculated catastrophe.
Apollo had leveraged the debris of the eastern wall, using the shattered remains of the merchant district as a tactical shroud.
The punch came from a blind spot in the geometry of the fight, a sudden, divine class impact that bypassed Rex’s perceived defenses.
CRACK BOOM!
The sound was like a mountain splitting in two.
The force of the blow, a concentrated burst of divine output, slammed into Rex’s armored flank.
The stone plates didn’t just crack; they exploded into shrapnel, shards of granite and dust flying like lethal shrapnel.
Rex was thrown sideways, his boots carving deep furrows into the plaza floor as he was launched backward.
He cleared fifteen meters of rubble in a single, violent arc, his body a blur of motion until he slammed into the ruins of a merchant’s ground floor.
The wall buckled and the ceiling groaned.
He came to a halt amidst the splintered wood and crushed stone of a home turned grave.
Rex stood up, brushing a layer of dust from his shoulder.
He didn’t look hurt; he looked annoyed.
He looked back across the plaza, his eyes narrowing as he analyzed the chaos.
Apollo stood there, his arm wrapped around Kaelira’s waist to support her exhausted frame.
But they weren’t just standing; they were fusing.
A radiant, golden light was flowing from Apollo into Kaelira, not the slow, healing drip of a spell but a violent, rapid surge of entropy reversal.
It was a biological overclocking.
Apollo was feeding his very essence into her cells, rebuilding her stamina in real time.
Kaelira’s energy signature was rebuilding itself, her breath hitching as her body was forced back into a state of combat readiness.
The rage conversion was still active, fueled by the life affinity surge.
It was a loop: Apollo gave her life, and her rage converted that life into pure, destructive output.
Rex watched them, and for the first time, a genuine spark of respect flickered in his eyes.
"That’s... new," he called out, his voice cutting through the dust like a blade.
He stepped out from the wreckage, his presence commanding.
"I take it back."
"That’s genuinely a fucking good idea, and you should have led with that."
"We were saving it," Apollo grunted, his voice strained, his face tight with the effort of the transfer.
The energy flow was a double-edged sword; it was rebuilding her, but it was draining him at a terrifying rate.
"Smart," Rex countered, his voice dripping with his usual arrogance.
He began to walk forward, his gait steady.
"But let’s be real."
"You’re advertising your limit right now, and I can see it," Rex crossed his arms.
"The drain is visible."
"You’re bleeding energy faster than you can replenish it."
He paused, his eyes scanning the field with the precision of a predator.
"You have four minutes max, and that’s your ceiling."
"You’re already halfway there."
But Rex’s gaze didn’t just stay on the people.
He looked at the ground.
He looked at the way the life affinity field was bleeding into the environment.
The entropy reversal wasn’t just healing Kaelira; it was rippling outward.
It was touching the broken stone.
It was touching the debris.
And then, Rex realized.
A low, dark laugh bubbled up from his throat.
It wasn’t the mocking laugh of a villain, nor the theatrical boast of a conqueror.
It was the laugh of a man who had just seen the punchline to a cosmic joke.
It was a genuine, unfiltered burst of amusement.
He laughed because the very thing they were using to survive was changing the rules of the fight itself.
"You healed... the outer plates," Rex said, his voice booming across the plaza, his eyes shining with a manic, triumphant light.
"You actually healed the armor."

chapters.title: Chapter 705. Twenty Seconds, Give or Take. I Was Right
paragraphs: The air in the plaza didn’t just vibrate; it felt like it was being shredded by the sheer force of the clash. The tension was no longer a psychological weight; it was a physical pressure that made the very molecules of oxygen feel heavy and jagged.
Apollo stared at his hands, then at the armor Rex wore. The realization hit him like a physical blow.
The entropy reversal, the passive, radiating aura of his designation, hadn’t just been healing Kaelira. It had been working on the enemy.

"Your designation’s entropy reversal," Rex called out, his voice booming with a mocking, predatory clarity. "The cracks from Calivara’s working, the shattered plates from Kaelira’s cascade... they didn’t just stay broken."
"You’ve been repairing my armor for the last forty seconds without even trying."
Apollo blinked, the weight of the absurdity hitting him.
"You’re welcome," he grunted, the words sounding ridiculous even to his own ears.
"Truly," Rex replied, a smirk playing on his lips, "you are a generous man, Apollo."
"Such kindness in the middle of a slaughter."
The atmosphere shifted. The playfulness evaporated, replaced by a cold, lethal intent. Apollo’s eyes turned hard.
"I’m going to enjoy this part," he said, his voice dropping an octave, losing its warmth and gaining a jagged, deadly edge.
"I figured you might," Rex countered.
He settled into a stance, his body a coiled spring of pure violence. "Come on then."
"Let’s see what four minutes buys you."
Then, the world exploded.
Apollo and Kaelira didn’t just move; they launched. It wasn’t a dance; it was a collision of tectonic plates.
There was no choreography here, only the brutal, unpredictable chaos of two gods colliding with a monolith.
Kaelira was a blur of crimson fury. Fed by Apollo’s restoration, her body was a furnace of kinetic energy.
She hit Rex with a strike that sounded like a cannon shot. The impact caused a shockwave to pass through the ground, cracking the pavement for meters.

Rex’s Martial Arts Full Potential kicked in, his body twisting in midair to absorb the impact, his muscles rippling like steel cables under his skin. He caught her fist, the sound of their collision echoing like a hammer hitting an anvil.
CRACK.
The sound of bone-on-bone impact echoed. Kaelira’s fists were like iron mauls, and Rex’s defense was a fortress.
But the pressure was immense. Every time they clashed, the air itself seemed to splinter.
While Kaelira provided the physical onslaught, Apollo was the silent storm. He didn’t just strike; he manipulated the very space around Rex.

Telekinetic bursts slammed into Rex’s flanks, trying to break his balance, while gravity wells threatened to crush his limbs. Rex was fighting a two-front war, a dance of death against a perfectly synchronized machine.

Rex’s Earthen Authority was working overtime. Every time a strike from Kaelira or a burst from Apollo chipped away at his armor, the Earthen Authority surged, the stone plates knitting themselves back together in a hiss of dust and grit.
He was a living fortress, constantly rebuilding himself even as he was being hammered.
But the cost was high. Rex’s Foresight was screaming.

He was seeing the next ten seconds of the fight before they happened, a constant stream of incoming violence. He saw the angle of Kaelira’s next punch and the trajectory of Apollo’s next gravity burst.
He was managing the chaos, but he was not unscathed.
His breath was heavy, a rhythmic growl in his chest. His eyes were burning with the intensity of a man holding back a flood.
He was tallying the blows. He was assessing the angles. He was fighting to endure.
He knew the clock was ticking. Apollo and Kaelira were a force of nature, a combination of speed, power, and regeneration that should have broken him.
But as long as he could hold the line, and as long as his foresight could predict the unpredictable, he could endure.
He was waiting for the moment the ceiling was reached. He was waiting for the moment the limit was hit.
Because he knew, deep in his marrow, that even the most mighty gods eventually run out of breath.

The air wasn’t just heavy; it was thick with the metallic tang of blood, the ozone of discharged energy, and the suffocating smell of pulverized stone. The battle had ceased to be a fight and had become a war of attrition, a brutal, rhythmic grinding of two-way destruction.
For three minutes and forty seconds, the world was nothing but a cacophonous blur of violence. There was no time for grand speeches or tactical reevaluations.

There was only the crack of bone meeting reinforced stone, the hiss of steam from overheated skin, and the thunderous boom of kinetic impacts. Rex was a monolith, absorbing blows that would have turned a lesser man into red mush, his body absorbing the brutal force of Kaelira’s unrelenting strikes.
Kaelira, in turn, was a whirlwind of fury, her body a vessel of pure rage, her skin flushing a deep crimson as she pushed past the limit of human biology. But even gods have a ceiling.
At the three-minute and forty-second mark, Rex saw it. The subtle shift.
The way Apollo’s energy signature began to flicker like a dying star. The way Kaelira’s regeneration speed slowed by a fraction of a percent.
The "edge" was fraying.
"Twenty seconds," Rex grunted, his voice a low growl hidden behind the mask.
He was breathing hard, his muscles screaming under the strain, but his eyes remained sharp as glass. "Give or take."
"You feel that? The drain?"
Apollo didn’t answer. He couldn’t answer because he was too busy holding the world together.
Rex didn’t wait for a reply. He saw the opening and he saw the moment the flow stuttered.
He didn’t just strike; he commanded the world to change.
"Gravity: sixfold!" he roared.
He slammed a wave of crushing force into the space between them. It wasn’t a gentle push; it was a gravitational hammer.
The gravity field slammed into Apollo and Kaelira like a falling ocean. It didn’t stop them, but it staggered them.
It broke the rhythm. And it gave Rex the seconds he needed.
With a predatory roar, Rex drove his fist into the earth. "Earthen Authority: RISE!"
The ground didn’t just move; it exploded. A massive slab of bedrock, two meters thick and five meters high, erupted from the plaza floor like a rising tombstone.
It wasn’t a slow growth; it was a violent geological surge. The stone groaned and screamed as it tore through the crust, a wall of pure mass slamming into the space between the combatants.
Apollo threw everything he had at the wall. A burst of divine energy, a concentrated blast of life force, a shriek of entropy reversal.
The wall took it all. The stone, being inanimate, didn’t feel the exhaustion.
It just stood there, a monolith of unyielding mass. And while Apollo was busy fighting the wall, Rex was already gone.
He was a blur of motion, circling the flank like a shark. He emerged from the right side of the barrier, his eyes locked on the vulnerable gap in their defense.
He saw the opening and he saw the weak point.
CRACK THOOM!
He hit Apollo with the full weight of his martial mastery. It wasn’t just a punch; it was a collision of will. The impact sounded like a cannonade.
Apollo’s body was thrown back, his breath escaping in a spray of blood and spit. He hit the ground hard, his limbs splayed, his energy signature flickering like a dying lamp.
Kaelira, still struggling against the six times gravity field, could only watch in horror. Her eyes, wide and wild, searched for the man who had been her anchor.
"Apollo!" she screamed.
It wasn’t a battle cry. It was a human sound.
A sound of fear. And a sound of vulnerability.
Rex stood over the fallen apostle, his shadow looming like a dark god. He looked down at the man who had just tried to kill him, his expression impassive, his breath steadying.
"Stay down," Rex commanded, his voice a low rumble of authority. "You’ve used your all, and there’s not a chance you win this one."
Apollo looked up, his vision blurred, his chest heaving. He had nothing left to say, and he had lost the tempo.
Kaelira let out a sound, a raw, guttural wail that was neither human nor animal. It was the sound of a berserker who had lost her focus, the sound of a predator whose prey had escaped.
But the fight wasn’t over. Not yet.
As the dust settled, the ground began to tremble. Not from Rex’s authority. Not from Apollo’s gravity. But from the distance.
From the rest of the island.
The earth groaned. The sky seemed to shudder.
The fight in the plaza had been the loudest, the most violent, the most brutal. But as the vibrations traveled through the rock, it was clear: the real war was only just beginning.

chapters.title: Chapter 706. Fear Smells Like Copper and Sweat. The Only Thing in This World That’s Real
paragraphs: The ground wasn’t just shaking anymore; it was screaming. The tectonic plates of the island were groaning under the weight of the approaching chaos.
Rex stood over the broken Apollo, his eyes glowing with a predatory fury. He wasn’t satisfied with just winning a fight; he wanted to erase the very concept of his opposition.
"You think you’ve seen the limit?" Rex roared at the sky, his voice a thunderclap that drowned out the settling dust. "You haven’t even seen the beginning!"
He planted his feet, his muscles bulging like braided steel cables. He reached upward, not with his hands, but with his will.

The Earthen Authority didn’t just even out the ground; it reached into the heavens. The gravity wells he had been manipulating began to pull, to condense, to drag the very debris of the shattered sky downward.
"DIE!" he screamed, his voice cracking with a manic intensity.

From the clouds, a mountain of stone and compressed matter began to descend. It wasn’t a rock; it was a meteor. A massive, burning, jagged mass of geological violence coalesced from the dust and debris of the battle above.
It was a celestial hammer, a crushing weight of millions of tons aimed directly at the shattered remains of the plaza. It was meant to be the final nail, the ultimate execution.
But just as the meteor began its final, terminal descent, two streaks of light slashed through the smoke.
SHINK! SHINK!
Rex’s eyes widened. His Foresight flared red hot.
He sensed the sudden shift in the air pressure. He twisted his body, a violent, unnatural snap of his torso, throwing himself to the left just as the first strike arrived.
BOOM!
The meteor didn’t hit the ground. It hit the space where he had just been.
The impact sent a shockwave that nearly tore his eardrums.
He looked up, his teeth bared in a snarl. Eryndra and Calivara had arrived.

They didn’t just land; they slammed into the earth like divine sentinels, standing shoulder to shoulder in front of the fallen Apollo and Kaelira. They were a shield of flesh and will, their eyes burning with a defiant, unyielding fury.
Rex stood there, his chest heaving, his hair matted with sweat and blood. He looked at the two women, then at the shattered plaza, and then, he began to laugh.
It wasn’t a heroic laugh. It was the sound of a man who had lost his tether to humanity, and it was a jagged, hysterical, manic sound that echoed off the cracked walls.
"Are you fucking kidding me?!" Rex spat, his voice dripping with a venomous rage. "Every time! Every single time! You little bitches just won’t fucking stay down!"
He wiped a smear of blood from his lip, his eyes turning a dark, unhinged shade of malice.
"You think you’re heroes? You think you’re protecting them?" He pointed a trembling, bloodstained finger at the defenders. "You’re just more meat for the grinder!"
"You’re just more obstacles in my way!"
He took a step forward, his aura exploding in a burst of unstable gravity and dust. His face, once the mask of a stoic warrior, was now the visage of a madman.
"Fine!" he screamed, his voice a raw howl of pure insanity. "If you want to play the shields, then I’ll just have to break you first!"
"I’ll tear the life out of your throats and use your bones to pave the way!"
"You’re all just fucking in the way!
He crouched down, his body coiling like a viper ready to strike. The arrogance was gone, replaced by a primal, unadulterated lust.
"I’m going to fucking shred you!" he roared, his eyes wide and bloodshot. "I’m going to turn your guts into the dust of this plaza!"
Apollo struggled to prop himself up, his voice a broken, wheezing rasp. Blood bubbled and leaked from his lips, staining his chin in a dark, viscous smear.
"Run..." he choked out, his eyes pleading. "Get out of here... now! He’s... he’s going to kill you both!"
Eryndra didn’t budge. She plants her feet firmly in the cracked stone, her blade reflecting the dull, dying light of the ruined plaza.
"I don’t run," she said, her voice hard as iron.
Calivara stood beside her, her fingers trembling but her grip on her staff tightening, her face a mask of fierce devotion.
"We protect our own," she spat, glaring at Rex. "You’re not touching him."
Rex didn’t answer. He didn’t have time.
Eryndra exploded into motion. She didn’t just attack; she unleashed a barrage of astral summons.

From the void between dimensions, translucent, jagged spirits tore through reality, shrieking with a thousand discordant voices. They descended on Rex like a tide of ghostly razors, pouring out waves of astral magic that turned the air into a searing vacuum.
Rex didn’t even flinch. He raised his hand, his palm open.
"Boring," he spat.
He slammed his hand down, and the ground didn’t just shake; it screamed. The Earthen Authority surged, not as a wall but as a living, sentient parasite.

The stone beneath the astral summons didn’t just rise; it liquified, turning into a churning maw of molten slag and jagged teeth. The astral summons were caught in the sudden vortex, sucked down into the crushing pressure of the earth.
There was a sound of glass shattering as the spirits were annihilated, their essence absorbed by the hungry stone.
"My turn," Rex grinned, and it was a look of pure, unadulterated sadism.
"I’m going to show you what ’creative’ really means," he whispered, his voice low and poisonous.

He slammed his fist into the ground, sending a pulse of focused gravity into the bedrock. Suddenly, the ground beneath Eryndra erupted. Not in a spray of dust, but in a spear of jagged, black obsidian.
It shot upward with the speed of a bullet. Eryndra danced back, the stone narrowly missing her, but Rex was already moving.
He appeared in front of her, his hand snapping out in a blur. He grabbed her by the throat, his fingers digging into her windpipe.
With a guttural roar, he slammed her face first into the stone wall behind them. The sound of her skull meeting the rock was a sickening crack.
"How’s that for a shield?" Rex snarled.
He didn’t let go. He lifted her up, her legs kicking uselessly, and then slammed her back down again.
And again. Her nose shattered; blood sprayed across the ground in a grotesque splatter.
Calivara screamed, launching a desperate bolt of energy at Rex’s head. He caught the blast with his free hand, the energy boiling his skin, but he didn’t flinch.
He turned his gaze toward her, his eyes cold and empty.
"You want to save him?" Rex asked. "Watch this.
He dropped Eryndra, who fell in a heap, gasping and choking on her own blood. Rex slammed his foot down, and the ground beneath Calivara simply vanished.
She plummeted into a pit of jagged stone spikes. There was a sharp, wet sound, the sound of flesh being impaled.
Calivara shrieked as a jagged, obsidian shard tore through her calf, pinning her to the bottom of the pit.
"Look at her!" Rex roared, stepping toward the pit. "Look at your ’champion’!"
He reached down, grabbing Eryndra by the hair and dragging her toward the pit. "You think you’re noble?"
"You think this is a fucking fairy tale?" He threw her down beside Calivara, the two of them colliding in a tangle of broken limbs and torn clothing.
Rex stood at the edge of the pit, looking down at them with a twisted, manic grin. He raised his hand, and the ground began to close back in.
The jagged rocks began to squeeze together, crushing the space around the two women.
"I can feel your fear," Rex chuckled, his voice echoing with a dark, twisted delight. "It smells like copper and sweat."
"Oh~! I love the smell of fear~!"
"It’s the only thing in this world that’s actually real."
He closed his fist, and the pressure increased. The sound of bones snapping filled the air, a brutal symphony of destruction.
"How much of you is left before you stop being a person and start being a stain on the pavement?" He laughed, a wild, jagged sound. "Let’s find out together!"
Rex stood at the edge of the pit, his chest heaving, eyes wide with a manic brilliance. The air around him began to distort, his own gravity warping the very space he inhabited.
Then, he slammed his fists together.
CLANG.
The sound was not a human noise; it was the collision of two continents. From the swirling dust and sparks, his gauntlets materialized as massive, blackened Sunder Gauntlets of the Earthen Authority.

They weren’t just armor; they were instruments of extinction, forged from the core of a dead world, pulsing with a malevolent, rhythmic cadence. Rex flexed his fingers, the metal groaning under the sheer pressure of his strength.
"Time for a lesson in anatomy," Rex sneered.
He didn’t jump down; he descended like a falling star. He hit the bottom of the pit with a force that shattered the remaining stone, creating a crater of debris.
Before Eryndra could even scream, Rex’s right fist collided with her jaw.
The impact was sickening. There was no grace in the strike, only raw, unmitigated violence.
Her head snapped back, her jaw unhinging with a loud, wet pop. Teeth and fragments of bone sprayed across the dirt, and she was flung against the wall of the pit like a ragdoll.
"AAGGHHHH!!!"
"STOP IT!!!" Apollo screamed.

"You haven’t even seen the beginning!"
He planted his feet, his muscles bulging like braided steel cables.
He reached upward, not with his hands, but with his will.
The Earthen Authority didn’t just even out the ground; it reached into the heavens.
The gravity wells he had been manipulating began to pull, to condense, to drag the very debris of the shattered sky downward.
"DIE!" he screamed, his voice cracking with a manic intensity.
From the clouds, a mountain of stone and compressed matter began to descend.
It wasn’t a rock; it was a meteor.
A massive, burning, jagged mass of geological violence coalesced from the dust and debris of the battle above.
It was a celestial hammer, a crushing weight of millions of tons aimed directly at the shattered remains of the plaza.
It was meant to be the final nail, the ultimate execution.
But just as the meteor began its final, terminal descent, two streaks of light slashed through the smoke.
SHINK!
SHINK!
Rex’s eyes widened.
His Foresight flared red hot.
He sensed the sudden shift in the air pressure.
He twisted his body, a violent, unnatural snap of his torso, throwing himself to the left just as the first strike arrived.
BOOM!
The meteor didn’t hit the ground.
It hit the space where he had just been.
The impact sent a shockwave that nearly tore his eardrums.
He looked up, his teeth bared in a snarl.
Eryndra and Calivara had arrived.
They didn’t just land; they slammed into the earth like divine sentinels, standing shoulder to shoulder in front of the fallen Apollo and Kaelira.
They were a shield of flesh and will, their eyes burning with a defiant, unyielding fury.
Rex stood there, his chest heaving, his hair matted with sweat and blood.
He looked at the two women, then at the shattered plaza, and then, he began to laugh.
It wasn’t a heroic laugh.
It was the sound of a man who had lost his tether to humanity, and it was a jagged, hysterical, manic sound that echoed off the cracked walls.
"Are you fucking kidding me?!" Rex spat, his voice dripping with a venomous rage.
"Every time!
Every single time!
You little bitches just won’t fucking stay down!"
He wiped a smear of blood from his lip, his eyes turning a dark, unhinged shade of malice.
"You think you’re heroes?
You think you’re protecting them?" He pointed a trembling, bloodstained finger at the defenders.
"You’re just more meat for the grinder!"
"You’re just more obstacles in my way!"
He took a step forward, his aura exploding in a burst of unstable gravity and dust.
His face, once the mask of a stoic warrior, was now the visage of a madman.
"Fine!" he screamed, his voice a raw howl of pure insanity.
"If you want to play the shields, then I’ll just have to break you first!"
"I’ll tear the life out of your throats and use your bones to pave the way!"
"You’re all just fucking in the way!
He crouched down, his body coiling like a viper ready to strike.
The arrogance was gone, replaced by a primal, unadulterated lust.
"I’m going to fucking shred you!" he roared, his eyes wide and bloodshot.
"I’m going to turn your guts into the dust of this plaza!"
Apollo struggled to prop himself up, his voice a broken, wheezing rasp.
Blood bubbled and leaked from his lips, staining his chin in a dark, viscous smear.
"Run..." he choked out, his eyes pleading.
"Get out of here... now!
He’s... he’s going to kill you both!"
Eryndra didn’t budge.
She plants her feet firmly in the cracked stone, her blade reflecting the dull, dying light of the ruined plaza.
"I don’t run," she said, her voice hard as iron.
Calivara stood beside her, her fingers trembling but her grip on her staff tightening, her face a mask of fierce devotion.
"We protect our own," she spat, glaring at Rex.
"You’re not touching him."
Rex didn’t answer.
He didn’t have time.
Eryndra exploded into motion.
She didn’t just attack; she unleashed a barrage of astral summons.
From the void between dimensions, translucent, jagged spirits tore through reality, shrieking with a thousand discordant voices.
They descended on Rex like a tide of ghostly razors, pouring out waves of astral magic that turned the air into a searing vacuum.
Rex didn’t even flinch.
He raised his hand, his palm open.
"Boring," he spat.
He slammed his hand down, and the ground didn’t just shake; it screamed.
The Earthen Authority surged, not as a wall but as a living, sentient parasite.
The stone beneath the astral summons didn’t just rise; it liquified, turning into a churning maw of molten slag and jagged teeth.
The astral summons were caught in the sudden vortex, sucked down into the crushing pressure of the earth.
There was a sound of glass shattering as the spirits were annihilated, their essence absorbed by the hungry stone.
"My turn," Rex grinned, and it was a look of pure, unadulterated sadism.
"I’m going to show you what ’creative’ really means," he whispered, his voice low and poisonous.
He slammed his fist into the ground, sending a pulse of focused gravity into the bedrock.
Suddenly, the ground beneath Eryndra erupted.
Not in a spray of dust, but in a spear of jagged, black obsidian.
It shot upward with the speed of a bullet.
Eryndra danced back, the stone narrowly missing her, but Rex was already moving.
He appeared in front of her, his hand snapping out in a blur.
He grabbed her by the throat, his fingers digging into her windpipe.
With a guttural roar, he slammed her face first into the stone wall behind them.
The sound of her skull meeting the rock was a sickening crack.
"How’s that for a shield?" Rex snarled.
He didn’t let go.
He lifted her up, her legs kicking uselessly, and then slammed her back down again.
And again.
Her nose shattered; blood sprayed across the ground in a grotesque splatter.
Calivara screamed, launching a desperate bolt of energy at Rex’s head.
He caught the blast with his free hand, the energy boiling his skin, but he didn’t flinch.
He turned his gaze toward her, his eyes cold and empty.
"You want to save him?" Rex asked.
"Watch this.
He dropped Eryndra, who fell in a heap, gasping and choking on her own blood.
Rex slammed his foot down, and the ground beneath Calivara simply vanished.
She plummeted into a pit of jagged stone spikes.
There was a sharp, wet sound, the sound of flesh being impaled.
Calivara shrieked as a jagged, obsidian shard tore through her calf, pinning her to the bottom of the pit.
"Look at her!" Rex roared, stepping toward the pit.
"Look at your ’champion’!"
He reached down, grabbing Eryndra by the hair and dragging her toward the pit.
"You think you’re noble?"
"You think this is a fucking fairy tale?" He threw her down beside Calivara, the two of them colliding in a tangle of broken limbs and torn clothing.
Rex stood at the edge of the pit, looking down at them with a twisted, manic grin.
He raised his hand, and the ground began to close back in.
The jagged rocks began to squeeze together, crushing the space around the two women.
"I can feel your fear," Rex chuckled, his voice echoing with a dark, twisted delight.
"It smells like copper and sweat."
"Oh~!
I love the smell of fear~!"
"It’s the only thing in this world that’s actually real."
He closed his fist, and the pressure increased.
The sound of bones snapping filled the air, a brutal symphony of destruction.
"How much of you is left before you stop being a person and start being a stain on the pavement?" He laughed, a wild, jagged sound.
"Let’s find out together!"
Rex stood at the edge of the pit, his chest heaving, eyes wide with a manic brilliance.
The air around him began to distort, his own gravity warping the very space he inhabited.
Then, he slammed his fists together.
CLANG.
The sound was not a human noise; it was the collision of two continents.
From the swirling dust and sparks, his gauntlets materialized as massive, blackened Sunder Gauntlets of the Earthen Authority.
They weren’t just armor; they were instruments of extinction, forged from the core of a dead world, pulsing with a malevolent, rhythmic cadence.
Rex flexed his fingers, the metal groaning under the sheer pressure of his strength.
"Time for a lesson in anatomy," Rex sneered.
He didn’t jump down; he descended like a falling star.
He hit the bottom of the pit with a force that shattered the remaining stone, creating a crater of debris.
Before Eryndra could even scream, Rex’s right fist collided with her jaw.
The impact was sickening.
There was no grace in the strike, only raw, unmitigated violence.
Her head snapped back, her jaw unhinging with a loud, wet pop.
Teeth and fragments of bone sprayed across the dirt, and she was flung against the wall of the pit like a ragdoll.
"AAGGHHHH!!!"
"STOP IT!!!" Apollo screamed.

chapters.title: Chapter 707. He Called Me a Monster. And Then I Was Busy Proving Him Right
paragraphs: Rex didn’t give her a second to recover. As she slid down the rock, he pivoted and drove his left fist into her stomach.
The air escaped her lungs in a pathetic, wheezing, blood-flecked gasp. He didn’t stop there.
He gripped her by the hair, pulling her head back to expose her throat, and slammed his fist into her ribs.
CRACK CRACK CRACK.
The sound of ribs snapping was like dry kindling being broken over a knee. Eryndra’s body convulsed, coughing up a spray of crimson that painted Rex’s gauntlet.
He laughed, a guttural, jagged sound, and tossed her aside.
Calivara tried to crawl away, her fingers clawing at the stone, but Rex was faster. He stepped on her wrist, the sound of small bones grinding together accompanying her shrill scream of agony.
"Where are you going, little bird?" Rex asked, his voice dripping with a sadistic, charismatic, and utterly terrifying calm. "The show’s just getting started."
He reached down and seized her by the collar, hoisting her up. With a sudden, violent, blurred motion, he slammed her face-first into the ground.
The sound was dull and heavy. Calivara’s nose shattered, blood erupting and flooding her mouth and nostrils.
She tried to fight back, swinging a desperate, weak fist at his head, but Rex simply tilted his head, the blow glancing off his cheek.
"My turn," he whispered.

He launched her into the air, and before she could even register the motion, he drove a clenched fist into her midsection. The force was so immense that she flew backward, her spine hitting the jagged wall of the pit.
A sickening crunch echoed through the cavern, the sound of vertebrae fracturing under the impact. She slumped to the ground, her body twisting at an unnatural angle.
With every step, Rex moved closer to her, each one a guarantee of further agony. He grabbed her by the hair again, pulling her up so her face was inches from his.
He could smell the copper of her blood and see the vacant, shocked look in her eyes.
"You’re not a shield," he told her, his voice a low, dangerous purr. "You’re just a punching bag."
He delivered a devastating hook to her temple. Her head whipped to the side, and she collapsed, her forehead hitting a sharp rock with a wet thud.
Blood began to pool under her, staining the grey stone a deep, vivid red.
Rex looked over at Apollo and Kaelira, who were watching in horrified silence. He grinned, a wide, bloodstained smile that didn’t reach his eyes.
"You see? This is how it’s done. This is how you break the world."

He stepped over the broken, twitching bodies of the two women, his gauntlets humming with the anticipation of the next strike. He stood tall, his presence filling the pit, a god of ruin amidst the wreckage.
"Who’s next?"

The air in the pit was thick with the metallic tang of blood and the suffocating scent of pulverized stone. Eryndra and Calivra lay broken, their bodies a ruin of bruised flesh and shattered bone, yet they were still alive, a testament to their unyielding will to survive, or perhaps just a testament to Rex’s cruel deliberation.
"STOP IT!" Apollo’s voice tore through the cavern, a raw, unfiltered scream of pure agony.
He tried to lunge forward, but his legs were trembling, his energy-depleted body barely able to support his own weight. "LEAVE THEM ALONE! YOU MONSTER!
Kaelira’s voice joined his, a high, piercing wail of despair. "Please! Have mercy! They’re already broken!"
Rex turned his head, a mocking grin spreading across his face. He looked like a god of malice, his eyes glowing with a dark delight.
"Mercy?" he echoed, the word full of sarcasm. "Mercy is for the weak."
"And right now... you’re all looking very weak."
He didn’t just want to kill them. He wanted to make them feel every single second of their demise.
Rex raised his hands, his fingers splayed like a conductor of a symphony of pain. "Gravity... increase!"
He didn’t use the earthen authority this time. He used his telekinetic will.
A sudden, invisible weight slammed down upon the two women. It wasn’t a blunt force; it was a concentrated, crushing pressure that seemed to target their very skeletons.
The gravity around Eryndra and Calivra intensified a thousand fold.
The sound was immediate. A sickening, wet crunch.
Eryndra’s ribs, already fractured, began to cave inward under the unrelenting weight. The sound of her lungs being compressed was like a bellows being squeezed too hard.

She couldn’t even scream; the pressure was so intense that the air was forced out of her throat in a bloody, gurgling wheeze. Her eyes bulged, the capillaries in her sclera bursting until her eyes were nothing but pools of crimson red.
Besides her, Calivara was undergoing a similar hell. The gravity was pinning her to the stone floor with such force that her skin seemed to be stretching, her limbs splaying at unnatural angles.
A bone in her forearm snapped with a sharp, crystalline crack, the jagged end of the radius piercing through the muscle and skin, a splinter of white bone dripping with dark blood.
"Look at them!" Rex laughed, his voice a manic howl. "Look at how they break!"
He intensified the pressure even further. The gravity field became a vice.

Eryndra’s spine began to arch unnaturally, the vertebrae grinding against each other with a sound like stones rubbing together. A spray of blood erupted from her mouth as her internal organs began to fail under the crushing weight. She was being turned into a living mush of flesh and bone.
Calivra’s legs, already bruised, began to give way. The bone structure in her thighs groaned under the load, the femurs bowing slightly before the pressure became too much.
A muffled, wet thud echoed as a piece of her pelvis finally gave way, the sound of the break lost in her stifled, blood-soaked gasp.
"STOP IT! PLEASE!" Apollo screamed again, his voice cracking.
He tried to lunge forward, but his knees buckled, and he fell to a single knee, his breath coming in ragged sobs.
Rex ignored him. He was lost in the beauty of the destruction.

He watched with a predatory intensity as the two women were slowly crushed, their bodies becoming a mangled mess of red and white. He was not just a warrior; he was a sculptor, and his medium was human suffering.
"Do you hear that, Apollo?" Rex taunted, his voice dropping to a whisper that was more terrifying than his roar. "That’s the sound of your hope breaking~!"
"That’s the sound of the world dying~!"
He stepped closer to the pit, his shadow looming over the dying women like a dark god. He raised a hand, his fingers twitching as if he were ready to deliver the final, crushing blow.
The air was thick with the smell of blood, the scent of death, and the unrelenting weight of gravity.
Rex stood at the edge of the crater, his eyes wide with a manic, divinelike madness. He wasn’t satisfied with just crushing them; he wanted to dismantle them.
"Let’s see what’s inside," Rex whispered, his voice a jagged blade of sound.
With a sudden, violent flick of his wrists, Rex used his telekinetic gravity manipulation to actually pull the broken bodies apart. He didn’t just press down; he applied lateral tension.
He began to literally peel the layers of their bodies away.
A sickening, tearing sound, like heavy wet canvas being ripped in half, echoed through the chamber. Eryndra’s skin began to split under the unnatural tension.

As the gravity field pulled her upper torso one way and her lower half another, her muscles began to fray like old rope. With a wet, gory thwip, a string of vessels and tendons snapped, spraying a fan of crimson across the stone.
"LOOK!" Rex screamed, pointing at the carnage. "LOOK AT THE BEAUTY OF IT!"
He then turned his attention to Calivra. He used his gravity to compress her torso into a singular, dense mass, literally squeezing the life and the organs out of her body.

The pressure was so intense that her ribs didn’t just break; they exploded inward, turning into shards of bone that acted like knives, shredding her lungs and liver from the inside out. A thick, dark slurry of blood and bile erupted from her mouth as her internal structure collapsed into a mushy, red mess.

Apollo, watching from above, was no longer a god; he was a man drowning in horror. He saw the way Eryndra’s eye popped from its socket under the pressure, the way Calivra’s body became a hollowed-out shell of shattered flesh.
"STOP IT! STOP IT, YOU MONSTER!" Apollo let out a soul-shattering cry.
Tears of pure agony streamed down his face, mixing with the dust and blood on his cheeks. The sight of his comrades being turned into a slaughtered mess was too much.
The pain was a physical weight in his chest.
But then, something changed. The crying stopped.
The sobbing turned into a low, vibrating growl. The grief in his eyes was swallowed by a blinding, white-hot fury.
"YOU... BASTARD!" Apollo roared.
His aura, which had been flickering, suddenly ignited. It wasn’t a warm light; it was a searing, blinding radiance that seemed to burn the very air.
The light didn’t just shine; it pulsed with the rhythm of a dying star. The ground beneath him began to melt, turning into a pool of glowing magma from the sheer intensity of his divine outrage.
"YOU TOOK EVERYTHING!" Apollo screamed, his voice echoing like thunder. "YOU TOOK THEIR LIVES."
"YOU TOOK THEIR DIGNITY! NOW... I WILL TAKE YOUR VERY SOUL!"
