The golem loomed over him, its shadow casting Veran into a dark, suffocating abyss.
"But you’re not going to live to tell a fucking soul," Rex roared, the sheer volume of his voice causing Veran’s ears to bleed.
"Your ’wisdom’ ends here!"
"Your neutrality ends here!"
"You’ll die a secret, buried under the weight of a world that doesn’t give a single damn about your opinions!"
The golem raised a fist composed of a hundred fused shards, a jagged, uneven mass of killing stone.
"Die in the silence you love so much!"
Rex wasn’t in a hurry to end Veran.
Unlike Ren, whose death had been a frantic, explosive release of rage, Veran’s end needed to be a slow, methodical deconstruction of his very identity.
He needed to feel the weight of his "neutrality" crushing the breath out of him.
The golem didn’t strike him down.
Instead, it used its massive, fused limbs to pin him.
Two colossal, jagged arms slammed down on either side of Veran, not crushing him instantly, but trapping him in a vise of serrated stone.
CRUNCH!
SKREEE!
The stone edges bit into Veran’s ribs, the jagged protrusions of the fused debris digging into his flesh like a thousand tiny, unyielding knives.
Veran let out a strangled gasp, his body arching as the sharp edges of the rock began to slice through his tunic and into his skin.
"You like to watch, don’t you, Veran?" Rex’s voice vibrated through the very ground.
Veran was pressed against a low, vibrating hum that felt like it was massaging his internal organs with sandpaper.
"You like to stand on the sidelines and judge the players."
"Well, now you’re on the board.
And the board is hungry."
The golem’s hand, a grotesque, lumpy mass of fused granite and basalt, descended toward Veran’s legs.
It didn’t grab him.
It began to grind.
GRRRRRIND...
The stone fingers moved with agonizing slowness, pressing against Veran’s thighs.
The sound was sickening, the sound of muscle being squeezed between two tectonic plates.
Veran’s eyes rolled back in his head, a guttural, rhythmic groan escaping his lips.
"Nnnnggh...
Haaa...
Haaa..."
"Tremor... you... bastard..." Veran choked out, a thin trickle of blood leaking from the corner of his mouth.
"Bastard?
No.
A god is not a bastard," the golem rumbled.
"A god is a consequence."
Suddenly, the golem’s grip tightened with a sudden, violent jerk.
SNAP CRACKLE!
Veran’s scream was a jagged, high-pitched wail that tore through the air, a sound of pure, unmitigated agony.
The golem had caught his left leg and applied a twisting force.
The sound of the tibia splintering was like a heavy branch breaking in a storm, a sharp, wet CRACK that echoed in the silence of the field.
Veran’s leg was left at an impossible, sickening angle, the bone pushing against the skin in a grotesque, white protrusion.
"Look at that!" Rex laughed, the sound booming through the golem’s chest.
"That’s the ’middle ground’ you were looking for!"
"Right there, between the skin and the air!"
But Rex wasn’t done.
He wanted to see the "observer" lose his composure.
The golem reached down with a single, razor-sharp shard of stone that had been fused into its palm.
It didn’t stab; it began to scrape.
It dragged the sharp edge across Veran’s abdomen, a slow, shallow furrow that peeled back the skin in a long, red ribbon.
SHHHHHHH, LICK!
Veran’s body convulsed, his fingers clawing at the stone arms holding him, his nails snapping and bleeding as he tried to find any way to escape the sensation.
The pain was so intense it transcended mere sensation; it was a blinding, white light that consumed his entire consciousness.
"Please..." Veran whimpered, his voice breaking, the dignified observer replaced by a terrified, broken animal.
"Just... end it... please..."
"End it?" The golem’s voice dropped to a terrifying, intimate whisper that seemed to come from inside Veran’s own skull.
"We’re just getting to the part where you realize how much you actually care!"
"You’re not neutral, Veran!"
"You’re just a coward who’s afraid to feel the weight of the world.
So let’s see how much you can feel."
The golem began to press its massive, heavy chest against Veran’s broken torso.
It wasn’t a sudden crush but a slow, relentless descent.
CREEEEEEAK...
Veran could feel his lungs struggling to expand, the air being squeezed out of him in short, frantic puffs.
Every time he tried to inhale, the weight of the stone seemed to increase, forcing the air back out in a bloody, wheezing spray.
The sound of his ribs groaning under the pressure was a constant, rhythmic torture, a slow, structural failure of his very body.
SPLAT...
CRUNCH...
A rib finally gave way, the sound a sharp, wet pop that sent a fresh jolt of agony through his entire nervous system.
Veran’s vision began to dim, the world turning into a red, pulsing blur of pain and stone.
He was being unmade, his "wisdom" being ground into the dirt, one agonizing inch at a time.

chapters.title: Chapter 715. A Tyrant Wants To Be Obeyed, But A God Wants To Be Felt
paragraphs: While the screams of Veran provided a rhythmic backdrop of agony, Rex turned his predatory gaze toward the market square of Caldmere. There, the air was thick with the scent of pulverized limestone and the metallic tang of blood.

Brant Hollow was a different beast entirely. He wasn’t a philosopher or a silent observer; he was a fighter, a man of action who met the chaos with a ferocity that actually made Rex’s blood sing with anticipation.

Brant was currently a whirlwind of steel and grit, his blade whistling through the air as he carved a path through the debris, his eyes locked on the massive, monolithic golem that had turned the market into a slaughterhouse.
Brant lunged, his movement a blur of practiced lethal intent. He slid beneath a swinging stone limb, the wind of the blow ruffling his hair, and drove his blade upward with a guttural roar.
SHIIIIING!

The steel bit deep into the golem’s thigh, a massive chunk of granite shearing off in a spray of grey dust and magical essence. Brant didn’t stop; he spun, using the momentum to deliver a devastating kick to the golem’s "knee," the impact sending a vibration up his own leg that felt like hitting a mountain.
Rex, watching through the golem’s sensory input, felt a surge of genuine excitement. This wasn’t just a victim; this was a challenge.
He decided to stop merely commanding the golem and start inhabiting the fight. He wanted to feel the impact of Brant’s steel against his stone skin. He wanted to taste the struggle.
"Not bad, Brant Hollow!" Rex’s voice erupted from the golem, not as a rumble, but as a thunderous, mocking shout that shook the very stalls of the market. "You’ve got more spine than the last one!"
"You actually think you can chip away at a god?"
Brant didn’t answer with words. He answered with a flurry of strikes, a lunge, a parry, and a heavy overhead chop that sent sparks flying as steel met stone.
CLANG! CLANG! CRACK!
But Rex was done playing defensive. He wanted to feel the "vibe" of the kill.
"You fight like a man who thinks there’s a point to it!" Rex roared, the golem’s massive arm suddenly lashing out with a speed that defied its bulk.
It wasn’t a slow, crushing movement; it was a whip crack of geological fury. Brant tried to parry, but the sheer kinetic energy of the stone limb was overwhelming.
The blade caught the edge, but the force sent Brant spinning backward, his boots skidding through the bloody dust. Before he could find his footing, the golem was on him.
It didn’t just strike; it hunted.

The golem lunged, its massive weight causing the cobblestones to erupt in its wake. Brant rolled, narrowly avoiding a stomp that pulverized a nearby merchant’s table into splinters, but the golem was already swinging a jagged forearm spike.
WHIP CRACK!
The spike caught Brant in the side. It didn’t pierce him clean; it tore.

The jagged edge of the stone hooked into his ribs, the sound of bone snapping CRACK SCHLICK echoing through the square. Brant let out a choked, pained grunt, blood spraying from the wound as he was yanked toward the golem’s massive chest.
"Look at you, scrambling in the dirt!" Rex laughed, the sound a terrifying, booming vibration that seemed to come from the earth itself. "You fight so hard, so desperately!"
"For what, Brant? For a ’cause’? For ’people’? Look around you!"
"The people are screaming! The cause is dying! There is nothing left but the weight of my will!"
The golem grabbed Brant by the throat with a hand of crushing granite. Brant’s feet dangled off the ground, his hands clawing uselessly at the unyielding stone.
His face turned a frantic, bruised purple as the air was squeezed from his lungs.
"GURGLE... HAAA... HAAA..."
"You’re... just... a... tyrant..." Brant wheezed, a single, defiant tear of blood trailing down his cheek.
"A tyrant?" Rex’s voice dropped to a low, sadistic purr, the golem’s grip tightening just enough to make the vertebrae in Brant’s neck groan. "No, Brant."
"A tyrant wants to be obeyed, but a god wants to be felt..."
’And by the time I’m done with you, you’re going to feel every single ounce of the earth’s hatred!"
With a violent, mocking jerk, the golem slammed Brant face-first into a stone pillar.
THUD CRUNCH!

The impact was sickening, the sound of a nose shattering and teeth clattering against the ground. Brant slumped, a broken mess of blood and bruised pride, as the golem loomed over him, its shadow a dark, suffocating shroud.
Rex didn’t want a quick death for Brant. Brant was a warrior, and warriors deserved to be broken before they were shattered.
The golem didn’t crush Brant’s skull. Instead, it used its massive, jagged fingers to pin Brant’s arms wide against the stone pillar, stretching his chest taut.
"Let’s see how much of that ’warrior spirit’ is left when we start peeling it away," Rex hissed through the stone.
The golem’s hand, a lumpy mass of fused obsidian, descended toward Brant’s midsection. It didn’t strike; it pressed a single, razor-sharp shard of rock into Brant’s stomach and began to rotate it.
SKREEEEEEEEE...
The sound of skin tearing and muscle being shredded was sickeningly slow. Brant’s scream was a ragged, desperate thing, a sound of pure, unadulterated agony that tore through the market square.
"AAAAAAAGGGGHHHH! TREMOORRGGHH! YOU... FUCKING... MONSTER!"
"Monster? No, Brant. I’m the inevitable," Rex mocked.
He commanded the golem to pull the shard upward.
RRRRIIIIIP!

The stone tore a jagged furrow through Brant’s abdomen, exposing the glistening, pulsing reality of his insides. Blood cascaded down his body in thick, hot rivers, pooling in the cracks of the cobblestones.

Rex watched the light in Brant’s eyes flicker, the sheer pain forcing the man into a state of semi-conscious delirium. Then, with a sudden, violent burst of sadistic glee, Rex commanded the golem to bring both massive fists down on Brant’s head simultaneously.
KRA KOOOOOM!
The sound was catastrophic. Brant’s skull didn’t just break; it disintegrated.

A spray of grey matter, bone fragments, and crimson fluid erupted outward, painting the surrounding stalls in a grotesque, wet mural of death. The warrior was gone, reduced to a shapeless heap of gore.
But the carnage was only beginning.
As Rex stood atop his throne of carnage, his consciousness expanded, sweeping across the battlefield. He saw them, the Reincarnator and the Apostles.
They were throwing everything they had at his golems. Magic flared, divine light clashed with earthen fury, and the air hummed with the desperate energy of a dying world.
He watched as the golems began to fail. The Apostles were powerful, their strikes cracking the stone titans, their light searing through the magical essence that held the golems together.
One by one, the massive constructs began to crumble, falling in heaps of lifeless rock. The tide was turning.
The "heroes" were overwhelming his army.
But Rex didn’t feel fear. He felt a dark, intoxicating anticipation.
He pulled his consciousness back, withdrawing from the golems and surging into his true, physical form. The earth groaned and buckled as Tremor manifested.
He didn’t just appear; he erupted from the ground, a towering, muscular god of tectonic fury, his tan skin glistening with the sweat of battle and the blood of his enemies.

He stepped into the center of the fray, his presence so heavy it felt like the gravity itself had increased. He walked straight toward the epicenter of the struggle, where Apollo and Kaelira were struggling to stand.

They were a wreck. Kaelira, once a vision of divine grace, was barely recognizable. Her armor was shattered, her skin was a map of deep, bleeding lacerations, and one of her arms hung limp and useless at her side.
Apollo was breathing in ragged, wet gasps, his divine light flickering like a dying candle.
Rex stood before them, a massive, dark silhouette against the chaos. He looked down at their broken forms, at the blood pooling around their feet, and a sound began to rise from his chest.
It wasn’t a roar. It was a laugh.
A deep, booming, melodic, and utterly deranged laugh that echoed even across the entire Underlayer. It was the laugh of a man who had watched the world burn and found the flames beautiful.

"HAHAHAHAHAHA! LOOK AT YOU!" Rex bellowed, his voice vibrating in their very bones. He leaned down, his massive, muscular frame casting a shadow that seemed to swallow them whole. "The great Apollo! The Berserker Kaelira!"
Look at the ’saviors’ of this world! You’re nothing but broken toys!"
"You’re bleeding, you’re dying, and you’re utterly, fucking hopeless!"
He stood tall, his eyes burning with a manic, godlike light, his laughter drowning out the sounds of the dying world around him.
"HAHAHAHA! WELCOME TO MY WORLD! WELCOME TO THE AGE OF TREMOR!"

chapters.title: Chapter 716. Welcome Home, Lady Morwenna. The Feast Is Already Laid Out!
paragraphs: The air in the plaza didn’t just feel heavy; it felt wrong. It was thick with the copper tang of fresh slaughter and the suffocating, dusty scent of pulverized granite.
The telepathic field, once a harmonious hum of the Apostle network, was now a jagged, screaming cacophony of tactical desperation.
Valentina’s presence in the mental ether had shifted. There was no more debate, no more philosophical tug of war with Rex’s encroaching darkness.
She had abandoned the luxury of argument for the cold, unyielding necessity of survival. Her transmission register had sharpened into a razor-edged frequency of tactical coordination.

Through her spatial awareness, she was mapping the golem network not as mere constructs but as a spreading, geological cancer. She was screaming out vectors, directing the remaining Apostle assets to intercept the shifting masses of stone before those golems could complete their next massacre.
But the golems were no longer just machines of war; they were engines of genocide.

Rex felt the shift in the frequency, a subtle vibration in the very substrate of the island. He felt the Apostles scrambling, the desperate, frantic energy of a species realizing the predator isn’t just at the door; the predator is the floor beneath their feet.
Through the Foresight, Rex watched the carnage unfold in slow, beautiful detail. He saw the way the golems didn’t just kill; they erased.

He saw a group of defenders caught in a pincer movement of basalt claws, their screams cut short by the sickening "CRACK SPLAT" of ribcages collapsing and skulls being flattened into the dirt. He felt the sheer, unadulterated joy of the genocide as the earth drank the blood of the fallen, turning the soil into a red, viscous mire.
And then, he felt her.

The geological passive awareness of his connection to the very bones of the world traced a rhythmic, powerful vibration approaching the plaza’s edge. The Foresight sharpened, feeding him the data: four seconds.
Four seconds before her physical form breached the visual horizon, the Foresight had already calculated the specific, lethal intent behind her approach.
Morwenna.
She was the shadow that the Nightwing household whispered about in hushed, reverent tones. She wasn’t just a combatant; she was a catastrophe in human form.

Rex had spent months observing her, dissecting her patterns, and the conclusion was always the same: she was a predator of a different order. She didn’t possess a loud, booming system that announced her presence like a herald; her power was the terrifying expertise of the silent blade, the kind of strength that didn’t need to scream because it never missed.
As she stepped into the plaza, the ground seemed to steady itself in her presence, a momentary truce between the earth and its master.
Rex didn’t move. He stood amidst the wreckage of the recent slaughter, a smear of Apollo’s blood drying on his cheek, a dark, triumphant grin playing on his lips.
He looked at her, his eyes gleaming with the madness of a man who had just tasted divinity through destruction.
"Lady Morwenna," Rex said, his voice cutting through the settling dust with a terrifying, calm clarity. "Welcome home."
"I’d say you picked a bad time to come back, but honestly..." He let out a short, dark chuckle that sounded like stones grinding together. "...your timing’s perfect for me."
"The feast is already laid out."
Morwenna didn’t flinch at the sight of the gore, nor at the monstrous, shifting golems looming in the periphery. Her eyes were cold, ancient, and utterly unimpressed by the carnage.
"Save it," Morwenna said.

Her voice was a flat, controlled monotone, the sound of a storm held behind a dam. She had already assessed the landscape, the broken bodies, the shattered golems, and the sheer scale of the massacre Rex had orchestrated.

She had arrived past the point of pleasantries, already locked into a state of lethal readiness. "I’ve heard about you... it seems like I heard enough about the underlayer that has changed because of you... or maybe you are the one that’s in disguise right now."
Rex’s grin widened, revealing teeth that seemed too sharp for a man. "That’s incredibly flattering, Lady Morwenna. Truly."

"It wasn’t meant to be flattering," Morwenna countered, her gaze narrowing as she stepped over the mangled remains of a fallen defender, her boots treading through a pool of thickening blood without a moment’s hesitation. "It was meant as a warning."
"And looking at this... looking at you... I realize now that I should have listened to it much sooner."
The air between them didn’t just crackle; it screamed.
The initial strike from Morwenna was a violent, reality-bending insult to Rex’s senses. His foresight had predicted a linear trajectory, a lunge, a strike, and a specific sequence of kinetic energy.
But the moment she moved, the predicted event chain shattered like cheap glass. She wasn’t just moving; she was warping the very concept of distance.

A wave of spatial distortion slammed into the plaza, a medium-range ripple of distorted reality that made the twenty meters of blood-soaked cobblestone between them fluctuate wildly. One second, she felt miles away; the next, the air buckled, and the distance collapsed as if the world were being folded by a giant, invisible hand.
Rex felt the sickening lurch in his gut as the spatial axis shifted. He threw himself sideways, a desperate, instinctive lunge that barely cleared the zone of distortion.
The ripple hissed past him, shearing the top off a nearby stone pillar as if it were made of soft butter.
"Fucking hell..." Rex spat, his boots skidding through a mixture of grit and gore as he regained his footing.
He wiped a spray of someone else’s blood from his jaw, his eyes burning with a newfound, predatory respect. "It seems like you used a counter for my foresight."
"You’re not just predicting the future; you’re fucking breaking it."
"You’ve been holding that one back, haven’t you?" Rex shrugged. "Waiting for the right moment to pull the rug out from under me."
Morwenna stood perfectly still amidst the chaos, her breathing shallow and rhythmic, her presence an island of terrifying calm in a sea of carnage.
"Thirty years I’ve mastered all sorts of counter magic and technique," she said, her voice cutting through the heavy air like a cold blade. "I don’t waste tricks on people who don’t deserve them."
"You’ve earned this, Tremor."
"I’m honored. Truly," Rex grinned, though his heart was hammering a frantic rhythm against his ribs. "But... let’s see if that counter can actually keep up!"
She didn’t give him time to savor the moment. She was already moving, and the difference in their combat styles became immediately, brutally apparent.
Fighting Apollo and Kaelira had been like fighting a thunderstorm: loud, overwhelming, and chaotic. But Morwenna was a surgical strike.

Her combat was the product of decades of refinement, a terrifying accumulation of muscle memory and optimized magical flow. Every movement was stripped of redundancy; there was no wasted breath, no unnecessary flair, no "cool" poses.
It was the pure, distilled essence of lethality. She had spent thirty years making mistakes against monsters and surviving them, and that survival had forged a terrifyingly adaptive style.
Rex had the Foresight, the Earthen Authority, and the godlike anchoring of the geological substrate. He had the sheer, unadulterated power of a high-tier villain system.
But Morwenna had thirty years of experience.
A massive golem, a jagged hunk of fused obsidian, surged toward her with a deafening roar. Rex commanded it to crush her, to turn her into a red smear on the plaza.
Morwenna didn’t dodge. She didn’t even flinch.
With a subtle, almost imperceptible shift in her stance, she caught the golem’s momentum. She didn’t absorb the impact; she redirected it.
CRACK! SHHH!

It was thick with the copper tang of fresh slaughter and the suffocating, dusty scent of pulverized granite.
The telepathic field, once a harmonious hum of the Apostle network, was now a jagged, screaming cacophony of tactical desperation.
Valentina’s presence in the mental ether had shifted.
There was no more debate, no more philosophical tug of war with Rex’s encroaching darkness.
She had abandoned the luxury of argument for the cold, unyielding necessity of survival.
Her transmission register had sharpened into a razor-edged frequency of tactical coordination.
Through her spatial awareness, she was mapping the golem network not as mere constructs but as a spreading, geological cancer.
She was screaming out vectors, directing the remaining Apostle assets to intercept the shifting masses of stone before those golems could complete their next massacre.
But the golems were no longer just machines of war; they were engines of genocide.
Rex felt the shift in the frequency, a subtle vibration in the very substrate of the island.
He felt the Apostles scrambling, the desperate, frantic energy of a species realizing the predator isn’t just at the door; the predator is the floor beneath their feet.
Through the Foresight, Rex watched the carnage unfold in slow, beautiful detail.
He saw the way the golems didn’t just kill; they erased.
He saw a group of defenders caught in a pincer movement of basalt claws, their screams cut short by the sickening "CRACK SPLAT" of ribcages collapsing and skulls being flattened into the dirt.
He felt the sheer, unadulterated joy of the genocide as the earth drank the blood of the fallen, turning the soil into a red, viscous mire.
And then, he felt her.
The geological passive awareness of his connection to the very bones of the world traced a rhythmic, powerful vibration approaching the plaza’s edge.
The Foresight sharpened, feeding him the data: four seconds.
Four seconds before her physical form breached the visual horizon, the Foresight had already calculated the specific, lethal intent behind her approach.
Morwenna.
She was the shadow that the Nightwing household whispered about in hushed, reverent tones.
She wasn’t just a combatant; she was a catastrophe in human form.
Rex had spent months observing her, dissecting her patterns, and the conclusion was always the same: she was a predator of a different order.

She didn’t possess a loud, booming system that announced her presence like a herald; her power was the terrifying expertise of the silent blade, the kind of strength that didn’t need to scream because it never missed.
As she stepped into the plaza, the ground seemed to steady itself in her presence, a momentary truce between the earth and its master.
Rex didn’t move.
He stood amidst the wreckage of the recent slaughter, a smear of Apollo’s blood drying on his cheek, a dark, triumphant grin playing on his lips.
He looked at her, his eyes gleaming with the madness of a man who had just tasted divinity through destruction.
"Lady Morwenna," Rex said, his voice cutting through the settling dust with a terrifying, calm clarity.
"Welcome home."
"I’d say you picked a bad time to come back, but honestly..." He let out a short, dark chuckle that sounded like stones grinding together.
"...your timing’s perfect for me."
"The feast is already laid out."
Morwenna didn’t flinch at the sight of the gore, nor at the monstrous, shifting golems looming in the periphery.
Her eyes were cold, ancient, and utterly unimpressed by the carnage.
"Save it," Morwenna said.
Her voice was a flat, controlled monotone, the sound of a storm held behind a dam.
She had already assessed the landscape, the broken bodies, the shattered golems, and the sheer scale of the massacre Rex had orchestrated.
She had arrived past the point of pleasantries, already locked into a state of lethal readiness.
"I’ve heard about you... it seems like I heard enough about the underlayer that has changed because of you... or maybe you are the one that’s in disguise right now."
Rex’s grin widened, revealing teeth that seemed too sharp for a man.
"That’s incredibly flattering, Lady Morwenna.
Truly."

"It wasn’t meant to be flattering," Morwenna countered, her gaze narrowing as she stepped over the mangled remains of a fallen defender, her boots treading through a pool of thickening blood without a moment’s hesitation.
"It was meant as a warning."
"And looking at this... looking at you...
I realize now that I should have listened to it much sooner."
The air between them didn’t just crackle; it screamed.
The initial strike from Morwenna was a violent, reality-bending insult to Rex’s senses.
His foresight had predicted a linear trajectory, a lunge, a strike, and a specific sequence of kinetic energy.
But the moment she moved, the predicted event chain shattered like cheap glass.
She wasn’t just moving; she was warping the very concept of distance.
A wave of spatial distortion slammed into the plaza, a medium-range ripple of distorted reality that made the twenty meters of blood-soaked cobblestone between them fluctuate wildly.
One second, she felt miles away; the next, the air buckled, and the distance collapsed as if the world were being folded by a giant, invisible hand.
Rex felt the sickening lurch in his gut as the spatial axis shifted.

chapters.title: Chapter 717. Yes. Yes. Do It Again. I Meant That
paragraphs: There was a chilling, weary quality to her voice, the sound of a woman who had heard that exact same boast from a hundred different "gods" over three decades and had found every single one of them wanting.
The exchange was a nightmare of high-speed violence. For eight agonizing minutes, the plaza became a theater of the impossible.

Space bent and snapped; stone was pulverized into fine mist; blood sprayed in rhythmic, violent bursts as Morwenna’s precision strikes found the gaps in Rex’s defenses. It was a dance of gods and masters, a collision of absolute power and absolute experience, where a single millisecond of hesitation meant a shattered bone or a severed limb.
The air was thick with the sound of grinding rock, the hiss of displaced space, and the heavy, rhythmic breathing of two predators locked in a struggle for total dominance.

The eight minutes that followed were not a fight; they were a localized apocalypse. To any onlooker, the two combatants were nothing more than a blurred strobing of light, shadow, and flying debris. The sheer speed at which they moved meant that the human eye could only perceive the aftermath—the craters, the blood, the shattered stone—rather than the actual exchange.
BOOM! CRACK THOOM!
Rex initiated the onslaught by slamming his palms into the ground. The entire plaza didn’t just shake; it heaved.
A massive, jagged wave of granite, twenty feet high and sharp as a serrated blade, tore through the earth toward Morwenna.
"DIE!" Rex roared, his voice a guttural command to the very tectonic plates.
Morwenna didn’t retreat. She sprinted into the wave.
As the stone wall reached her, she performed a microadjustment of her spatial field. The air in front of her rippled like heat haze on a desert road.
SHHH LINK!

The massive wave of stone hit the distortion and didn’t crash; it slid. The kinetic energy was diverted upward, the massive wave curling over her head like a harmless ribbon of water, the wind of its passage nearly stripping the skin from her face.
Before the stone could settle, she was already on his guard.
WHIP CRACK!
Her movement was so sudden it sounded like a sonic boom. She appeared in Rex’s personal space, her palm striking his chest.
It wasn’t a heavy blow, but it was perfectly timed with a burst of her spatial energy. Rex felt his lungs compress as the air was literally sucked out of his chest cavity.
"GURK!" He coughed, a spray of crimson hitting the ground, but he was too fast to be caught off guard.
He used his earthen authority to instantly erupt a pillar of basalt directly beneath his own feet, launching himself backward to create distance.
THUD CRUNCH!
As he ascended, he sent a volley of stone shards, hundreds of them, each the size of a dagger, spiraling toward her like a swarm of furious hornets.
SKREEEEE!
The shards whistled through the air.
Morwenna danced through the storm. It was a terrifying display of economy; she didn’t dodge with wide, frantic leaps.
Instead, she performed tiny, precise tilts of her head and microscopic shifts of her hips. She moved through the gaps in the projectiles with the grace of a needle threading silk.
"Too slow, you bastard!" Rex yelled, his eyes glowing a deep, volcanic orange.
He clenched his fist, and the very air around Morwenna seemed to thicken. He was using his authority to increase the local gravity, trying to pin her down.
"GRRRRHNNN!" Morwenna grunted, her knees buckling for a fraction of a second as the weight of the world pressed down on her shoulders.
The cobblestones beneath her boots shattered under the sudden pressure.
CRACKLE!
But she didn’t stay pinned. She used the very pressure Rex was exerting against her.

She channeled the gravitational force into a singular, downward burst of her own energy, essentially "falling" faster than the gravity could hold her, turning the downward pressure into a horizontal launch.
"FUCK!" Rex hissed as she breached his line.
She was a blur of lethal intent. Her hand caught the edge of his jaw, her fingers digging into the muscle.
CRACK!

The sound of his mandible straining was sickening. She followed the strike with a knee to his solar plexus, a blow so precise it bypassed his muscular armor and sent a shockwave straight into his internal organs.
"OOF—HAA!" Rex staggered, his vision swimming with white spots.
He didn’t wait to recover. He reached out, his hand catching her ankle as she tried to pull away.
"GOTCHA!"
"SHATTER!" Rex commanded.
The ground beneath Morwenna didn’t just rise; it exploded upward in a series of violent, jagged spikes.
"ARRGH!" Morwenna let out a sharp, rare cry of pain as a stone spike grazed her thigh, tearing through her clothing and carving a deep, bloody furrow in her skin.
SPLAT!
A spray of her blood hit Rex’s face.
But even as she was lifted, she was attacking. She twisted in mid-air, her body coiling like a spring.
She brought her heel down on Rex’s forearm with the force of a falling hammer.
KRA KOOOOM!
Rex’s arm buckled, the bone groaning under the immense pressure.
"GODDAMN IT!" he snarled, the pain fueling his madness.
He released her ankle and slammed both hands onto the ground, creating a massive, localized earthquake that sent Morwenna spiraling into the air.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

He followed up by launching massive, fist-sized boulders from the earth, timed to intercept her while she was airborne. The fight moved from the ground to the sky in a chaotic, vertical ballet of violence.
CLANG! SMASH! WHACK!
Morwenna used the falling boulders as stepping stones, her feet hitting the moving stone with impossible precision. She was a predator navigating a shifting landscape of death.
She leaped from one boulder to the next, closing the distance to Rex, who was now conjuring a shield of dense, compressed, diamond-hard stone.
"BREAK!" she screamed, her palm hitting his shield.
The impact was a deafening KRA THOOM! that shook the entire plaza, shattering every remaining window in the surrounding buildings.
The two of them collided in midair, a whirlwind of limbs, magic, and raw, unbridled fury. For the remaining minutes, the plaza was a vortex of dust and blood.

They were moving so fast that the sound of their combat became a continuous, terrifying roar, a symphony of breaking bones, tearing flesh, and the thunderous percussion of the earth being torn asunder. It was a relentless, high-octane exchange where every millisecond was a gamble between a killing blow and a fatal mistake.
Rex was a force of nature, a tectonic god throwing the very foundations of the world at his opponent. But Morwenna... Morwenna was something far more terrifying. She was the master of the moment.

Despite the decades etched into the subtle lines around her eyes, the mark of a woman who had lived through eras of blood, she moved with a terrifying, predatory lightness that defied her age. She wasn’t just a combatant; she was a grandmaster of the fundamental laws of reality.
"TAKE THIS, YOU OLD BITCH!" Rex roared, his eyes burning like dying stars.
He slammed his fists together, and the air itself seemed to solidify.
CRUSH!
A massive, invisible hammer of pressurized gravity slammed down on Morwenna’s position. The ground beneath her didn’t just crack; it pulverized into a fine, grey powder.
KRA THOOOOM!
Rex grinned through the sweat and the stinging spray of blood on his face. He loved this.

The sheer, unadulterated intensity of it, the way his bones vibrated with every impact, the way the adrenaline made his blood feel like liquid fire. It wasn’t that he sought the pain, but he craved the friction of a fight that actually pushed him to the brink of annihilation.
But Morwenna didn’t collapse.
As the gravity hammer descended, she didn’t fight the weight; she threaded it. With a movement so fluid it looked like water flowing around a stone, she twisted her torso.
The gravitational force, meant to flatten her, instead caught the edges of her spatial field and was spun outward in a violent, centrifugal burst.
WHIRRRRR SNAP!

The pressure that should have crushed her ribs was instead redirected into the ground, creating a massive crater that spiraled away from her in a perfect circle. Before the dust could even settle, she was moving.
She didn’t run; she flickered.
FWOOSH!
She appeared behind Rex, her hand moving in a precise, whiplike motion. Her fingers, calloused by decades of mastery, struck the nerve cluster at the base of his neck.
THWACK!
"AGH!" Rex gasped, his entire left side momentarily going numb.
It wasn’t a heavy blow, but it was a perfect one. The precision was insulting, and it was the difference between being hit by a sledgehammer and being pierced by a needle.
"Is that all?" Rex hissed, spinning around with a feral grin, his arm already conjuring a jagged blade of obsidian. "You’re getting slow, Morwenna!"
"Slow?" Her voice was a calm, chilling whisper amidst the roar of the battle. "You’re just loud, boy."
She stepped into his guard, her movements a masterclass in efficiency. As Rex swung the obsidian blade in a wide, murderous arc, VREEEEEE! she didn’t retreat.
She stepped into the swing, her shoulder dipping just enough to let the blade whistle past her ear by a fraction of an inch.
CRUNCH!
Her elbow connected with his ribs. It wasn’t a brute-force strike; it was a concentrated burst of kinetic energy focused into a single point.
Rex felt the sickening sensation of a rib snapping, the sharp, white-hot flare of pain radiating through his chest.
"HAAAH!" He spat a mouthful of crimson, but the pain only made him laugh harder.
"YES! YES! DO IT AGAIN!" he bellowed, his madness rising.

chapters.title: Chapter 718. How Does It Feel to Be a Rock? I Asked Her That Question Honestly
paragraphs: He slammed his hands into the earth, sending a dozen massive, spiked pillars of granite erupting in a frantic, chaotic pattern around her. "DIE, YOU FUCKING WITCH!"
"SKREEEEEEEEE!" The stone pillars tore through the air, seeking to impale her.
Morwenna’s eyes narrowed. This was where her true terrifying power manifested.
She didn’t just dodge; she manipulated the flow. As the pillars closed in, she performed a series of rapid-fire hand gestures, her fingers dancing through the air like a conductor.
"REVERSE!" she commanded.
The space around the pillars began to warp and fold. The momentum of the massive stones was suddenly inverted.
Instead of traveling toward her, they were sucked into a localized spatial vortex, spinning around her in a dizzying, lethal orbit.
WHIRRRRR WHIRRRRR!
Rex watched, mesmerized and enraged, as the very weapons he sent to kill her became a swirling shield of destruction around her.
"You think you can control the world?" Morwenna said, her eyes glowing with a cold, ancient light as she stepped through the spinning vortex of stone. "The world is just a tool."
"And you, Tremor... you’re just a clumsy child playing with a hammer."
She launched herself through the vortex. She was a blur of white and silver, a comet of pure, disciplined intent.
She struck him with a flurry of blows—palm, elbow, heel, fingertip—each one timed to the millisecond, each one finding the exact moment his defenses flickered.
BAM! CRACK! THUD! SNAP!
Rex was being dismantled. Not by strength, but by geometry.

He was being hit in the gaps, in the seams, in the tiny, infinitesimal moments of vulnerability that only thirty years of perfection could exploit. His skin was a map of bruises and shallow cuts; his breathing was a ragged, desperate struggle.
But as he felt his ribs groan and his vision blur, a dark, triumphant joy surged through him. He was being pushed. He was being broken.
And in the breaking, he felt more alive than he ever had in his entire godlike existence.
"HAHAHA... HA!" Rex coughed, wiping a thick smear of blood from his mouth, his eyes locked onto hers with a terrifying, manic intensity. "Come on, Grandma... show me... show me what else you’ve got!"
Rex’s laughter died into a low, guttural growl. The playful edge was gone; the time for testing was over.
He wasn’t just fighting a master combatant anymore; he was dismantling a legend.
"Enough," Rex whispered, his voice vibrating with a sudden, crushing weight.
He snapped his fingers.
CRUSH!

The gravity in a twenty-foot radius around Morwenna didn’t just increase; it became absolute. The ground beneath her feet vanished, replaced by a localized singularity that dragged her violently downward.
KRAA THOOM!
She slammed into the ruined cobblestones, the impact sending a shockwave that cracked the foundation of the nearby buildings.
Before she could even gasp for air, Rex was on her. He didn’t fly; he fell with the weight of a thousand mountains.
SPLAT!
His heel descended like a falling star, driving her shoulder deep into the crater. Morwenna shrieked, a sound of genuine agony as her clavicle snapped with a sickening
POP CRACK!
But Rex wasn’t finished. He grabbed her by the throat, his massive fingers digging into her windpipe, and launched her upward with a burst of gravitational repulsion.
VREEEEEE!
As she soared, Rex slammed his fist into the air.
SKEWER!

From the ground, five obsidian spikes erupted with the speed of bullets. Morwenna twisted in midair, her reflexes still sharp, but the gravity field was fluctuating wildly, making her movements erratic.
One spike caught her in the thigh, tearing through the muscle and pinning her leg to the ground.
SHLUCK!
"AAAAAAGH!" she screamed, her voice rasping as she tried to pull herself free.
Rex landed beside her, his face a mask of cold, calculated fury. He didn’t give her a second to recover. He grabbed her arm and slammed it back against the ground.
KRRRRR SPLAT!
The sound of her radius and ulna shattering was a dull, wet thud.
"You’re a relic, Morwenna!" Rex roared, his voice booming over the sound of the dying plaza. "A fucking museum piece!"
"Let’s see how much of you is left when I’m done!"
He raised his hand, and the very ground beneath her began to churn. The broken stones and dust swirled into a vortex, a grinding maw of geological debris.
GRIND!

The stone shards didn’t just hit her; they acted like a thousand tiny saws, shredding her clothing and slicing into her skin. Morwenna gasped, trying to conjure a spatial shield, but Rex’s gravity field was a chaotic, fluctuating mess, disrupting her ability to focus.
SCRRREEEEEE!
He reached down and seized her by the hair, jerking her head up to face him. Her eyes were wide, filled with a mixture of shock and a lingering, stubborn defiance.
Rex grinned, a cruel, jagged expression.
"You’re tough," he admitted, his fingers tightening. "But I’m the god of this fucking rock."
He slammed her face first into a protruding slab of granite.
CRACK!
Blood sprayed from her nose and mouth, splashing across Rex’s chest. He didn’t let go.
Instead, he used his Earthen Authority to fuse the stone slab with her hair, welding her to the ground in a grotesque, living sculpture of pain.
"Let’s see how you handle a million tons of pressure," Rex whispered, his voice right in her ear. He placed his hand on her back and concentrated. "COMPRESS!"
The air around her solidified into a dense, crushing shell. Morwenna’s chest constricted, her ribs groaning under the mounting weight.
GURRRRRK!
She clawed at the ground, her fingers digging into the dirt as she tried to find leverage.
Rex leaned in, his expression a mix of fascination and sadism. "Do you feel it?"
"The earth is trying to eat you alive... and you’re becoming part of the landscape, Morwenna."
"How does it feel to be a fucking rock?"
He suddenly released the pressure and, in the same breath, launched a series of rapid-fire stone projectiles.
WHACK! SMACK! THUD!
Each one hit a different part of her body: her ribs, her stomach, her temple. She was tossed around like a ragdoll, her body bouncing off the debris of the plaza.
BOOM!
The final strike was a massive boulder that caught her midair, slamming her back into the crater. She lay there, broken and bleeding, her breathing a ragged, wet wheeze.
Rex walked toward her, his boots crunching on the rubble. He looked down at her, his eyes dark and empty of any mercy.
"You’re still breathing," he observed, his voice devoid of emotion. "Impressive."
"But look around you, Morwenna!"
"This is what’s left of your world!"
"This is what I’ve built from the ruins."
He stood over her, the shadow of his massive frame eclipsing her. "I’m not going to kill you yet~!"
"I want you to watch, and I want you to see everything you love turn into dust!"

The eight minutes of combat had ceased to be a mere exchange of blows; they had become a violent, tectonic collision that had rewritten the geography of the plaza. What was once a bustling center of commerce was now a cratered, hellish wasteland of pulverized granite and slick, dark crimson.
The air itself tasted of ozone, dust, and the metallic tang of spilled life.
Rex’s will had not only shattered the stalemate but also pulverized it under its relentless pressure.

Morwenna lay broken against the shattered cobblestones, her body pinned by a localized, suffocating field of Gravity Manipulation. The force was monstrous, six times the standard gravitational constant, pressing her into the earth with the weight of a collapsing mountain.
CRUNCH.

Every shallow, desperate gasp she took sounded like dry parchment tearing as her lungs fought the invisible hammer trying to flatten them. Her spatial distortion, that terrifying tool of predictive disruption that had once made her untouchable, was bled dry; the air around her shimmered weakly, a dying ember of the powerhouse it had been moments before.
She was experiencing the soul-crushing, visceral exhaustion of a mortal who had poured every drop of her essence into a sustained war against an opponent who hadn’t even begun to sweat.
Rex stood over her, a dark, looming silhouette that blotted out the sun. He wasn’t panting.

He wasn’t trembling. His skin, though splattered with her blood, looked as unbothered as if he had merely finished a light stroll through a manicured garden. He looked like a god who had just finished a casual afternoon of recreation.
Morwenna tilted her head back, her vision swimming. Her face was a mask of grit, bruises, and a thick trickle of blood running from the corner of her mouth, staining her chin.
Even through the haze of agony, her eyes held a razor-sharp, predatory intelligence.
"You..." she wheezed, the words forced out through the crushing weight of the gravity, sounding like grinding stones. "You’re not... the Undead Bringer."
Rex tilted his head, a dark, amused glint dancing in his eyes as he watched her struggle. "No..."
"Not quite."
"You’re something else entirely," she spat, a grimace of pure, unadulterated pain twisting her features.
"GURRRK!" She coughed, a spray of red hitting the stone near his boot. "Something... fucking unquantifiable."
"You weren’t in any of our goddamn assessments..."
"You’re a variable... a fucking anomaly we didn’t account for."
"Assessments are just guesses made by people too afraid to look at the truth," Rex replied.
His voice was smooth, terrifyingly calm, and lacked even a hint of the exertion required to keep her pinned to the dirt. "People love their little charts and their predictable little numbers."
"But the earth doesn’t care about your numbers."

chapters.title: Chapter 719. I Catalogue Everyone’s Technique. It Wasn’t Personal. At the Time.
paragraphs: "Eight minutes," Morwenna hissed, her fingers clawing weakly at the stone, her nails splintering as she tried to find purchase in a world that was trying to flatten her into a smear. "Eight fucking minutes of absolute, unmitigated hell... and you’re not even winded."
"I’ve fought Apostles, gods, and monsters... Most of them couldn’t last eight minutes in a real scrap with me without begging for mercy..."
"And here you are, standing there like we just had a casual fucking conversation over tea."
"We did just have a conversation," Rex said, his grin widening into something predatory, beautiful, and utterly terrifying. "And a damn good one at that."
"You’re the best fight I’ve had all morning, Morwenna. And trust me..." He leaned down slightly, his shadow swallowing her whole, "...I’ve had a few."
"That’s a fucking insult... where the hell am I standing?" she muttered, closing her eyes for a second to stave off the violent vertigo of the gravity field.
"No," Rex agreed, his voice dropping an octave, vibrating with a dark, heavy resonance that seemed to echo in her very bones. "I suppose it is."

The heavy, rhythmic thud of approaching footsteps tore through the suffocating silence of the ruined plaza. Rex didn’t even bother to turn his head; his geological awareness had registered the vibrations of their arrival long before they breached the crater’s edge.
The earth, his domain, had whispered their approach in a symphony of dread.

Aurelia emerged from the dust and debris of the south, her presence a crushing mass of pure, unbridled combat potential. Behind her, Iris trailed like a silent, lethal shadow, her eyes scanning the devastation with a cold, calculating intensity.
Rex turned slowly to face them, his mind instantly shifting into a high-level tactical assessment. He was already managing a three-front war, and now, he was adding a fourth.
’Oh...? Here she is... someone that I’ve been waiting for because she’s going to be the next girl I’ve fucked so fucking hard.’
’But now... I have to teach her some lesson.’

His foresight mapped them in a flash of precognitive data. And then he found Iris, where she was a scalpel, an assassin-class energy signature built for precision, speed, and the surgical removal of vital organs.
She was a knife aimed at the heart. Aurelia, however, was a warhammer.
Her energy profile was massive, a direct combat powerhouse designed for overwhelming force and absolute, unrelenting dominance.

Both women froze. Their eyes darted from the broken, bloody form of Morwenna pinned against the shattered cobblestones by a localized, crushing field of gravity to the unbothered, godlike figure of Rex.
"You... you actually put her down," Aurelia said.

Her voice wasn’t filled with disbelief; it was filled with a sudden, violent realization. It was the sound of a woman undergoing a mental recalculation so drastic it threatened to shatter her composure.
The world they knew had just changed.
"I did," Rex said, his tone casual, almost bored.
He glanced down at Morwenna, who was coughing up a thick, bubbling spray of crimson. "She lasted longer than the stories suggested."
"I’ll give her credit for that," Rex laughed. "She’s got a hell of a lot more spine than I expected.
Aurelia’s jaw tightened, her knuckles whitening as her hand drifted instinctively toward the weapon at her side. "Iris told me you were dangerous."
"She told me you were a goddamn menace judging by how you murder those innocent reincarnators and apostles!"
Rex locked onto her, his eyes piercing through her, stripping away the bravado. "And?"
"And I told her she was being dramatic," Aurelia admitted, her voice strained and brittle. "I told her you were just another high-tier anomaly to be managed, cataloged, and then put down."
Rex’s expression didn’t change, but the air around him began to hum. The ground beneath their feet groaned, a low, subterranean rumble that vibrated up through their boots and into their marrow.
The very molecules of the air seemed to thicken, turning heavy and oppressive.
"She wasn’t being dramatic," Rex said, his voice dropping to a cold, lethal whisper that cut through the wind. "She was being fucking polite."
SNAP!
A nearby shard of broken granite exploded into dust as the gravity field expanded slightly, a warning shot that sent a shockwave of pure force through the plaza.
"But I think it’s time we stop being polite," Rex continued, his eyes gleaming with a predatory light. "Come on then!"
"Let’s see if you two can do any better than she did."

Aurelia didn’t wait for a formal invitation to violence. She exploded forward, her aura erupting in a shockwave of pure, unadulterated kinetic force that sent a cloud of pulverized stone screaming outward.
She was a juggernaut, a force of nature that didn’t just move; she conquered the space she occupied.
She came in first, a direct, devastating lunge designed to shatter everything in her path.
Her strikes were precisely what her designation promised: sheer, overwhelming structural impact. Each punch carried the weight of a falling monolith, intended to pulverize bone and dent steel.

Rex met the onslaught with the terrifying efficiency of his martial arts mastery. He didn’t just block; he redirected, using the momentum of her own massive force to slide past her guard, his movements a fluid, lethal dance of redirection and counterpressure.

He was managing the high-intensity engagement with Aurelia in close quarters, all while maintaining the crushing, localized gravity field on the broken Morwenna, ensuring the old woman remained a pinned, bleeding spectator to her own demise.
BOOM! CRACK!
As Aurelia hammered at him, a blur of gold and fury, Iris moved. She was the silent shadow, the lethal variable.
She utilized the chaos of Aurelia’s heavy engagement as a veil, circling wide to find the blind spot, the exact angle required for a precision strike that would end the fight before it truly began.
Rex’s Foresight flared. He saw the trajectory before Iris even tightened her grip.

He saw the glint of the blade at the seven-second mark, the specific, murderous arc she intended to take. Without breaking his rhythmic, brutal exchange with Aurelia, Rex flicked a finger, a microburst of telekinetic gravity snapping toward the incoming steel.
WHIP SNAP!
The knife didn’t just stop; it was seized mid-flight by an invisible hand, its momentum violently inverted. The blade hissed through the air, returning to Iris’s hand at a sharp, unnatural angle.
She caught it with a sharp, metallic "CLACK," her eyes narrowing as she stabilized her stance.
"You weren’t even looking at me," Iris said, her voice a low, dangerous silk.
"I didn’t need to be," Rex replied, his voice steady despite the thunderous impact of Aurelia’s fist slamming against his forearm.
THUD!
He didn’t even flinch. "I’ve watched you fight before!"
"You throw with your wrist angled slightly inward on the release, a tiny, microscopic habit."
"Most people wouldn’t catch it, but it leaves a signature in the air." He glanced at her, a dark, knowing smirk playing on his lips. "I caught it the first time I saw you spar with Theo, actually."
"Never told anyone. Seemed rude to spoil the surprise."
"I fucking knew it... Underlayer people are assholes for eavesdropping and even eyeing us like that!"
A heavy silence descended for a heartbeat, punctuated only by the ragged, wet breathing of the pinned Morwenna.
"You’ve been cataloguing my technique since then," Iris said.
It wasn’t a question; it was a cold realization that settled in her gut like lead. Her voice had gone deathly still, the predatory calm of a hunter who realized she was being hunted.
"I catalogue everyone’s technique," Rex said, his eyes snapping back to Aurelia as she lunged again, her fist whistling through the air like a cannonball.
WHOOSH!
"It’s not personal. Well... it wasn’t, at the time."
The battle reignited with a ferocity that turned the air into a war zone. Rex was now operating at the razor’s edge of his capacity.

He was solving a complex, high-speed mathematical equation of violence: maintaining the crushing gravity hold on Morwenna to keep her out of the fray, parrying Aurelia’s direct, bone-shattering assaults, and simultaneously tracking Iris’s lethal, shifting positioning.
CRUNCH! SMASH! SHLUCK!

Blood sprayed from a shallow cut on Rex’s cheek as Iris’s blade grazed him, and the ground groaned under the weight of Aurelia’s relentless pressure. He was managing a three-front war of attrition, a masterpiece of resource distribution where a single millisecond of distraction would mean a blade in his throat or a fist through his chest.
He was dancing on the edge of a precipice, and the view was magnificent.

A nearby shard of broken granite exploded into dust as the gravity field expanded slightly, a warning shot that sent a shockwave of pure force through the plaza.
"But I think it’s time we stop being polite," Rex continued, his eyes gleaming with a predatory light.
"Come on then!"
"Let’s see if you two can do any better than she did."
Aurelia didn’t wait for a formal invitation to violence.
She exploded forward, her aura erupting in a shockwave of pure, unadulterated kinetic force that sent a cloud of pulverized stone screaming outward.
She was a juggernaut, a force of nature that didn’t just move; she conquered the space she occupied.
She came in first, a direct, devastating lunge designed to shatter everything in her path.
Her strikes were precisely what her designation promised: sheer, overwhelming structural impact.
Each punch carried the weight of a falling monolith, intended to pulverize bone and dent steel.
Rex met the onslaught with the terrifying efficiency of his martial arts mastery.
He didn’t just block; he redirected, using the momentum of her own massive force to slide past her guard, his movements a fluid, lethal dance of redirection and counterpressure.

He was managing the high-intensity engagement with Aurelia in close quarters, all while maintaining the crushing, localized gravity field on the broken Morwenna, ensuring the old woman remained a pinned, bleeding spectator to her own demise.
BOOM!
CRACK!
As Aurelia hammered at him, a blur of gold and fury, Iris moved.
She was the silent shadow, the lethal variable.
She utilized the chaos of Aurelia’s heavy engagement as a veil, circling wide to find the blind spot, the exact angle required for a precision strike that would end the fight before it truly began.
Rex’s Foresight flared.
He saw the trajectory before Iris even tightened her grip.
He saw the glint of the blade at the seven-second mark, the specific, murderous arc she intended to take.
Without breaking his rhythmic, brutal exchange with Aurelia, Rex flicked a finger, a microburst of telekinetic gravity snapping toward the incoming steel.
WHIP SNAP!
The knife didn’t just stop; it was seized mid-flight by an invisible hand, its momentum violently inverted.
The blade hissed through the air, returning to Iris’s hand at a sharp, unnatural angle.
She caught it with a sharp, metallic "CLACK," her eyes narrowing as she stabilized her stance.
"You weren’t even looking at me," Iris said, her voice a low, dangerous silk.
"I didn’t need to be," Rex replied, his voice steady despite the thunderous impact of Aurelia’s fist slamming against his forearm.
THUD!
He didn’t even flinch.
"I’ve watched you fight before!"
"You throw with your wrist angled slightly inward on the release, a tiny, microscopic habit."
"Most people wouldn’t catch it, but it leaves a signature in the air." He glanced at her, a dark, knowing smirk playing on his lips.
"I caught it the first time I saw you spar with Theo, actually."
"Never told anyone.
Seemed rude to spoil the surprise."
"I fucking knew it...
Underlayer people are assholes for eavesdropping and even eyeing us like that!"
A heavy silence descended for a heartbeat, punctuated only by the ragged, wet breathing of the pinned Morwenna.
"You’ve been cataloguing my technique since then," Iris said.
It wasn’t a question; it was a cold realization that settled in her gut like lead.
Her voice had gone deathly still, the predatory calm of a hunter who realized she was being hunted.
"I catalogue everyone’s technique," Rex said, his eyes snapping back to Aurelia as she lunged again, her fist whistling through the air like a cannonball.
WHOOSH!
"It’s not personal.
Well... it wasn’t, at the time."
The battle reignited with a ferocity that turned the air into a war zone.
Rex was now operating at the razor’s edge of his capacity.

He was solving a complex, high-speed mathematical equation of violence: maintaining the crushing gravity hold on Morwenna to keep her out of the fray, parrying Aurelia’s direct, bone-shattering assaults, and simultaneously tracking Iris’s lethal, shifting positioning.
CRUNCH!
SMASH!
SHLUCK!
Blood sprayed from a shallow cut on Rex’s cheek as Iris’s blade grazed him, and the ground groaned under the weight of Aurelia’s relentless pressure.
He was managing a three-front war of attrition, a masterpiece of resource distribution where a single millisecond of distraction would mean a blade in his throat or a fist through his chest.
He was dancing on the edge of a precipice, and the view was magnificent.

chapters.title: Chapter 720. Pain Is a Teacher. This Was the Best Lesson I’ve Had All Day.
paragraphs: The air in the plaza grew thick with the scent of ozone and the heavy, metallic aroma of blood. The rhythm of the fight shifted. It was no longer three separate engagements; it was a synchronized symphony of destruction.
The sisters were no longer fighting as individuals; they were a single, multiheaded hydra of lethal intent.
"HRAAAAH!" Aurelia let out a primal roar, her aura flaring into a blinding, golden corona.
She didn’t just lunge; she surged. She transitioned from a direct assault into a devastating flurry of high-tier brawling.
Her fists became a blur of kinetic energy, each strike accompanied by the sound of a sonic boom.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
She unleashed a heavy combination: a gut-wrenching liver blow followed by a sweeping roundhouse kick that carried enough force to shatter a granite pillar.
Rex felt the impact of the liver shot.
"OOF!" The air was driven from his lungs, and for a split second, his vision clouded with white heat.

A grin, sharp and jagged, split his face. He wasn’t a masochist, but he was a man who lived for the friction of life, and this was the ultimate friction. The pain was a teacher, a sharp, electric reminder that he was truly alive.
He ducked under Aurelia’s sweeping kick, the wind of her movement whistling past his ear with a terrifying WHOOSH!, but he didn’t move away. He moved into the opening.
That was the trap.
As Rex stepped into Aurelia’s guard to deliver a counterstrike, Iris materialized from the periphery like a ghost woven from shadows. She didn’t just strike; she flowed.
Using the momentum of Aurelia’s heavy lunge as a smokescreen, Iris launched herself upward, her body a coiled spring of lethal grace.
SHING!
Iris’s daggers were no longer just tools; they were extensions of her very soul. She moved with a terrifying, silent speed that contrasted Aurelia’s thunderous violence.
She aimed for the carotid artery, her movement a surgical line of intent.
Rex’s Foresight screamed. The world slowed.
He saw the golden arc of Aurelia’s fist coming for his jaw and the silver flash of Iris’s blade aiming for his throat.
"GRRR..." Rex gritted his teeth, a low sound of intense focus.
He couldn’t dodge both. He chose to absorb.
He pivoted his torso at the last microsecond, a feat of impossible core strength. Aurelia’s massive fist caught him squarely in the ribs.
CRACK! THUD!

The sound of his ribs groaning under the pressure was sickening, a dull, wet snap that sent a jolt of white-hot agony through his nervous system. He felt the bruise forming instantly, the internal pressure mounting.
But the pivot worked. It tilted his head just enough.
Iris’s blade hissed past his ear, so close he could feel the cold steel’s temperature.
SST!
The tip of the dagger grazed his cheek, carving a thin, red line that wept blood down his jaw.
"Too slow!" Rex barked, a laugh bubbling up through the pain.
He didn’t wait for them to reset. He slammed his palm into the ground.
"EARTHTHROB!"
The ground beneath the sisters didn’t just shake; it buckled and surged upward in a violent, jagged wave of stone.
KRRR SHOOOM!
The sudden upheaval forced them to break their synchronization; the sudden loss of footing disrupted the perfect flow of their sisterly coordination.
Aurelia stumbled, her heavy footing betrayed by the shifting earth, and Iris was forced to leap backward to maintain her balance.

Rex stood in the center of the chaos, his chest heaving slightly, blood dripping from his chin and his side. His ribs were screaming, and his cheek was stinging, but his eyes were burning with a terrifying, ecstatic light.
He wasn’t just fighting them; he was savoring the struggle.
"That’s it!" Rex shouted, his voice echoing against the ruined walls of the plaza. "Don’t hold back!"
"Give me everything you’ve got! Show me the strength of the blood you share!"
He raised his hands, and the very gravity in the crater began to pulse like a dying heart.
THUMP... THUMP...
The pressure increased, making the blood in their veins feel heavy, pulling them back toward the center of his killing field. The real slaughter was only just beginning.

The plaza had transcended the realm of a battlefield; it was now a churning cauldron of elemental fury and human grit. The air was so thick with dust and the metallic scent of blood that it felt like breathing liquid iron.
Aurelia was the first to recover from the earth’s upheaval. She didn’t just regain her footing; she reclaimed it with a roar of defiance.
"HRAAAAAH!" She surged forward, her golden aura intensifying until it looked like molten sunlight.
She wasn’t just a brawler anymore; she was a storm of kinetic devastation.
She unleashed a "Meteor Hammer" sequence, a brutal, continuous chain of heavy impact strikes.
BOOM! CRACK! WHAM!
Her fists moved in a rhythmic, pulverizing cadence. She drove a heavy left hook toward Rex’s temple, followed instantly by a crushing straight right to his solar plexus.
Rex parried the hook with a forearm block. CLANG! The sound of bone meeting concentrated energy, but the sheer momentum of the second strike caught him in the gut.
"OOF!" He was lifted inches off the ground, the air whistling out of his lungs in a ragged burst.
But Rex was a predator who thrived in the teeth of the storm. As he was pushed back, he didn’t retreat; he spun.
He used the force of the gut shot to fuel a centrifugal rotation, his heavy boot sweeping out in a wide, punishing arc.
WHOOSH THUD!
The kick caught Aurelia in the midsection, a heavy, blunt impact that forced her to skid backward across the grit.
"NOW, IRIS!" Aurelia bellowed, her voice a command that bridged the gap between sisters.
Iris didn’t need the prompt. She was already there.
She moved through the dust like a needle through silk, her silhouette blurring as she utilized a "shadow step" technique. She wasn’t running; she was flickering in and out of existence.
FIP! FIP! FIP!
Rex’s foresight was working overtime, his mind a frantic, high-speed processor. He saw the golden trail of Aurelia’s recovery and the silver shimmer of Iris’s approach.
He was being squeezed between a hammer and an anvil.
Iris launched a "Thousand Sting" flurry. Her daggers became a shimmering web of steel.
SHLICK! SHLICK! SHLICK!

The blades whistled past Rex’s throat, his ribs, and his thighs. He was forced into a desperate, high-speed defensive dance, his hands moving in a blur of martial arts mastery to deflect the razor-sharp edges.
TING! TING! CLACK!
Each deflection sent a vibration of stinging pain up his arms, a frantic staccato of near misses.
"You’re dancing on a razor’s edge, Tremor!" Iris hissed, her voice appearing from everywhere and nowhere at once.
"Then let’s see if you can cut me!" Rex countered.
He slammed his hands together. "GRAVITY WELL!"
A sudden, violent spike in gravitational pressure erupted in a sphere around him.
VREEEEE!
The sudden increase in weight acted like a physical barrier, momentarily slowing Iris’s lightning-quick lunge and forcing Aurelia to brace her entire body to keep from being crushed into the dirt.
Taking advantage of that microsecond of hesitation, Rex went on the offensive. He lunged at Aurelia, his fist shrouded in a dense, earthen coating that made it as hard as diamond.
KRA THOOM!
The punch connected with her shoulder, a sickening "CRUNCH" echoing through the plaza as the impact shook her entire frame.
Aurelia grunted, her teeth bared in a snarl of pain, but she didn’t back down. She caught his arm, her fingers digging into his muscle like iron clamps.
"GOT YOU!"
She pulled him inward, intending to deliver a devastating headbutt, but Rex was ready. He tilted his head, letting her forehead slam into his cheekbone with a wet
THWACK!
The pain was exquisite, a blinding flash of white that made his ears ring, but it allowed him to get close enough to her face.
SPLAT!
He drove a short, brutal elbow into her nose, breaking it instantly. Blood sprayed across both their faces, a crimson mist in the moonlight.
As Aurelia recoiled, clutching her face, Iris struck from above. She had used the distraction to leap off a rising pillar of stone.
SREEEEEE!
She descended like a falling star, her daggers held in a reverse grip, aimed straight for the gap in Rex’s guard.
Rex didn’t look up. He felt the shift in the air, and he felt the weight of her descent.
CRUNCH!
He slammed his heel into the ground, causing a jagged spike of obsidian to erupt directly beneath Iris’s landing zone. It didn’t hit her, but it forced her to twist in midair to avoid being impaled.
The sudden, unnatural rotation threw her off her lethal trajectory.

Rex turned, his eyes wild and glowing with a terrifying, primal energy. He was covered in blood, his own and theirs; his clothes were torn; his ribs ached with every breath; his skin was bruised and battered.
But he wasn’t defeated. He looked like a man who had finally found a worthy way to die, or a god who had finally discovered a reason to kill.

"Is that all?" Rex roared, his voice a guttural, earth-shaking sound that seemed to come from the very core of the planet. "THE SISTERS OF THE BLADE AND THE HAMMER? SHOW ME THE REAL YOU! SHOW ME THE BLOOD THAT MAKES YOU LEGENDS!"
He raised both hands, and the ground began to liquefy, turning into a swirling vortex of sand and stone. The very atmosphere began to groan under the weight of his escalating power.
The true climax was approaching, and the plaza was ready to swallow them all.

chapters.title: Chapter 721. She Thought I Was Slumped In Defeat (I Was Coiling)
paragraphs: The vortex of sand and stone roared like a starving beast, a swirling maelstrom of debris that obscured the very sun. In the heart of the chaos, a sickening THUD CRACK! echoed through the plaza.
Iris, caught mid-rotation by the jagged obsidian spike, had been thrown violently sideways. Her body collided with a crumbling granite pillar with the force of a falling meteor.
CRUNCH!
The sound of her ribs buckling against the stone was unmistakable. She slumped to the ground, a limp, bloodied silhouette in the dust, her consciousness flickering out like a candle in a gale.
The battlefield shifted instantly. The symphony of two was now a brutal, lonely duet.
Aurelia’s eyes widened, a flash of raw, uncharacteristic panic crossing her face as she saw her sister fall.
"IRIS!" she screamed, a sound of pure, unadulterated fury.
The panic didn’t break her; it forged her. Her golden aura didn’t just flare; it ignited, turning from a warm glow into a searing, violent, white-hot corona that hissed against the air.
FSSSSSS!
She was no longer fighting to manage a threat. She was fighting to avenge a soul.
"You... you fucking monster!" Aurelia bellowed, her voice cracking with rage.
She launched herself at Rex, not with a lunge but with a full-body kinetic explosion.
BOOM!
She was a juggernaut of pure, unmitigated wrath. She unleashed a "World Breaker" sequence, a series of strikes so heavy they seemed to warp the air around her fists.
WHAM! CRACK! THOOM!
Each blow was a hammer strike of divine proportions. She drove a massive, glowing fist into Rex’s chest, the impact sounding like a cannon firing at point blank range.
KABOOM!
Rex felt his sternum groan, the sensation of his bones vibrating to the point of shattering. He was thrown backward, his heels carving deep trenches into the pulverized earth.
SKREEEEE!
He skidded for twenty feet, a trail of dust and blood marking his path, before slamming into the crater’s edge.
He spat a mouthful of thick, dark blood, his eyes gleaming with a terrifying, manic joy.
"Yes!" he roared, the word a jagged edge of ecstasy. "That’s the fury! That’s the blood!"
Aurelia didn’t give him a second to breathe. She was on him in an instant, her movements a terrifying blur of heavy-weight martial arts.
She transitioned into a "mountain-crushing" clinch, wrapping her powerful arms around Rex’s waist and driving her knee upward with the force of a tectonic shift.
CRUNCH!
The knee caught Rex in the solar plexus. The sound was sickening, a wet, heavy thud that signaled the compression of internal organs.
Rex’s eyes bulged, his breath hitching in a silent, agonizing scream.
But as she pulled back to deliver a finishing blow, Rex acted. He didn’t fight her strength; he used her momentum.
As her fist swung toward his face in a wide, devastating arc, he dropped his center of gravity, sliding beneath her massive arm like a serpent.
SST!
He drove his shoulder into her midsection, a "core breaker" strike designed to disrupt her massive energy flow.
THUD!
The collision sent them both reeling. Aurelia gasped, the wind stolen from her lungs, and Rex felt the searing heat of her aura burning his skin.
"You think... you can take her... and still stand?" Aurelia hissed, her face a mask of sweat, blood, and divine rage.
She wiped a smear of crimson from her lip, her eyes burning with a white-hot intensity.
"I don’t think," Rex replied, his voice a low, vibrating growl as he forced himself upright, his muscles trembling with the effort to keep his shattered ribs in place. "I know."

Aurelia lunged again, but this time, she wasn’t just using her fists. She began to channel her kinetic energy into her entire body, her movements becoming a terrifying blend of brawler and wrecking ball.
She unleashed a "Cataclysmic Flurry," a relentless, high-speed barrage of strikes that seemed to come from every direction at once.
BAM! BAM! BAM! BAM!

Rex was forced into a desperate, frantic defense. He parried a left hook CLANG!, ducked a heavy body blow WHOOSH!, and caught a rising knee with his forearm CRACK!, the impact sending a jolt of white-hot agony up his spine.
He was being hammered and pulverized, his body becoming a canvas of bruises and lacerations.
SHLICK!
Aurelia’s elbow caught him across the temple, opening a deep gash that sent a curtain of red over his left eye.
CRUNCH!
A heavy kick to his thigh sent a sickening tremor through his leg, and the muscle bruised instantly.

Rex was bleeding, he was broken, and he was being systematically dismantled by a woman possessed by the spirit of a goddess. And yet, as he stood there, swaying on his feet, a wide, bloody, and utterly terrifying grin spread across his face.
"More!" he screamed, the sound tearing from his throat like a landslide. "Give me more!"
"Break me! Tear me apart! Let’s see who’s left standing when the dust settles!"
He slammed his fists into the earth, and the ground didn’t just shake; it screamed.
KRRRRR AAAAA!

Massive pillars of stone erupted around them, creating a jagged, claustrophobic arena of debris. The gravity in the center of the crater intensified, pulling everything—the dust, the blood, the very air—into a crushing, violent vortex.

Aurelia charged into the heart of the storm, her golden light clashing with the dark, earthen power of Rex. They collided in the center of the crater with a sound that could have been heard for miles, a thunderous, world-shaking BOOOOOOOM! that signaled the beginning of the final, most brutal phase of their war.
The world became a blur of gold and grit. The air was no longer gas; it was a pressurized medium of violence, vibrating with the sheer frequency of their clashing energies.
Aurelia was no longer a woman; she was a celestial event. Driven by the sight of her sister’s limp form, she had transcended the limits of human martial arts.
She entered a state of "Absolute Kinetic Flow," where every movement was a perfect, devastating calculation of force.
BOOM! CRACK! THUD!
She moved with a terrifying, heavy grace. Rex attempted to parry a high roundhouse, but Aurelia didn’t just kick; she drove her entire mass through the strike.
WHAM!
The impact sent Rex spinning, his feet barely touching the ground as he was forced into a frantic, stumbling retreat.

Before he could stabilize, Aurelia was there. She unleashed a "gravity-defying blitz." She didn’t just run; she used micro bursts of kinetic energy from her heels to leap, appearing as a golden strobe light around him.
BAM! BAM! BAM!
A left hook caught Rex in the jaw, snapping his head back with a sickening CRACK! The sound of his teeth clashing was audible even over the roar of the wind.
Before he could recover, a heavy knee slammed into his solar plexus, "OOF!" followed by a devastating elbow that caught him right in the bridge of his nose.
SPLAT!

KABOOM!

CRUNCH SHLICK!

"Is this... the god... you claimed to be?" Aurelia hissed, her voice a low, vibrating roar of contempt.
She didn’t stop. She stepped into his personal space, her movements a relentless, crushing rhythm.

She unleashed the "Titan’s Requiem." It was a sequence of strikes designed to end a life. A heavy palm strike to the chest THOOM! followed by a spinning back fist that caught Rex’s temple WHACK! and finally, a massive, two-handed overhead hammer strike intended to drive him into the very core of the earth.
Rex was reeling. His vision was swimming in a sea of red and gold.
His ribs were a mess of agony, his lungs were screaming, and his left eye was swollen shut. He looked broken.
He looked defeated. He was slumped on one knee, his head hanging low, the heavy, ragged sound of his breathing the only thing audible in the sudden, tense lulls of the fight.

Aurelia stood over him, her golden aura flickering like a dying star, her chest heaving, her face splattered with his blood. She raised her fist one last time, the kinetic energy condensing into a single, blinding point of light.
"End... of the line," she whispered, her voice trembling with the sheer exhaustion of her fury.
She lunged. The hammer strike descended like a falling moon.
WHOOOOOOOOSH!

Rex’s head didn’t lift; it tilted. It was a subtle, almost imperceptible movement, a predator’s feint. As her fist descended, he didn’t move away from the impact; he moved into the vacuum created by her strike.

"GRAVITY SINGULARITY: ZERO POINT!" Rex roared, his voice a tectonic shift.
