chapters.title: Chapter 722. The Shadow Always Follows The Light. I Should Have Counted The Shadows
paragraphs: As Aurelia’s fist passed an inch from his head, Rex exploded upward. He didn’t just strike; he detonated.

He channeled every ounce of his remaining strength, every fragment of his broken ribs, every drop of his blood, and the entirety of his gravitational field into a single, concentrated point in his fist.
KRA KOOOOOOOM!!!
It wasn’t just a punch. It was a collision of two worlds.

His fist caught Aurelia squarely in the center of her solar plexus, right at the moment her energy was most vulnerable from the exertion. The impact was so violent it created a visible shockwave that cleared the dust from the entire plaza in a single, massive ring.
VREEEEEEEEE!
The sound of the impact was a sickening, hollow THUD CRUNCH that seemed to echo in the very marrow of the earth.
Aurelia’s eyes went wide, the golden light in them snuffing out instantly. The air was driven from her body so violently it sounded like bellows being squeezed.
Her entire skeletal structure seemed to buckle under the concentrated force. She was lifted off her feet, her body flying backward like a ragdoll caught in a gale.
SKREEEEEEEEE!
She crashed into the far wall of the crater, the impact shattering the stone and burying her in a tomb of rubble.
Silence fell. A heavy, suffocating silence.
Rex stood in the center of the crater, his body trembling, blood leaking from every wound, his chest heaving in shallow, painful gasps. He looked like a man who had just crawled out of hell.
Slowly, the dust settled. From the wreckage of the far wall, a single, trembling hand reached out, clutching a piece of broken granite, before falling limp.
Aurelia, the unstoppable juggernaut, the sister of the blade, lay motionless, defeated by the very man she thought she had broken.
Rex looked at his bloodied fist, a dark, exhausted smile tugging at the corner of his mouth.
"Told you," he rasped, his voice barely a whisper. "Don’t... hold back."
The silence that followed Aurelia’s massive impact was not the silence of peace, but the heavy, pressurized hush before a thunderstorm breaks.

Rex stood in the center of the crater, a silhouette of carnage. His ribs were a jagged mess beneath his skin, his left eye was a swollen slit of crimson, and his breath came in wet, rattling gasps that sounded like gravel being turned in a drum.
He looked like a man who had been through a meat grinder.
Then, a sound began to rise from his throat.
It started as a low, guttural wheeze, a vibration of pain. But it quickly morphed, growing louder, sharper, and more deranged.
"Heh... hehe... HAAAAA! HAHAHAHAHA!"
The laughter was manic, a jagged, terrifying sound that echoed off the ruined walls of the plaza.
It wasn’t the laugh of a victor; it was the laugh of a man who had stared into the abyss and found it hilarious.
"Is that... is that all?" Rex roared, his voice cracking with a terrifying, unhinged joy.
He wiped a thick smear of blood from his mouth, his eyes wide and gleaming with a predatory, enlightened madness. "You hit so hard, Aurelia!"
"You hit with the weight of a god!" Rex raised both arms to taunt. "Every bone you broke... every breath you stole... it was all a lesson!"
Aurelia, struggling to push herself up from the rubble, stared at him in sheer horror. Her golden aura was flickering, her strength spent.
"You’re... you’re insane..." she rasped, her voice trembling.
"Insane? No!" Rex stepped forward, his movements a strange, rhythmic limp that hid a terrifying precision. "I wasn’t just taking the hits!"
"I was measuring them! Every time you swung that heavy fist, you left a trail of kinetic residue!"
"Every time you lunged, your center of gravity shifted a fraction of a millimeter to the left to compensate for your mass!" Rex grinned. "I didn’t just feel the pain, Aurelia... I studied it!"
He lunged forward, not with a heavy strike, but with a terrifyingly swift, calculated movement.
WHOOSH!

He bypassed her guard with a surgical grace that defied his battered state. He didn’t aim for her head or her chest; he struck the exact pressure point on her thigh that he had identified during her earlier "Mountain Crushing" clinch.
THWACK!
Aurelia’s leg buckled instantly. She collapsed, gasping.
"You’re a brawler, Aurelia! You’re a storm! But storms... storms are predictable!" Rex leaned over her, his face a mask of blood and madness. "And predictability is the precursor to death!"
He raised his fist for a final, crushing blow, his gravity field beginning to swirl around him in a violent, dark vortex. "GRAVITY BURST: OBLIVION!"
He was pouring everything into one last, massive strike to end the fight once and for all. He was a man possessed, a maniacal god of gravity about to flatten the world.
But he had forgotten one thing.
The storm wasn’t just the hammer. It was also the shadow.
As Rex’s fist descended, a sudden, chilling drop in temperature swept through the plaza. The air didn’t roar; it hissed.
FSSSSSS...
From the periphery of Rex’s own gravitational vortex, a shadow detached itself from the darkness. Iris.
She hadn’t just woken up; she had evolved. Her eyes were cold, dead pools of obsidian, her movements so silent they bypassed the very concept of sound.
She didn’t lunge; she simply was there.
SHING!
The sound was almost too rapid for the human ear to process. It was the sound of a single, perfect note played on a razor blade.
Iris utilized her ultimate assassin technique: "THE SILENT HEARTBEAT."

She didn’t strike his armor, his muscles, or his bones. She moved through the microscopic gaps in his gravitational field, her daggers vibrating at a frequency that allowed them to slip through the air itself.
She didn’t aim for a wound; she aimed for the essence.
SST CLICK!
The blades passed through Rex’s chest, appearing to glide through him like a ghost through a wall. There was no spray of blood, no dramatic explosion of force.
Just a single, clean, terrifyingly quiet movement.
Rex froze. His fist, inches from Aurelia’s face, stopped in midair.
The manic laughter died in his throat, replaced by a sudden, hollow stillness. His eyes, once burning with madness, suddenly went wide and vacant.
The light in them didn’t fade; it was extinguished.
"THUMP..."
The sound of his heart was the only thing heard in the entire world. A single, heavy, final beat.
Then, the blood arrived.
A massive, sudden eruption of crimson burst from his chest, as if a dam had finally broken.
SPLASH!
The sheer volume of blood was impossible, a torrential flood that soaked the ground and painted the air red.
Rex’s knees hit the dirt with a heavy, dead weight.
THUD.

He didn’t fall like a warrior; he fell like a mountain of meat. His body slumped forward, his head hanging low, his eyes staring at nothingness. The man who had laughed at the gods, the man who had studied the very essence of violence, was suddenly, terrifyingly still.
Iris stood behind him, her daggers already sheathed, her expression as unreadable as a tombstone. She didn’t look triumphant; she looked as if she had simply completed a task.
"The shadow always follows the light," she whispered, her voice a cold breeze in the carnage.

Rex lay there, a broken monument of blood and bone, the silence of the plaza swallowing his legend whole. It looked as if the very soul of the man had been surgically extracted, leaving behind only a hollow shell in the wake of the assassin’s perfect, lethal grace.
The silence that followed Rex’s supposed death was heavy, suffocating, and thick with the iron scent of the massive pool of blood spreading across the plaza.

Aurelia, still trembling from her near defeat, stared at the slumped, lifeless form of the man who had just been laughing like a demon. Her golden aura flickered out, replaced by a profound, hollow exhaustion.
"We... we actually did it," she breathed, her voice a fragile thread of disbelief. "The hammer and the shadow... we finally broke the mountain."

Iris, standing perfectly poised with her daggers still humming from the lethal vibration of her technique, allowed a rare, microscopic softening of her gaze. She sheathed her blades with a rhythmic "CLICK CLACK" and stepped toward her sister.
The tension that had held her spine rigid for the entire battle finally began to dissolve.
"It was the only way," Iris murmured, her voice regaining its cool, melodic composure.
She reached out a hand to help Aurelia up, a gesture of sisterly triumph. "He was too unpredictable, and he was feeding on the chaos."
"We had to force the stillness upon him."
Aurelia took Iris’s hand, a small, weary smile touching her blood-stained lips. "Together, then. Always together."

chapters.title: Chapter 723. The Best Way To Kill a Legend Is To Let Them Feel The Triumph First
paragraphs: They stood there for a moment, two legends amidst a wasteland, basking in the intoxicating rush of a hard-won victory. They were beginning to celebrate, the adrenaline receding to leave only the warmth of survival.
CRRRRR ACK...
The sound was subtle. It wasn’t the sound of a body moving; it was the sound of mineral grinding against mineral.
Aurelia froze. The smile died on her face.
She looked down at the "body" of Rex lying at their feet. The crimson pool of blood wasn’t flowing anymore; it was hardening.
The skin, once warm and bruised, was turning a dull, matte grey.
CRUNCH! SHATTER!
With a sudden, violent structural failure, the corpse of Rex didn’t just move; it disintegrated. The "flesh" splintered into jagged shards of granite and sedimentary rock.
The blood turned into a dark, viscous sludge of wet clay and crushed garnet.
"What... what is this?" Aurelia gasped, stumbling back as the man she thought she had killed crumbled into a heap of lifeless stone.
SHRRRRR!
"A diversion..." Iris hissed, her eyes snapping wide, her hand instantly flying back to the hilt of her dagger.
Her predatory instincts screamed a warning a millisecond too late.

The realization hit them like a physical blow: The Rex they had been fighting, the one who had taken the brutal hits, the one who had laughed, the one who had bled, wasn’t a man. It was a masterpiece of deception.
VREEEEEEEEE!

The air behind them didn’t just vibrate; it rippled. The very fabric of reality seemed to fold as a massive, overwhelming surge of gravitational energy erupted from the empty space directly behind the sisters.
BOOOOOOM!
Rex materialized out of the dust and the shadow, not as a broken man, but as a god of the earth itself. He hadn’t been dying; he had been reconstituting.

The "Rex" or "Tremor" they had been battling was a highly realistic creation using the "Earthen Apostle" technique, which is a living clay that can feel impact and imitate how a human body reacts, including feeling pain and showing blood.

"Did you really think..." Rex’s voice boomed, no longer a raspy whisper but a thunderous, resonant roar that shook the very foundations of the plaza. "That a man like me could be stopped by a mere trick of the light?"

He stood tall, his skin glowing with a dark, earthen luster, his muscles rippling with a strength that felt as ancient as the tectonic plates. He looked completely uninjured, his eyes burning with a terrifying, triumphant intelligence.
WHAM!
He slammed his fist into his open palm, the sound echoing like a thunderclap.
CLACK!

"The Apostle who’s ascending to godhood doesn’t feel pain, Aurelia," Rex taunted, stepping into their personal space, his presence so massive it felt like the atmosphere was being displaced by his sheer will. "It only learns..."
"Like I said earlier... every strike you gave it, every ’lethal’ blow Iris delivered... was just data," Rex clenched his fists. "It was just shaping the mold!"
Aurelia and Iris spun around, trapped between the pile of shattered stone at their feet and the living mountain of a man looming over them. They were caught in the pincer of his trap.
"You... you let us think we won!" Aurelia yelled, her hands glowing with a desperate, flickering gold as she tried to find her footing. "You let us lower our guard!"
"I didn’t let you think it," Rex grinned, a wide, predatory expression that promised a new kind of devastation. "I made you believe it."
"Because the best way to kill a legend... is to let them feel the triumph first.
He raised both hands, and the ground beneath the sisters began to liquefy, turning into a swirling vortex of hungry, grasping stone.
GURGLE... SHHHH!
"Now," Rex bellowed, his aura expanding until it eclipsed the moon. "Let’s see how you handle the real TREMOR!"

The ground didn’t just shake; it groaned in agony as Rex unleashed the full, unbridled weight of his true form. The "Earthen Apostle" had been a mere puppet, a sacrificial lamb of clay, but the man standing before them now was a titan of pure, concentrated kinetic force.
"The celebration is over!" Rex roared, his voice a tectonic landslide.
KRA KOOOOOM!
He didn’t lunge; he simply stepped, and the sheer displacement of his movement shook the earth.
WHOOSH!
Before Aurelia could even raise her golden aegis, Rex was on her guard. He didn’t use a punch; he used a "Gravity Anchor" strike.
He drove his palm into the center of her chest, not just hitting her but momentarily increasing her own body weight by a factor of a hundred.
THOOMP!

The sound was sickening, the sound of a heavy weight hitting wet sand. Aurelia’s eyes rolled back as the sheer pressure crushed the air from her lungs and drove her straight into the pulverized earth.
CRUNCH!
She didn’t just fall; she was planted. Her body hit the ground with such violence that a crater blossomed outward from her spine, sending shards of stone flying like shrapnel.
SHLICK SHATTER!
She lay there, paralyzed by the sudden, overwhelming heaviness of her own limbs, her golden aura flickering like a dying candle in a storm.
Rex didn’t even look at her. His predatory gaze shifted, locking onto the one who remained standing.
Iris.

The assassin, the shadow, the girl who had just "killed" a god, was suddenly staring into the eyes of the actual predator. For the first time in her life, the ice in Iris’s veins began to melt into pure, unadulterated panic.
Her breath came in short, jagged stabs. "HAA... HAA..."
"You..." Iris whispered, her fingers trembling as she reached for her daggers. "You’re... different."
"I’m the reality you failed to account for," Rex growled.
Iris didn’t wait to find out more. Her survival instinct, honed by a thousand assassinations, screamed one command: RUN.
She turned on her heel, her movements a blur of desperate speed.
FSSSSST!

She attempted to use her "Shadow Step," a technique meant to turn her into a literal flicker of darkness to bypass physical obstacles. She vanished into a streak of black smoke, aiming for the ruins of the outer wall.
But Rex was faster. He didn’t chase her; he manipulated the world to bring her to him.
"GRAVITY WELL: COLLAPSE!"
He slammed both fists into the ground.
BOOOOOOOOOM!
The earth didn’t just rise; it reached. A massive, jagged pillar of stone erupted directly beneath Iris’s path, intercepting her mid-dash.
WHAM!
The collision caught her mid-air, tossing her upward like a pebble.
SKREEE!
As she flailed in the air, vulnerable and stripped of her momentum, Rex was already there.
He had launched himself upward, a dark comet of muscle and stone.
WHACK! CRACK! THUD!
He descended upon her with a relentless, brutal choreography. He caught her mid-air with a rising knee to the abdomen.
"OOF!" Then, as she tumbled, he caught her with a spinning elbow to the temple.
CLANG!
Iris was a leaf in a hurricane. She tried to parry, to twist, to find a footing, but Rex was everywhere. He was a wall of meat and a mountain.
He grabbed her by the throat with a hand that felt like a vice of iron GRIP!, and for a terrifying second, they hung suspended in the air.
"Where is your silence now, little shadow?" Rex hissed, his face inches from hers, his breath hot and smelling of ozone and earth.
He swung her violently against a standing pillar of obsidian.
KRRR ACK!

The impact sent a shudder through her entire frame. He didn’t let her fall; he caught her again, delivering a devastating "Core Breaker" punch to her ribs that sounded like a heavy mallet hitting a sack of dry sticks.
CRUNCH!

Iris slumped in his grip, her vision spinning, her lungs burning, her legendary composure shattered into a million jagged pieces. She was broken, breathless, and staring up at a man who looked ready to finish her once and for all.
The air didn’t just move; it screamed.

Rex’s fist was a descending comet of dark, crushing gravity, aimed straight for the center of Iris’s shattered ribcage. The sheer pressure of his aura was already beginning to liquefy the ground beneath her, turning the stone into a swirling, hungry maw of dust and grit.

Iris looked up, her vision swimming in a haze of crimson and gray, her heart hammering a frantic, dying rhythm against her bruised lungs. She could feel the heat of his approaching strike, a heat that promised nothing but the end.
"DIE!" Rex roared, the sound vibrating through her very marrow.
"STAY THE FUCK AWAY FROM MY GIRLFRIEND, YOU MONSTER!"
The command didn’t just travel through the air; it sliced through it.
A sudden, violent atmospheric shift erupted from the heavens. A massive, invisible weight slammed into the plaza, not from the ground up, but from the sky down.
It was a sudden, chaotic explosion of pressure that momentarily stalled Rex’s descent, forcing his fist to veer inches away from Iris’s face with a thunderous
WHOOOOOOOSH!
High above, silhouetted against the sun like a vengeful deity, was Veylor.
He didn’t descend with a graceful landing; he arrived like a storm front. Utilizing his high-tier wind affinity, Veylor wasn’t just flying; he was commanding the very medium of life and death.
He hovered approximately thirty meters above the carnage, his eyes glowing with a piercing, cyan light.
Without a moment’s hesitation, Veylor unleashed his first working: "AERIAL TURBULENCE: THE WHIRLWIND DOMINION."

chapters.title: Chapter 724. The Sky Is Falling, Little Bird! I Said That Before I Launched Myself
paragraphs: He didn’t aim a single strike. Instead, he threw his arms wide, and the air itself fractured. A massive, distributed wave of localized, high-velocity wind currents exploded outward from his position, sweeping across the entire plaza in a violent, swirling carpet of chaos.
It was a masterpiece of area denial, a chaotic, unpredictable web of microtornados and sudden pressure drops designed to strip an opponent of their most vital asset: their footing.
VREEEEEEE!
The sound of the wind was a high-pitched, agonizing shriek that tore at the ears.

For Aurelia, struggling to rise from her crater, the wind was a nightmare. Every time she tried to stabilize her heavy, bruised limbs, a sudden gust would catch her, tilting her world and forcing her to fight just to stay upright.
For Iris, the turbulence was a dizzying, nauseating blur that made her head spin and her wounds weep fresh blood.
But Rex... Rex was a different matter entirely.

As the winds lashed against him, attempting to buffet his massive frame and throw him off balance, he simply leaned into the chaos. He didn’t fight the wind; he anchored himself to the very core of the world.

Using his gravity manipulation to create a "gravitational anchor," he turned himself into a living mountain. The winds that were tossing the sisters like autumn leaves merely brushed against him, unable to move a single inch of his colossal, blood-stained mass.
To Rex, the turbulence was nothing more than a light breeze against a fortress.
"Is this the best the heavens can send?!" Rex bellowed, a dark, mocking laugh tearing from his throat as he stood unshaken amidst the howling gale. "HAHAHAHA!"

Iris, clutching her side as the wind threatened to sweep her off her feet, looked up through the swirling dust. Her face was a mask of exhaustion and desperation, her hair whipping wildly around her face.
"Veylor!" she screamed, her voice nearly lost in the roaring tempest. "Get higher! You’re catching us in the crossfire!"
"It’s making it impossible to move!"
She struggled to plant her feet, her boots sliding across the vibrating stone as the wind tried to rip her away from the earth.
High above, Veylor’s expression was one of intense, focused concentration. He could see the carnage below the blood, the broken bodies, and the terrifying silhouette of Rex.
He adjusted his stance in the air, his cape snapping like a whip in the gale.
"Sorry!" Veylor called back, his voice projecting with unnatural clarity through the howling wind.
He began to ascend, his aura flaring as he pushed his altitude higher to clear the turbulence he had created. "Trying! Just... hold on a little longer!"
Rex stood amidst the swirling, chaotic winds, a dark monolith of absolute stillness. He didn’t look like a man under siege; he looked like a predator watching a new, captivating insect enter his web.
His eyes, bloodshot and glowing with a terrifying, gravitational hunger, drifted upward, tracking the shimmering silhouette of Veylor in the sky.
’The wind caller,’ Rex thought, a slow, predatory grin spreading across his face. ’The stabilizer...’
’The one who provides the breath to their dying embers.’

He analyzed the tactical shift instantly. Veylor was playing the perfect support role, maintaining distance, providing area denial, and complicating the battlefield to prevent Rex from focusing a singular, lethal kill on either Aurelia or Iris.
It was a sophisticated, high-level maneuver. But in Rex’s eyes, Veylor wasn’t a savior; he was a variable that needed to be crushed.
"Veylor! Don’t just watch!" Iris screamed from the ground, her voice cracking with a mixture of fury and pure, unadulterated terror.
She was coughing up flecks of blood, her hand pressed hard against her shattered ribs. "He’s not like the others! He’s not just a brute! He’s... he’s a god of the earth!
"RUN! Get out of his range before he locks onto you!"
Veylor looked down, seeing the desperation in Iris’s eyes, a look he had never seen on her composed, stoic face. It sent a chill through his soul.
"I’m not leaving you, Iris!" he shouted back, his voice booming through the gale. "Just hold on! I’ll bring the sky down on him!"
"You don’t understand!" Iris shrieked, her voice breaking into a sob of warning. "He’s been waiting for you! BE CAREFUL!"
Rex’s laughter was a low, guttural rumble that seemed to come from the very bowels of the earth. "Careful? Why should a god be careful of a breeze?"
He didn’t lunge. He didn’t even move his feet. He simply raised his right hand, his fingers curling as if he were grasping an invisible throat in the sky.
"GRAVITY WELL: HEAVEN’S COLLAPSE!"
Rex didn’t aim for a strike; he aimed for the space itself. He projected a concentrated, violent surge of gravitational force directly toward Veylor’s position, thirty meters above the carnage.
VREEEEEEEEEEE!
The air didn’t just ripple; it imploded. The localized gravity at Veylor’s altitude didn’t just increase; it skyrocketed to ten times the standard Earth constant in a single, brutal heartbeat.
For a normal fighter on the ground, ten times gravity would have turned their bones to powder and flattened them into the dirt instantly. But Veylor was a master of the Wind Affinity.
His very essence was built on defying weight and constantly manipulating his relationship with gravity to achieve flight.
"GAAAAAAH!" Veylor let out a strangled cry as the invisible hammer slammed into him.
The sky seemed to fall. His flight, working, which had been a graceful, buoyant dance, suddenly became a desperate, violent struggle for survival.
He was fighting a war against the very fundamental laws of the universe. The air around him groaned as his wind aura fought to push back against the crushing, invisible weight.
CRACKLE... HSSSS!
The sound of his mana straining was like the sound of a ship’s hull groaning under the pressure of the deep ocean.
Six seconds.

That was all the time the universe gave him. For six agonizing seconds, Veylor’s energy burned with a blinding, desperate intensity, his entire body vibrating as he fought to keep from being slammed into the earth like a fallen star.
But the reserve requirements were astronomical. The cost of defying ten times the world’s weight was a drain that even his vast reserves could barely withstand.
"HAA... HAA... HAAAA!"
His aura flickered. The shimmering blue light around him began to stutter, the sheer exhaustion of the effort visible in the way his hands trembled. He was reaching the breaking point.
The "Earth Bound" dragged down the "Sky Born."
Rex watched the descent with the patience of a spider. He saw the moment the wind caller’s strength faltered, and he saw the moment the predator’s prey lost its ability to fly.
"The sky is falling, little bird," Rex whispered, his eyes gleaming with a sadistic light.
As Veylor’s flight stabilized into a desperate, wobbling hover, Rex lowered his hand, his muscles coiling like massive, iron springs. The era of support was over.
The era of direct, catastrophic confrontation had begun.
"COME DOWN AND DIE!" Rex roared, launching himself upward like a projectile of pure destruction.

The world seemed to slow down as Rex ascended. He was no longer a man; he was a kinetic missile of dark, crushing mass, a black streak of gravitational fury tearing through the atmosphere toward Veylor.
WHOOOOOOOM!

Veylor, hovering at the precipice of total energy exhaustion, felt the sheer terror of the approaching titan. His lungs burned, his vision was blurring, and the crushing weight of Rex’s gravity was still tugging at his very soul.
He looked down and saw Iris broken, bleeding, and screaming his name with a desperation that pierced his heart.
"Don’t you dare... don’t you dare leave us like this!" her voice echoed in his mind.
Something inside Veylor snapped. It wasn’t the snap of breaking but the snap of a dam bursting.
Suddenly, a roaring, incandescent need to be the hero she deserved eclipsed her fear of death. A surge of pure, unadulterated willpower flooded his veins, igniting his mana core like a supernova.
"You think... you can just drag me down?!" Veylor roared, his voice shedding its politeness and taking on a divine, commanding edge. "I AM THE WIND! AND THE WIND... NEVER STAYS STILL!"
FSSSHHHHHHHHHH!
As Rex reached the apex of his jump, his fist cocked back for a world-ending blow, Veylor didn’t dodge.
He didn’t retreat. He expanded.
He unleashed a massive, omnidirectional burst of high-pressure wind: "AERO DISRUPTION: THE GREAT CLEANSING!"
BOOOOOOOM!

The shockwave was so intense it created a vacuum in its wake. The swirling, dark gravitational aura surrounding Rex, the very magic that made him so dangerous, was caught in the violent, spiraling currents and literally stripped away.
The dark energy was shredded, torn into microscopic particles by the sheer friction of the wind, leaving Rex momentarily naked, his magical armor blown away like tattered rags.
Rex’s eyes widened. For the first time, his momentum was disrupted.
"WHAT?!"
"Watch closely, Iris!" Veylor shouted, his eyes glowing with a blinding, cyan brilliance.
He began to move, not just flying but dancing through the air with a speed that defied physics. "Because this is how a savior looks!"
He dived straight at the stunned Rex, initiating a relentless, high-speed aerial assault.
"STRIKE ONE: ZEPHYR’S LANCE!"
Veylor spun his body into a tight, aerodynamic drill, his mana condensing into a razor-sharp point at his feet.
SHING!
He struck Rex’s shoulder, the wind pressure acting like a physical blade that sliced through skin and muscle.
SPLASH!
A spray of dark, heavy blood erupted as the wind carved a shallow trench into Rex’s massive deltoid.
"Too slow!" Veylor yelled, pivoting in midair with a violent flick of his wrist. "STRIKE TWO: THE TWISTER’S WHIP!"

Don’t just watch!" Iris screamed from the ground, her voice cracking with a mixture of fury and pure, unadulterated terror.
She was coughing up flecks of blood, her hand pressed hard against her shattered ribs.
"He’s not like the others!
He’s not just a brute!
He’s... he’s a god of the earth!
"RUN!
Get out of his range before he locks onto you!"
Veylor looked down, seeing the desperation in Iris’s eyes, a look he had never seen on her composed, stoic face.
It sent a chill through his soul.
"I’m not leaving you, Iris!" he shouted back, his voice booming through the gale.
"Just hold on!
I’ll bring the sky down on him!"
"You don’t understand!" Iris shrieked, her voice breaking into a sob of warning.
"He’s been waiting for you!
BE CAREFUL!"
Rex’s laughter was a low, guttural rumble that seemed to come from the very bowels of the earth.
"Careful?
Why should a god be careful of a breeze?"
He didn’t lunge.
He didn’t even move his feet.
He simply raised his right hand, his fingers curling as if he were grasping an invisible throat in the sky.
"GRAVITY WELL: HEAVEN’S COLLAPSE!"
Rex didn’t aim for a strike; he aimed for the space itself.
He projected a concentrated, violent surge of gravitational force directly toward Veylor’s position, thirty meters above the carnage.
VREEEEEEEEEEE!
The air didn’t just ripple; it imploded.
The localized gravity at Veylor’s altitude didn’t just increase; it skyrocketed to ten times the standard Earth constant in a single, brutal heartbeat.
For a normal fighter on the ground, ten times gravity would have turned their bones to powder and flattened them into the dirt instantly.
But Veylor was a master of the Wind Affinity.
His very essence was built on defying weight and constantly manipulating his relationship with gravity to achieve flight.
"GAAAAAAH!" Veylor let out a strangled cry as the invisible hammer slammed into him.
The sky seemed to fall.
His flight, working, which had been a graceful, buoyant dance, suddenly became a desperate, violent struggle for survival.
He was fighting a war against the very fundamental laws of the universe.
The air around him groaned as his wind aura fought to push back against the crushing, invisible weight.
CRACKLE...
HSSSS!
The sound of his mana straining was like the sound of a ship’s hull groaning under the pressure of the deep ocean.
Six seconds.
That was all the time the universe gave him.
For six agonizing seconds, Veylor’s energy burned with a blinding, desperate intensity, his entire body vibrating as he fought to keep from being slammed into the earth like a fallen star.
But the reserve requirements were astronomical.
The cost of defying ten times the world’s weight was a drain that even his vast reserves could barely withstand.
"HAA...
HAA...
HAAAA!"
His aura flickered.
The shimmering blue light around him began to stutter, the sheer exhaustion of the effort visible in the way his hands trembled.
He was reaching the breaking point.
The "Earth Bound" dragged down the "Sky Born."
Rex watched the descent with the patience of a spider.
He saw the moment the wind caller’s strength faltered, and he saw the moment the predator’s prey lost its ability to fly.
"The sky is falling, little bird," Rex whispered, his eyes gleaming with a sadistic light.
As Veylor’s flight stabilized into a desperate, wobbling hover, Rex lowered his hand, his muscles coiling like massive, iron springs.
The era of support was over.
The era of direct, catastrophic confrontation had begun.
"COME DOWN AND DIE!" Rex roared, launching himself upward like a projectile of pure destruction.
The world seemed to slow down as Rex ascended.
He was no longer a man; he was a kinetic missile of dark, crushing mass, a black streak of gravitational fury tearing through the atmosphere toward Veylor.
WHOOOOOOOM!
Veylor, hovering at the precipice of total energy exhaustion, felt the sheer terror of the approaching titan.
His lungs burned, his vision was blurring, and the crushing weight of Rex’s gravity was still tugging at his very soul.
He looked down and saw Iris broken, bleeding, and screaming his name with a desperation that pierced his heart.
"Don’t you dare... don’t you dare leave us like this!" her voice echoed in his mind.
Something inside Veylor snapped.
It wasn’t the snap of breaking but the snap of a dam bursting.
Suddenly, a roaring, incandescent need to be the hero she deserved eclipsed her fear of death.
A surge of pure, unadulterated willpower flooded his veins, igniting his mana core like a supernova.
"You think... you can just drag me down?!" Veylor roared, his voice shedding its politeness and taking on a divine, commanding edge.
"I AM THE WIND!
AND THE WIND...
NEVER STAYS STILL!"
FSSSHHHHHHHHHH!
As Rex reached the apex of his jump, his fist cocked back for a world-ending blow, Veylor didn’t dodge.
He didn’t retreat.
He expanded.
He unleashed a massive, omnidirectional burst of high-pressure wind: "AERO DISRUPTION: THE GREAT CLEANSING!"
BOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave was so intense it created a vacuum in its wake.
The swirling, dark gravitational aura surrounding Rex, the very magic that made him so dangerous, was caught in the violent, spiraling currents and literally stripped away.
The dark energy was shredded, torn into microscopic particles by the sheer friction of the wind, leaving Rex momentarily naked, his magical armor blown away like tattered rags.
Rex’s eyes widened.
For the first time, his momentum was disrupted.
"WHAT?!"
"Watch closely, Iris!" Veylor shouted, his eyes glowing with a blinding, cyan brilliance.
He began to move, not just flying but dancing through the air with a speed that defied physics.
"Because this is how a savior looks!"
He dived straight at the stunned Rex, initiating a relentless, high-speed aerial assault.
"STRIKE ONE: ZEPHYR’S LANCE!"
Veylor spun his body into a tight, aerodynamic drill, his mana condensing into a razor-sharp point at his feet.
SHING!
He struck Rex’s shoulder, the wind pressure acting like a physical blade that sliced through skin and muscle.
SPLASH!
A spray of dark, heavy blood erupted as the wind carved a shallow trench into Rex’s massive deltoid.
"Too slow!" Veylor yelled, pivoting in midair with a violent flick of his wrist.
"STRIKE TWO: THE TWISTER’S WHIP!"

chapters.title: Chapter 725. All That Light... All That Noise... Just To Impress a Girl (Pathetic Simp)
paragraphs: He swung his arm in a wide arc, a concentrated ribbon of gale-force wind lashing out like a sentient whip.
WHACK CRACK!
The wind caught Rex across the jaw, the force so immense it snapped the titan’s head to the side, the sound of the impact echoing like a whip cracking against a stone wall.
Rex growled, a sound of pure, wounded pride, trying to swing a heavy fist at the blur of blue light, but Veylor was already gone.
"STRIKE THREE: CYCLONE BURST!"
Veylor appeared above Rex, his hands pressed downward.
VREEEEE!
A localized, high-pressure downdraft slammed into Rex’s head, forcing him back toward the earth.
THUD!
"Did you see that, Iris?!" Veylor’s voice was a triumphant melody amidst the chaos, his confidence soaring as high as his altitude.
He was performing a ballet of destruction intended for an audience of one. "I’m just getting started!"
"Don’t blink, or you’ll miss the best part!"

He descended like a falling star, his energy spiraling around him in a massive, roaring vortex. He was gathering every scrap of wind in the plaza, every gust, every breeze, every thermal, into a single, devastating point of focus.
"ULTIMATE COMBO: THE TEMPEST GOD’S JUDGMENT!"
KRRRRRR BOOOOOOOM!
Veylor became a blur of white and cyan light. He struck Rex with a barrage of a hundred rapid-fire air-pressure punches, where each one hit with the force of a cannonball.
BAM! BAM! BAM! BAM!

He followed with a spinning kick that sent a crescent wave of wind slicing through Rex’s midsection SHLICK! and finished by slamming his palms against Rex’s chest, releasing a massive, concentrated explosion of atmospheric pressure.
KRA KOOOOOOOM!

The explosion sent a massive cloud of dust and debris erupting outward. Rex was sent hurtling backward, his body skipping across the ground like a stone across a lake, carving a massive, bloody furrow through the plaza.
SKREEEEEEE!

Veylor hovered in the center of the settling dust, his chest heaving, his hair windswept and wild, a confident, dazzling smirk on his face as he looked down at the carnage. He looked every bit the legendary hero, the master of the skies, waiting for the applause of the woman he loved.
The dust from Veylor’s massive explosion hadn’t even settled before the air began to vibrate with a low, ominous hum. Rex wasn’t dead; he was recovering.

He rose from the bloody furrow in the earth, his skin bruised a deep, angry purple, his breathing heavy and ragged. He wiped a smear of dark blood from his lip, his eyes burning with a renewed, terrifying madness.
"Impressive... little bird," Rex rasped, his voice sounding like grinding tectonic plates. "But a bird that flies too high... is just an easier target for the storm."
Veylor didn’t wait for him to finish. The adrenaline was a drug in his veins, a roaring fire that burned away the exhaustion of the gravity well.
He looked down at Iris, seeing her gaze fixed on him not with the pity he expected, but with wide-eyed, breathless awe. That look was all the fuel he needed.
"You want to see a god of the sky, Tremor?" Veylor’s voice dropped an octave, becoming a resonant, melodic roar that cut through the settling debris. "Then stop looking at the ground and LOOK UP!"
FSSSHHHHHHHH!
Veylor ignited. His energy didn’t just glow; it erupted in a violent, cyan supernova.
He didn’t just fly; he became a streak of pure kinetic energy.
"FIRST FORM: GALE FORCE REVOLVER!"
Veylor descended like a falling star, spinning his entire body into a high-velocity drill of compressed air.
WHIIIIIIIIIIIIIIII!
The sound was a piercing, ultrasonic scream. He slammed into Rex’s chest with the force of a meteor.
KRA THOOOOOM!
The impact didn’t just hit; it penetrated. The air pressure acted like a physical drill, carving a deep, bloody indentation into Rex’s sternum.
CRUNCH!
The sound of Rex’s ribs buckling under the atmospheric pressure was sickeningly audible.
"Too slow, Tremor!" Veylor shouted, already pivoting mid-air.
He used the momentum of the impact to flip backward, his feet catching the air as if it were solid ground. "You’re too heavy! You’re anchored to a dying world!"
"SECOND FORM: THE SHATTERING SONIC BOOM!"
Veylor clapped his hands together with a violent, snapping motion.
CLAP!
A massive, invisible wall of compressed air shot forward, a horizontal blade of wind so sharp it sliced through the very air itself.
SHIIIIIIIIING!
The wave hit Rex squarely in the midsection.
THWACK!
The force was so concentrated it didn’t just push him; it ripped. A jagged, bloody laceration opened across Rex’s abdomen, spraying dark ichor across the stones.
SPLASH!
"Iris! Did you see that?!" Veylor called out, his voice brimming with a cocky, exhilarating joy.
He was performing a dance of death, and he was loving every second of it. He was no longer the boy trying to survive; he was the master of the heavens!
"THIRD FORM: TWISTER LANCE VERTICAL ASCENSION!"
Veylor dove under Rex’s guard, his hands glowing with swirling, miniature hurricanes. He drove both palms into Rex’s solar plexus.
VREEEEEEEEE!
A massive upward surge of wind exploded from the point of contact.
BOOOOOOOOM!
Rex was launched skyward, his massive body soaring into the air like a discarded ragdoll.
WHOOOOOOSH!
"Don’t blink, Iris! Because the sky is about to fall on him!" Veylor yelled, his eyes locked on the rising titan.
He didn’t let Rex reach the apex. Veylor vanished, moving so fast he left afterimages of blue light in his wake.
He appeared above Rex, silhouetted against the sun, looking down with the predatory grace of a hawk.
"FOURTH FORM: THE TEMPEST’S WRATH RAZOR RAIN!"
Veylor swung his arms in a wide, sweeping motion, and the air itself seemed to fracture into thousands of tiny, microscopic blades of wind.
SHLICK! SHLICK! SHLICK! SHLICK!
A torrential downpour of invisible, high-velocity air slashes descended upon Rex. Each one hit with the precision of a surgeon’s scalpel and the force of a whip.
SLASH! CUT! RIP!
Rex’s skin was shredded, his muscles weeping blood as the "rain" carved a thousand tiny wounds into his massive frame.
"You’re nothing but a mountain of meat!" Veylor roared, his voice echoing through the entire plaza.

He began his final descent, his energy swirling around him in a massive, roaring cyclone that dwarfed everything else. The air was screaming, the ground was vibrating, and the very atmosphere felt like it was about to ignite.
"ULTIMATE TECHNIQUE: THE CELESTIAL SUPERNOVA!"

Veylor gathered every ounce of his remaining energy, compressing it into a single, infinitesimal point at the tip of his outstretched finger. The air around him began to warp and distort, creating a vacuum of terrifying intensity.
VREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
"Watch this, Iris! WATCH ME!"
He drove his hand downward, releasing the compressed heavens in a single, catastrophic burst of pure, unbridled wind pressure.
KRA KAAAAAAA BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!

A pillar of cyan light and white wind erupted from the sky, slamming into Rex with the force of a collapsing star. The ground beneath them groaned and shattered, sending a shockwave that leveled the remaining ruins of the plaza.
CRACK! SHATTER! ROAR!
The sound was deafening, a thunderous explosion of divine fury that seemed to shake the very foundations of the world.

The colossal pillar of cyan light slowly ebbed away, leaving behind a landscape that looked like it had been struck by a divine hammer. A thick, choking fog of pulverized stone and steam rose from the crater, obscuring the center of the battlefield.

Veylor hung in the air, his silhouette trembling. His energy was a flickering candle in a hurricane; his lungs felt like they were filled with broken glass, and every muscle in his body screamed in a chorus of agony.
"HAA... HAA... HAA..."
He had given everything. He had poured his very soul into that final strike, a desperate, beautiful display of power intended to end the nightmare and win the heart of the woman he loved.
He looked down through the haze, his eyes searching for Iris, waiting for the look of triumph, the smile, the recognition.
But the silence that followed was not the silence of victory. It was the heavy, suffocating silence of a tomb.
"GULP..."
A sound emerged from the center of the crater. Not a groan of pain, but a low, rhythmic, terrifyingly stable sound.
"Heh... hehe... HAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The laughter erupted from the dust, a deep, guttural, and mocking sound that sent a fresh wave of dread washing over Veylor. As the debris cleared, the silhouette of Rex emerged.
Veylor’s heart plummeted. The wounds the deep, jagged gashes across his abdomen, the shattered ribs, the shredded skin from the razor rain were gone.

The flesh was knitting itself back together in real time, a grotesque, mesmerizing display of [Infinite Regeneration] and [Supreme Healing]. The blood was being reabsorbed, the scars vanishing before the eyes could even register them.
Rex stood there, his skin unblemished, his muscles rippling with a terrifying, renewed vitality. He looked as if he hadn’t just survived a supernova, but had merely taken a refreshing bath.
"Is that... is that it?" Rex asked, his voice dripping with a sadistic, condescending amusement.
He stepped out of the crater, the ground thudding heavily under his feet.
THOOM. THOOM.
Rex looked up at Veylor, his eyes narrowing with pure, unadulterated mockery. "All that noise... all that flashy, sparkling light... just to impress a girl?"
Veylor flinched as if he’d been struck. "What...?"
"You looked like a fucking clown up there!" Rex roared, his laughter turning into a mocking jeer. "A pathetic, desperate little simp! ’Watch me, Iris! Look at me, Iris!’ HAHAHA!"
"You weren’t fighting a war; you were performing a goddamn circus act!"
"You poured your life into a show because you wanted a girl to clap for you!"
"You’re not a warrior, Veylor... you’re a fucking CLOWN!"

chapters.title: Chapter 726. He Wanted To Be A Hero... So I Showed Hin How Much a Hero Can Lose
paragraphs: SHLICK!
Rex wiped a stray bit of dust from his shoulder, his expression turning cold and predatory. "You wasted your most precious energy on a vanity project."
"You thought you were the storm? You were just a gust of wind trying to catch a lady’s eye."
Veylor’s face flushed a deep, humiliated crimson. His hands shook, not from exhaustion this time, but from a stinging, soul-crushing shame.
The "heroic" moment he had envisioned was being torn to shreds by the very man he thought he had broken.
"It wasn’t... it wasn’t just for her..." Veylor whispered, his voice cracking.
"Liar!" Rex bellowed, his aura suddenly flaring with a dark, suffocating intensity that made the air feel heavy enough to drown in.
The ground beneath him began to crack and sink, not from wind, but from the sheer, concentrated mass of his presence.
CRACKLE! RUMBLE!

Rex’s eyes turned a deep, abyssal black, and the temperature in the plaza seemed to drop as his gravity began to warp the very light around him. The mockery vanished, replaced by a terrifying, singular purpose.
"You’ve had your fun, little performer of a fucking clown," Rex growled, his voice dropping to a lethal, quiet hiss that carried more weight than his roar. "You’ve shown the world your tricks."
"Now... it’s time the world sees the truth of what a real god looks like."
Rex planted his feet, his stance widening, his muscles bulging to the point of tearing. The earth beneath him didn’t just crack; it liquefied under the pressure.
"BRACE YOURSELF, BOY!"
"GRAVITY SINGULARITY: EVENT HORIZON!"
Rex didn’t just move; he collapsed the space between himself and Veylor. He became a black hole of pure, kinetic intent.
The air was sucked into the vacuum of his movement, creating a deafening, roaring howl of a thousand dying stars.
VREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
He launched himself upward, not as a man, but as a concentrated point of infinite mass. The sheer force of his ascent shook the plaza, which sent Aurelia and Iris tumbling backward.
BOOOOOOOM!
Veylor, seeing the darkness approaching, felt a primal, ancient fear scream in his mind. This wasn’t a flurry of wind or a flashy trick.
This was the end of all things. The predator wasn’t just coming for him; the universe itself was coming to crush him.
"HAAAAAA!" Rex’s roar echoed through the heavens as he closed the distance in a heartbeat, his fist aimed not at Veylor’s body, but at the very center of his existence.
The collision was not a sound; it was a cataclysm.
KRA THOOOOOOOOOM!

When Rex’s fist met Veylor’s desperate, last-ditch wind barrier, the impact didn’t just break the shield; it shattered the very concept of space. The air exploded outward in a violent, concussive ring of pressure that sent Iris and Aurelia skidding across the dirt.
WHOOOOOOOSH!

Veylor didn’t fly backward; he was driven. Rex’s fist, backed by the weight of a collapsing mountain, punched through Veylor’s energy, through his ribs, and slammed him into the ground with such ferocity that a crater twenty meters wide erupted instantly.
CRUNCH BOOM!
Veylor lay in the center of the wreckage, a broken heap of blue and white. His breathing was a wet, rattling sound.
"Gurgle... huff... huff..." He tried to lift his head, but Rex was already there, standing over him like a dark god of ruin.
"Still trying to stand, little bird?" Rex sneered.
He didn’t use a flashy technique this time. He used raw, brutal, unadulterated violence.
WHACK!
Rex’s heavy boot descended on Veylor’s stomach.
CRACK!
The sound of Veylor’s diaphragm collapsing was sickening. Veylor’s eyes bulged, a spray of crimson blood erupting from his lips.
PHTOOO!
"Stop... please..." Veylor wheezed, his fingers clawing at the dirt.
"Stop? We’re just getting to the encore!" Rex laughed, a cruel, jagged sound.
He reached down, grabbed Veylor by his hair, and hauled his head up.
SHLICK!
The scalp strained, the pain white hot and blinding. "Look at her, Veylor! Look at your precious Iris! See how she watches her ’hero’ turn into a pile of bloody meat!"
BAM!
Rex delivered a short, piston-like punch to Veylor’s jaw.
CRACK!
Veylor’s head snapped to the side, his jaw audibly dislocating.
POP!
BAM! BAM! BAM!
A relentless barrage of heavy, gravitational strikes rained down on Veylor. Rex wasn’t just hitting him; he was using his gravity to pull Veylor’s head into the fist, amplifying the impact.
THUD! CRUNCH! SPLAT!
Each blow was a masterpiece of misery. Veylor’s face became a mask of swelling purple bruises and weeping lacerations.
His nose was flattened, his eyes swollen nearly shut, and his beautiful, flowing hair was matted with a thick, dark slurry of blood and grit.
"NO! STOP IT! STOP ITTTTTTTTT!"
Iris’s scream tore through the air, a sound of pure, unrefined agony. She was crawling toward the crater, her hands bleeding as she dragged her broken body across the stones.
"Tremor! Please! He’s done! He can’t take any more!"
"PLEASE, HAVE MERCY!"

Rex didn’t even look at her. He grabbed Veylor by the throat, his massive fingers sinking into the soft tissue, and lifted him high enough that Veylor’s legs dangled uselessly, kicking the air in a rhythmic, dying spasm.
FLAP FLAP FLAP!
"Mercy?" Rex mocked, his voice a low, terrifying growl.
He leaned in close to Veylor’s ear, so close that Veylor could feel the heat of his murderous breath. "Mercy is for the weak!"

Rex slammed Veylor face-first into a jagged pillar of stone that remained standing in the crater.

The stone shattered, and Veylor’s face followed suit.
SPLAT!

"Look at him, Iris!" Rex roared, turning his head slightly toward her, a sadistic glint in his eyes. "Look at your savior!"
"He looks like a crushed insect!" Rex laughed. "Is this the man you wanted to protect you?!"

"AAAAAAAAAAAAAGGHHHHHHHH!"
Veylor’s scream was a jagged, soul-tearing thing. It wasn’t a warrior’s cry; it was the high-pitched, primal shriek of a wounded animal.

SPLAT! SPURT!
"Look, Iris! Look at his arm!" Rex laughed, holding the limp, mangled limb up like a trophy. "He can’t even hold his sword!"
"He can’t even hold his own dignity!"
Iris was hyperventilating, her hands pressed against her mouth to stifle the sounds of her own retching. "STOP! STOP IT! TREMORRRR, YOU MONSTER!"
"TAKE ME INSTEAD! PLEASE!"

KRA KAAAA BOOOOM!
The impact was so violent that Veylor’s ribcage didn’t just break; it collapsed inward, the jagged bone shards piercing his lungs and heart.
SQUELCH!
Veylor coughed, and instead of breath, a fountain of dark, clotted gore erupted from his mouth.
GURGLE... SPLASH!
He was drowning in his own life force.
"Still breathing? Let’s fix that!" Rex growled. He reached down and gripped Veylor’s jaw and the top of his skull.
With a terrifying, slow-motion heave, he began to pull.
CREEEEEEEAK... RRRRRIP!
The skin of Veylor’s face began to tear away from the bone, the subcutaneous fat and muscle glistening in the sunlight.
SHLICK!
"GYAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH! HEEEEEELP! IRIS! HEEEEEEEELP!"

chapters.title: Chapter 727. He Was A Variable... And I Solved For The Variable
paragraphs: Veylor’s voice was breaking, turning into a wet, gargling whistle as his lungs filled with fluid. His eyes were wide, rolling back in his head, showing only the bloodshot whites as he stared into the abyss of his own demise.
Rex wasn’t finished. He wanted the spectacle to be absolute.
He gathered a massive amount of gravitational energy into his palm, turning it into a dense, black sphere of crushing force.
VREEEEEEEEEEEEE!
"This is the end of the show, little bird!"
"BOOOOOOOOOM!"
He slammed the gravity sphere directly into Veylor’s midsection. The sheer pressure didn’t just bruise; it eviscerated.
The abdominal wall gave way with a sound like a wet sack of grain being struck by a sledgehammer.
THWACK SQUISH!
Intestines, slick and steaming in the cool air, were forced out of the gaping wound, spilling onto the blood-soaked stones.
SLITHER... SPLAT!
Veylor’s screams had faded into a rhythmic, pathetic whimpering. His body was a ruin of shredded meat, exposed bone, and pulsing organs.
He was a hollowed out shell of the man who had just moments ago danced through the clouds.
"He’s... he’s dying... he’s really dying..." Iris whispered, her voice a hollow shell of its former self.
She watched, paralyzed by a mixture of horror and a strange, hypnotic fascination, as the light in Veylor’s eyes began to flicker like a dying lamp.
Rex stood back, breathing heavily, his hands drenched in the warm, red life of his enemy. He looked down at the mess at his feet with a look of profound boredom. "Pathetic!"
"A waste of a good scream."
Veylor tried to lift a hand, the one that wasn’t completely shattered, toward Iris. His fingers twitched in the dirt, leaving red streaks in the dust.
"Hhh... hhh... I... sss..."
But there was no strength left. The connection between his mind and his broken body finally snapped.
The last spark of mana flickered out, and the overwhelming weight of his injuries finally claimed him.
The tension in his broken frame vanished. The frantic, agonizing twitching stopped.
And then, slowly, helplessly...
He fell.

The air was no longer air; it was a thick, metallic soup of pulverized stone and atomized blood. The silence that followed Veylor’s final, shuddering collapse was more deafening than the roar of the battle had ever been.
The stone below his fallen form didn’t just sit there. As Veylor descended, a mangled heap of meat and broken bones, the ground itself seemed to lunge upward to meet him.

Rex, with the cold, calculated precision of a god playing with clay, manipulated the very tectonic plates of the plaza. A massive, jagged golem formation of obsidian-like rubble rose with predatory intent, meeting Veylor’s descent.
CRUNCH THUD!

The impact was sickeningly precise. The stone didn’t cushion him; it crushed him further into the earth, the jagged edges of the rising formation acting like a grinding stone against his already shattered ribs.
Veylor hit the formation and did not bounce. He did not groan and he did not even twitch.
He simply became part of the wreckage. And he also did not get up.
Rex stood over the ruin of the man, his chest rising and falling in a slow, rhythmic tempo. He didn’t look exhausted; he looked satisfied, like a man who had just finished a tedious chore.

He glanced at the flickering holographic interface of his [Foresight], watching the data streams confirm the absolute cessation of Veylor’s vital signs. The red lines had gone flat, and the variable was zeroed out.
Then, Rex turned his gaze toward Iris.
She was a wreck. The legendary assassin, the woman who could move through a room of killers without a sound, was now a trembling, broken thing.

Her energy signature was fluctuating wildly, not with the explosive, chaotic roar of a berserker, but with the terrifying, razor-sharp intensification of a predator pushed to the brink of madness. It was a cold, sharpening grief, a silent scream vibrating in the very atoms of her being.
"Veylor..." Iris whispered. The name was a plea, a prayer to a god that had clearly abandoned them. "VEYLOORRRRR! "

Her voice rose, cracking, losing all the lethal, controlled grace she was known for. She began to crawl, her fingers digging into the blood-soaked cracks of the plaza, dragging her body toward the mound of gore that used to be the man she loved.

"NOOO! VEYLOOORRRRRR! HWAAAAHHHHHHHH!" A strangled, guttural sob tore from her throat, a sound so raw it felt like it was ripping her own vocal cords apart. "VEYLOR! PLEASE...! WAKE UP! WAKE UUUUUUPPPP!"

She reached the edge of the crater, her eyes widening as she saw the reality of him. The sight of his mangled limbs, the hollowed-out cavity of his torso, the way his blood had pooled into a dark, stagnant lake around his head—it was too much.
She collapsed at the edge of the carnage, her hands hovering over him, terrified that if she touched him, he would simply dissolve into red mist.
"You... you monster..." she breathed, her eyes locking onto Rex.
The grief in her gaze was so heavy it felt like it had its own gravitational pull. "You didn’t have to do that...! You didn’t have to make him... you didn’t have to kill him like an animal!!!"

Each word was a jagged shard of glass, delivered with a terrifying, deliberate cadence. She was holding herself together by a single, fraying thread of sheer willpower, her entire being structured around the refusal to scream until her lungs gave out.
Rex looked down at her, his expression as impassive as a mountain. There was no remorse in his eyes, no flicker of guilt, no shadow of an apology.
There was only the flat, chilling acknowledgment of a completed task.
"I know," Rex said. His voice was a low, steady hum in the wake of her hysteria. "I did it anyway."
"Why?" Iris shrieked, the sound echoing off the ruined walls of the plaza, a high, piercing wail of pure, unadulterated agony. "Why him?! Why this way?!"
"Was it not enough to win?!"
"Did you have to destroy him?!"
Rex stepped closer, his shadow falling over her like a shroud.
"Because he was the most efficient way to remove your support without removing you," he stated, his voice devoid of any warmth. "You were the one I was managing for, Iris.
"He was a variable in that equation... An unpredictable, sentimental variable that threatened the stability of the outcome." Rex clenched his fist. "So, I solved for the variable."
"He’s not a variable!" Iris roared, her voice breaking into a sob that sounded like a death rattle.
She slammed her fist into the bloodstained ground, spraying crimson across her own face. "He’s a person! He’s a man! He fought by my side for years! He was--"
She choked on the word. The reality of the silence hit her all over again.
The "was" hung in the air, heavy and suffocating, a tombstone for the man who had just been slaughtered for the sake of a calculation.
"He was," Rex corrected softly.
The small, clinical correction landed on her like a final, crushing blow, more brutal than any of the physical strikes he had dealt Veylor.

Iris turned her head toward Rex, and for the first time since their meeting, the legendary shadow of the battlefield vanished. There was no lethal grace left in her, no calculated poise of a master assassin.

Her face was a ruin of raw, unbridled fury and catastrophic heartbreak. Her eyes, once sharp enough to track a heartbeat from a mile away, were now bloodshot, overflowing with tears that mixed with the grime and blood on her cheeks.
She looked less like a warrior and more like a woman who had just watched the entire world bleed out in front of her.

She opened her mouth to scream a sound that promised a vengeance so deep it would hollow out the earth, but the scream caught in her throat, turning into a jagged, choked sob that made her entire frame shudder violently.
"Hhh... hhh... you... you fucking..." she gasped, her voice trembling with the weight of a thousand unspoken agonies.
Before the outburst could shatter the heavy air, Aurelia moved. Aurelia, ever the tactician, processed the mathematics of the moment faster than Iris’s grieving mind could.

She saw the way Rex’s eyes were still glowing with the residual, cold light of his gravitational aura, the look of a predator that hadn’t quite finished the kill. She saw the way the air around Rex was still vibrating with the violent energy of the slaughter.

With a fluid, decisive motion, Aurelia stepped into the space between them. She didn’t stand in front of Iris like a shield; she positioned herself with the precise, calculated geometry of a redirection, a barrier meant to guide a falling star back into its orbit.
"We need to go," Aurelia commanded. Her voice was low, a sharp blade cutting through the thick, metallic fog of the plaza. "Now!!!"
Iris didn’t even blink. Her gaze remained locked on the mangled, unmoving heap that was Veylor, her eyes tracing the dark, widening pool of crimson that was slowly swallowing his remains.
She was anchored to the carnage.
"Iris," Aurelia said, her voice hardening, injecting a sense of urgent survival into the air. "We need to go... NOW!"
"He just..." Iris started, her voice a broken whisper, a fragile thread of a sentence that died in the heavy silence. "He was just... there... and now he’s..."
She couldn’t finish. To finish the sentence was to accept the finality of the blood and the bone.
"I know," Aurelia intercepted, her eyes darting briefly to Rex, then back to her friend. "I know. But not here. Not like this!"
"Not while the scent of him is still in the air! Come on!"

Rex stood over the ruin of the man, his chest rising and falling in a slow, rhythmic tempo.
He didn’t look exhausted; he looked satisfied, like a man who had just finished a tedious chore.
He glanced at the flickering holographic interface of his [Foresight], watching the data streams confirm the absolute cessation of Veylor’s vital signs.
The red lines had gone flat, and the variable was zeroed out.
Then, Rex turned his gaze toward Iris.
She was a wreck.
The legendary assassin, the woman who could move through a room of killers without a sound, was now a trembling, broken thing.
Her energy signature was fluctuating wildly, not with the explosive, chaotic roar of a berserker, but with the terrifying, razor-sharp intensification of a predator pushed to the brink of madness.
It was a cold, sharpening grief, a silent scream vibrating in the very atoms of her being.
"Veylor..." Iris whispered.
The name was a plea, a prayer to a god that had clearly abandoned them.
"VEYLOORRRRR!
Her voice rose, cracking, losing all the lethal, controlled grace she was known for.
She began to crawl, her fingers digging into the blood-soaked cracks of the plaza, dragging her body toward the mound of gore that used to be the man she loved.
"NOOO!
VEYLOOORRRRRR!
HWAAAAHHHHHHHH!" A strangled, guttural sob tore from her throat, a sound so raw it felt like it was ripping her own vocal cords apart.
"VEYLOR!
PLEASE...!
WAKE UP!
WAKE UUUUUUPPPP!"
She reached the edge of the crater, her eyes widening as she saw the reality of him.
The sight of his mangled limbs, the hollowed-out cavity of his torso, the way his blood had pooled into a dark, stagnant lake around his head—it was too much.
She collapsed at the edge of the carnage, her hands hovering over him, terrified that if she touched him, he would simply dissolve into red mist.
"You... you monster..." she breathed, her eyes locking onto Rex.
The grief in her gaze was so heavy it felt like it had its own gravitational pull.
"You didn’t have to do that...!
You didn’t have to make him... you didn’t have to kill him like an animal!!!"
Each word was a jagged shard of glass, delivered with a terrifying, deliberate cadence.
She was holding herself together by a single, fraying thread of sheer willpower, her entire being structured around the refusal to scream until her lungs gave out.
Rex looked down at her, his expression as impassive as a mountain.
There was no remorse in his eyes, no flicker of guilt, no shadow of an apology.
There was only the flat, chilling acknowledgment of a completed task.
"I know," Rex said.
His voice was a low, steady hum in the wake of her hysteria.
"I did it anyway."
"Why?" Iris shrieked, the sound echoing off the ruined walls of the plaza, a high, piercing wail of pure, unadulterated agony.
"Why him?!
Why this way?!"
"Was it not enough to win?!"
"Did you have to destroy him?!"
Rex stepped closer, his shadow falling over her like a shroud.
"Because he was the most efficient way to remove your support without removing you," he stated, his voice devoid of any warmth.
"You were the one I was managing for, Iris.
"He was a variable in that equation...
An unpredictable, sentimental variable that threatened the stability of the outcome." Rex clenched his fist.
"So, I solved for the variable."
"He’s not a variable!" Iris roared, her voice breaking into a sob that sounded like a death rattle.
She slammed her fist into the bloodstained ground, spraying crimson across her own face.
"He’s a person!
He’s a man!
He fought by my side for years!
He was--"
She choked on the word.
The reality of the silence hit her all over again.
The "was" hung in the air, heavy and suffocating, a tombstone for the man who had just been slaughtered for the sake of a calculation.
"He was," Rex corrected softly.
The small, clinical correction landed on her like a final, crushing blow, more brutal than any of the physical strikes he had dealt Veylor.
Iris turned her head toward Rex, and for the first time since their meeting, the legendary shadow of the battlefield vanished.
There was no lethal grace left in her, no calculated poise of a master assassin.
Her face was a ruin of raw, unbridled fury and catastrophic heartbreak.
Her eyes, once sharp enough to track a heartbeat from a mile away, were now bloodshot, overflowing with tears that mixed with the grime and blood on her cheeks.
She looked less like a warrior and more like a woman who had just watched the entire world bleed out in front of her.

She opened her mouth to scream a sound that promised a vengeance so deep it would hollow out the earth, but the scream caught in her throat, turning into a jagged, choked sob that made her entire frame shudder violently.
"Hhh... hhh... you... you fucking..." she gasped, her voice trembling with the weight of a thousand unspoken agonies.
Before the outburst could shatter the heavy air, Aurelia moved.
Aurelia, ever the tactician, processed the mathematics of the moment faster than Iris’s grieving mind could.
She saw the way Rex’s eyes were still glowing with the residual, cold light of his gravitational aura, the look of a predator that hadn’t quite finished the kill.
She saw the way the air around Rex was still vibrating with the violent energy of the slaughter.
With a fluid, decisive motion, Aurelia stepped into the space between them.
She didn’t stand in front of Iris like a shield; she positioned herself with the precise, calculated geometry of a redirection, a barrier meant to guide a falling star back into its orbit.
"We need to go," Aurelia commanded.
Her voice was low, a sharp blade cutting through the thick, metallic fog of the plaza.
Iris didn’t even blink.
Her gaze remained locked on the mangled, unmoving heap that was Veylor, her eyes tracing the dark, widening pool of crimson that was slowly swallowing his remains.
She was anchored to the carnage.
"Iris," Aurelia said, her voice hardening, injecting a sense of urgent survival into the air.
"We need to go...
NOW!"
"He just..." Iris started, her voice a broken whisper, a fragile thread of a sentence that died in the heavy silence.
"He was just... there... and now he’s..."
She couldn’t finish.
To finish the sentence was to accept the finality of the blood and the bone.
"I know," Aurelia intercepted, her eyes darting briefly to Rex, then back to her friend.
"I know.
But not here.
Not like this!"
"Not while the scent of him is still in the air!
Come on!"

chapters.title: Chapter 728. She Is The Spine of The Defense. If She Breaks, The Island Breaks
paragraphs: Aurelia was right. Rex was currently working in a very intense and focused way, where subtlety was ignored in favor of straightforward, harsh decisions.

He wasn’t feeling "bloodlust" in the traditional sense; he was executing a sequence of violent equations. He was a machine of geometry and mass, and if they stayed, he might just decide that the "variable" of Iris’s grief needed to be solved as well.
Iris looked at Rex one last time. Her gaze was a searing, silent accusation, a promise of a pain he hadn’t yet calculated.
It was a look of pure, concentrated hatred, wrapped in the velvet of absolute misery.
"Look at what you’ve done," her eyes seemed to scream, even as her lips remained parted in a silent, trembling gasp.
Aurelia didn’t wait for a response. She reached out, her arm hooking firmly around Iris’s shaking shoulders, physically forcing the assassin’s momentum away from the crater of death.
She steered her, a heavy, grounding weight, away from the blood-soaked stones of the plaza and toward the relative safety of the nearest intact street.
Rex watched them go. He didn’t move to follow, nor did he offer a parting word.

He simply stood amidst the ruins of the man he had dismantled, his eyes tracking their retreating forms with the detached interest of a scientist watching a reaction settle. He let them go because Aurelia’s assessment was mathematically sound: the interaction had reached its logical conclusion.
The massacre was over. For now.
Rex turned his back on the retreating shadows of Iris and Aurelia, his gaze shifting with predatory smoothness toward the only threat still standing in his immediate vicinity.
Apollo.

The man was back on his feet, his silhouette trembling against the backdrop of the ruined plaza. The life affinity designation had begun its silent, microscopic work, stitching together the fraying edges of Apollo’s stamina.

It hadn’t restored him to his full, luminous glory, but it had dragged him back from the brink of collapse to a functional, desperate level of combat readiness. He was coming with everything he had left, a lashing, frantic energy born of grief and necessity.
"You didn’t just kill my friends... but you too killed someone close to her," Apollo said.
His voice was low, a serrated whisper that vibrated with a rage so profound it had moved past the stage of shouting and into something much more dangerous: a cold, vibrating stillness.
"Veylor... he wasn’t even fighting you directly..." Apollo gritted his teeth. "He was just... he was just there, and you slaughtered him like a beast in a pen!"
Rex didn’t even blink. He stood amidst the gore of Veylor’s remains, the blood of a comrade still wet on his boots.
"He was supporting two people who were fighting me," Rex countered, his voice as flat and unyielding as a tombstone. "In any logical system, that person qualifies as a combatant."
"He was fighting me from a distance." Rex raised both his arms. "The distance is a variable, not an excuse."
"That’s not how the world works!" Apollo roared, his energy flaring in a jagged, golden burst that cracked the stones beneath his feet.
CRACK!
"That’s not how honor works!"
"It is, actually," Rex said, a flicker of genuine, chilling boredom crossing his features. "It’s exactly how it works."
"I don’t understand why everyone is so perpetually surprised by the fundamental nature of conflict," Rex shrugged. "The fighting part was never going to be the gentle part...
"It was always going to be the part where things break."
"You son of a—" Apollo’s hands began to glow, the light of his life affinity turning a violent, pressurized gold.
"Save your breath," Rex interrupted, his eyes narrowing as his gravitational aura began to hum with a low, terrifying frequency.
VREEEEEEEEE!
"You’re going to need every lungful for what comes next."
Rex lunged. The air screamed as he moved, a blur of concentrated mass.
He met Apollo halfway, and the collision was a deafening explosion of light and pressure.
BOOOOOOM!
The second engagement was a frantic, brutal dance of golden light and crushing darkness, a symphony of clashing energies that tore the very air asunder until the world itself seemed to split open.
SHHHHHHHH LINK!
Valentina arrived. She did not descend from the sky, nor did she run across the dirt.

She manifested through the very fabric of the island’s surface. It was the high-tier projection technique used by the most elite mages, a way to engage the battlefield without the vulnerability of physical transit.

She deployed a spatial separation technique, a masterpiece of impossible physics. In less than two seconds, a yawning, invisible chasm of distorted space slammed between Rex and Apollo, forcing forty meters of "nothingness" to exist between them.
The sudden vacuum caused a violent atmospheric snap.
WHUMP!
Rex skidded to a halt, his boots carving deep grooves into the stone. He stared at the shimmering, distorted void that now separated him from his prey.
He didn’t look frustrated; he looked observant. And then he turned his head, orienting his senses toward the source of the spatial distortion.
Valentina was positioned at the Academy’s main gate. Through the [Foresight], Rex mapped her position and realized she hadn’t sent this as a mere defensive barrier.

She wasn’t a distant operator playing a game of chess; she was a direct opponent, a grandmaster stepping onto the board. The massive mana signature she was weaving at the gate wasn’t a continuation of the spatial separation; it was the opening gambit of a much larger, much more lethal engagement.
Rex began to walk toward her. His stride was heavy and purposeful, each step echoing like a heartbeat in the silent courtyard.
As he moved, the golems scattered across the island fed him a relentless stream of data through the relay network. The tactical picture was grim.
The situation for Aethelgard was catastrophic. The enemy had neutralized, broken, or forcibly redirected sixty percent of the island’s active combat forces.
The golem network’s elevated, systemic output had acted like a tightening noose, creating a pressure that individual warriors simply couldn’t withstand. The outer ring villages were smoldering ruins.
The consolidation sweep was a success, effectively cutting off the reincarnator population from the Apostle network’s protection in four out of the seven populated areas.

The only thing keeping the island from total collapse was the remaining thirty percent of the force; the thirty percent were anchored to Valentina’s telepathic coordination network. She was the spine of the entire defense.
If she broke, the island broke.
Rex looked at Valentina across the shattered, bloodstained courtyard. The distance between them felt heavy, pregnant with the weight of the coming storm.
She looked back at him. Her expression was not one of fear but of terrifying, crystalline clarity.

She was the most powerful mage on the island, a woman who had just witnessed the unthinkable: the fall of Morwenna Nightwing in a mere eight minutes of brutal, lopsided combat. She had processed the implications.
She had seen the math. And she knew exactly what kind of monster was walking toward her.

Rex’s footsteps were slow, rhythmic, and maddeningly casual as he crossed the threshold of the broken courtyard. He walked as if he were strolling through a garden rather than a graveyard of his own making.
A low, dark chuckle bubbled up from his chest, a sound that lacked any warmth; it was the sound of a man who had already seen the end of the world and found it amusing.
"Headmaster," Rex called out, his voice carrying effortlessly across the expanse of shattered stone.
He tilted his head back, a cocky, lopsided grin spreading across his face. "I was hoping we’d get to this eventually."
"Though, I’ll admit, I expected the conversation to go a little differently than this." He gestured vaguely at the smoking ruins and the blood-slicked ground around them.

Valentina stood like a statue of ancient marble, her energy radiating from her in visible, shimmering waves of violet light. Her eyes were cold, but there was a flicker of something, exhaustion perhaps, or a deep, simmering fury behind them.
"Did you?" she countered, her voice a sharp, melodic blade. "And what, exactly, did you expect, Tremor?"
Rex laughed again, a sharp, barking sound that seemed to mock the very gravity of the situation. "HA!"

He wiped a stray droplet of Veylor’s blood from his cheek, looking at it with detached curiosity before flicking it away. "Honestly? I expected to be having a much quieter discussion with you in your office sometime next month."
"Maybe over a glass of something expensive," Rex laughed. "We were talking about a name, remember? A legacy."
He paused, his grin widening into something more predatory. "I’d hoped that conversation would carry more weight than it apparently does right now."
"But then again, you always were a bit too fond of the ’heroic’ struggle, weren’t you?"
For a fraction of a second, something flickered across Valentina’s face, a momentary crack in her impenetrable mask. A shadow of doubt, or perhaps a flash of old respect.
Rex’s [Foresight] caught it instantly, and his grin turned triumphant.
"It does matter," she said, her voice regaining its ironclad composure. "The past matters."
"But that doesn’t change what I am going to do to you in the next five minutes."
"Fair enough!" Rex conceded, though his tone suggested he found her resolve adorable.
He spread his arms wide, his silhouette framed by the chaos of the burning island. "I love the passion! Truly!"
