chapters.title: Chapter 748. She Figured Out The Battlefield Was A Stage. Twelve Minutes Too Late
paragraphs: Ignivara’s eyes burned with a fierce, unyielding light. Despite the crushing weight, despite the agony of the gravity and the exhaustion of her transformation, she refused to give him the satisfaction of a silent death.
"It... will... not... help... you..." she hissed, the words forced out through a haze of steam and golden blood.
Rex let out a short, sharp laugh, his eyes locking onto hers with a terrifying, clinical hunger.
"It is already helping me," Rex said, his grin widening. "Every time you perform above my estimated capacity, I learn something new about the upper boundary of what a half dragon can generate."
"You aren’t just an opponent, Ignivara... You are extremely useful data."

The fire erupted again, but the sheer, crushing weight of the ninefold gravity was fighting the very nature of the flame. Instead of a soaring pillar of destruction, the fire was forced downward, a heavy, viscous torrent of molten light that curved toward the earth like a waterfall of sunfire.
FSSSSSS BOOOOM!
Rex didn’t flinch. He timed the curve with the predatory precision of a man who lived in the gaps between seconds.
He stepped right through the edge of the thermal arc, the heat singeing the hair on his arms and the edges of his clothes, but he emerged unscathed on the other side.
"I am describing what I found in the geological substrate when I integrated with the island," Rex said, his voice steady, almost academic.

He transitioned back to the topic with a terrifying, seamless ease, as if they were sitting in a library rather than hovering in a localized gravity well of death. "Your survey markers. The three months of analysis. All of it is still etched into the rock."
"It is the most detailed third-party assessment of this island’s foundational architecture ever produced. It’s better than anything the Academy’s geological department has on file."
HAAAAAH... HAAAAAH... GRRRRRR!
Ignivara’s breathing was a ragged, violent thing.
FSSSSSS... HAAAAA!

Steam hissed from her scales as her body fought the degradation of the transformation. The sheer effort of maintaining her massive form under nine times gravity was causing her muscles to twitch and ripple with agonizing micro spasms.
"I am not going to stop talking about it," Rex continued, his eyes glowing with a cold, intellectual fervor. "Because it genuinely deserves to be said."
"Whatever Kregg did with the rest of his career, whatever the Legion has been doing for thirty years... that analysis was real work."
"Most people do not do real work, Ignivara."
"Most people do ’adequate’ work and call it real because they are too blind to see the difference."
He tightened his grip on the Gravity Manipulation, holding the frequency steady against the chaotic, crumbling layers of her transformation. "You do."
"That is his essence, and it transferred to you."
"Stop..." she rasped.
The word was a jagged shard of glass, torn from a throat that was struggling to exist under the weight of a mountain.
KRRR ACK!
The sound of her straining vocal cords was almost as painful as the gravity itself.
"Stop what?" Rex countered, a cocky, infuriating tilt to his head. "Stop being right about it?"
"Stop... using it!" she snarled, a plume of smoke escaping her nostrils in a frustrated burst.
FSSSSS!
"You are not saying it because you mean it!"
"You are saying it because you calculated... that it is the thing most likely to make me angrier than I already am!"
"You want me angry... because an angry opponent makes worse decisions."
Rex didn’t deny it. He didn’t even blink.
"Both things can be true at the same time," he said, his voice smooth as silk. "I mean it, and it makes you angry."
"That isn’t manipulation, sweetheart. That is efficiency."
Then, the breaking point arrived.

The massive, draconic overlay began to dissolve. It was a violent, shimmering process, the scales receding into skin, the wings folding into bone and sinew with a series of wet, sickening CRUNCHES and SLURPS.
For twenty agonizing seconds, the transformation fought itself, a chaotic shedding of divinity.
As the dragon faded, the humanoid Ignivara was left suspended sixty meters in the air, still trapped in the ninefold gravity field. Without the lift of her wings, she was a stone waiting to fall.
"Got you," Rex whispered.
Before the gravity could turn her into a red smear on the streets below, he lashed out with telekinesis.
VREEEEE!

He caught her mid-air, a shimmering invisible cushion absorbing the terrifying momentum of her descent. He guided her down, a controlled, gentle descent that contrasted sharply with the brutal violence of the last few minutes.
He lowered her to the nearest intact rooftop of Aethelgard.
THUD.
She hit the tiles on her knees, the impact sending a small tremor through the roof. She stayed there, hunched over, her chest heaving in deep, shuddering gasps.
HAAAH... HAAAH... HAAAH...
Her skin was flushed, slick with sweat and the golden residue of her dragon blood. Rex landed two meters away, his movements fluid and effortless, and finally released the gravity manipulation.
The air seemed to sigh as the pressure returned to standard.
The rooftop was eerily quiet, the heavy, ringing silence that follows a thunderclap.

Ignivara stared at the tiles beneath her trembling hands for a long moment, her fingers tracing the cracks in the stone. Then, she slowly lifted her head, her eyes burning with a mixture of exhaustion and pure, unadulterated fury.
"You planned this rooftop," she said, her voice low and dangerous.
"I planned for the engagement to end somewhere with structural integrity," Rex replied, his tone as casual as if he were discussing the weather. "This was the closest option with a stable surface."
"You planned where I would land," she corrected, her gaze piercing through him. "Before the engagement even started.
Rex offered her a small, devastatingly confident smirk. "I planned for several possible landing locations depending on how the geometry of the fight evolved."
"This was simply the one the math selected."
"Don’t be mad, Ignivara... I prepared for all of them."
Ignivara stared at him, her chest still heaving, the sweat on her skin glistening like liquid gold under the morning sun. Her eyes weren’t filled with admiration, nor were they filled with contempt.

It was something far more unsettling: the hollow, wide-eyed expression of a strategist who had just realized the entire battlefield had been a stage and the director had been playing her the whole time. She wasn’t just reacting to the loss of the fight; she was processing the terrifying scope of being comprehensively outmanaged.
"What... are you?" she asked.

It wasn’t an aggressive snarl. It was a genuine, breathless question, the kind of sound a person makes when their entire worldview has just been shattered and they are desperately searching for a new framework to hold the pieces together.
"A student," Rex replied, his voice possessing the infuriatingly pleasant composure of a man delivering an answer he had rehearsed and thoroughly enjoyed giving.
"You know damn well," she spat, a small puff of smoke escaping her lips, FSSSSS, "that is not going to be enough."
"What you choose to accept does not change the reality of what I am," Rex countered, his gaze unwavering.
She sat back on her heels, her muscles aching with a deep, structural fatigue. She turned her head to look at the city below the rooftop’s edge.

The district was a scarred mess of shattered masonry and smoldering ruins. In the streets, the tiny, ant-like movements of people were beginning to shift; they were realizing the immediate terror of the dragon’s wrath had passed, and they were beginning the frantic, messy business of surviving a catastrophe they never expected to live through.
"The analysis was correct," Rex said, his voice cutting through the distant sounds of the city. "The island’s foundational principle is real."
"The vulnerability point is real." He glanced up at the morning sky, where the secondary dragon was still circling at a lower altitude.

The beast’s behavior had shifted; it was no longer the coordinated, lethal weapon it had been under Ignivara’s command. It was now just a restless, confused animal, searching for a rider who had fallen.
"And none of that is going to happen today."
Ignivara looked up at him, her golden eyes narrowing. "Why are you telling me this?"

"Because the work you did was real work," Rex said, his tone dropping into something uncharacteristically solemn. "And real work deserves an honest assessment of why it failed to produce the result it was designed for."
The silence that followed was heavy, pregnant with the tension of things unsaid.
"You want something," she said finally, her voice a low, dangerous vibration.
"I always want something," Rex admitted with a cocky, lopsided grin. "Today specifically, I want this island to still be here by evening and the people on it to still be alive."
"I’ve been working toward that since before you even touched down, and I intend to continue long after this conversation ends."
"That is not the only thing you want," she hissed, her eyes flashing.
"No," Rex agreed, his eyes locking onto hers. "But it is the thing most relevant to the next hour."
She looked at him, really looked at him.
She saw the silhouette of the one that caused chaos in the underlayer with its mask and cape. And the face of a man who looked far too calm for someone who had just survived a god-tier engagement.
She saw a man who was too depleted to perform any more grand gestures and was therefore performing nothing but the most brutal truth.
"You are..."

sentences.text: Ignivara’s eyes burned with a fierce, unyielding light.
Despite the crushing weight, despite the agony of the gravity and the exhaustion of her transformation, she refused to give him the satisfaction of a silent death.
"It... will... not... help... you..." she hissed, the words forced out through a haze of steam and golden blood.
Rex let out a short, sharp laugh, his eyes locking onto hers with a terrifying, clinical hunger.
"It is already helping me," Rex said, his grin widening.
"Every time you perform above my estimated capacity, I learn something new about the upper boundary of what a half dragon can generate."
"You aren’t just an opponent, Ignivara...
You are extremely useful data."
The fire erupted again, but the sheer, crushing weight of the ninefold gravity was fighting the very nature of the flame.
Instead of a soaring pillar of destruction, the fire was forced downward, a heavy, viscous torrent of molten light that curved toward the earth like a waterfall of sunfire.
FSSSSSS BOOOOM!
Rex didn’t flinch.
He timed the curve with the predatory precision of a man who lived in the gaps between seconds.
He stepped right through the edge of the thermal arc, the heat singeing the hair on his arms and the edges of his clothes, but he emerged unscathed on the other side.
"I am describing what I found in the geological substrate when I integrated with the island," Rex said, his voice steady, almost academic.
He transitioned back to the topic with a terrifying, seamless ease, as if they were sitting in a library rather than hovering in a localized gravity well of death.
"Your survey markers.
The three months of analysis.
All of it is still etched into the rock."
"It is the most detailed third-party assessment of this island’s foundational architecture ever produced.
It’s better than anything the Academy’s geological department has on file."
HAAAAAH...
HAAAAAH...
GRRRRRR!
Ignivara’s breathing was a ragged, violent thing.
FSSSSSS...
HAAAAA!
Steam hissed from her scales as her body fought the degradation of the transformation.
The sheer effort of maintaining her massive form under nine times gravity was causing her muscles to twitch and ripple with agonizing micro spasms.
"I am not going to stop talking about it," Rex continued, his eyes glowing with a cold, intellectual fervor.
"Because it genuinely deserves to be said."
"Whatever Kregg did with the rest of his career, whatever the Legion has been doing for thirty years... that analysis was real work."
"Most people do not do real work, Ignivara."
"Most people do ’adequate’ work and call it real because they are too blind to see the difference."
He tightened his grip on the Gravity Manipulation, holding the frequency steady against the chaotic, crumbling layers of her transformation.
"You do."
"That is his essence, and it transferred to you."
"Stop..." she rasped.
The word was a jagged shard of glass, torn from a throat that was struggling to exist under the weight of a mountain.
KRRR ACK!
The sound of her straining vocal cords was almost as painful as the gravity itself.
"Stop what?" Rex countered, a cocky, infuriating tilt to his head.
"Stop being right about it?"
"Stop... using it!" she snarled, a plume of smoke escaping her nostrils in a frustrated burst.
FSSSSS!
"You are not saying it because you mean it!"
"You are saying it because you calculated... that it is the thing most likely to make me angrier than I already am!"
"You want me angry... because an angry opponent makes worse decisions."
Rex didn’t deny it.
He didn’t even blink.
"Both things can be true at the same time," he said, his voice smooth as silk.
"I mean it, and it makes you angry."
"That isn’t manipulation, sweetheart.
That is efficiency."
Then, the breaking point arrived.
The massive, draconic overlay began to dissolve.
It was a violent, shimmering process, the scales receding into skin, the wings folding into bone and sinew with a series of wet, sickening CRUNCHES and SLURPS.
For twenty agonizing seconds, the transformation fought itself, a chaotic shedding of divinity.
As the dragon faded, the humanoid Ignivara was left suspended sixty meters in the air, still trapped in the ninefold gravity field.
Without the lift of her wings, she was a stone waiting to fall.
"Got you," Rex whispered.
Before the gravity could turn her into a red smear on the streets below, he lashed out with telekinesis.
VREEEEE!
He caught her mid-air, a shimmering invisible cushion absorbing the terrifying momentum of her descent.
He guided her down, a controlled, gentle descent that contrasted sharply with the brutal violence of the last few minutes.
He lowered her to the nearest intact rooftop of Aethelgard.
THUD.
She hit the tiles on her knees, the impact sending a small tremor through the roof.
She stayed there, hunched over, her chest heaving in deep, shuddering gasps.
HAAAH...
HAAAH...
HAAAH...
Her skin was flushed, slick with sweat and the golden residue of her dragon blood.
Rex landed two meters away, his movements fluid and effortless, and finally released the gravity manipulation.
The air seemed to sigh as the pressure returned to standard.
The rooftop was eerily quiet, the heavy, ringing silence that follows a thunderclap.
Ignivara stared at the tiles beneath her trembling hands for a long moment, her fingers tracing the cracks in the stone.
Then, she slowly lifted her head, her eyes burning with a mixture of exhaustion and pure, unadulterated fury.
"You planned this rooftop," she said, her voice low and dangerous.
"I planned for the engagement to end somewhere with structural integrity," Rex replied, his tone as casual as if he were discussing the weather.
"This was the closest option with a stable surface."
"You planned where I would land," she corrected, her gaze piercing through him.
"Before the engagement even started.
Rex offered her a small, devastatingly confident smirk.
"I planned for several possible landing locations depending on how the geometry of the fight evolved."
"This was simply the one the math selected."
"Don’t be mad, Ignivara...
I prepared for all of them."
Ignivara stared at him, her chest still heaving, the sweat on her skin glistening like liquid gold under the morning sun.
Her eyes weren’t filled with admiration, nor were they filled with contempt.

It was something far more unsettling: the hollow, wide-eyed expression of a strategist who had just realized the entire battlefield had been a stage and the director had been playing her the whole time.
She wasn’t just reacting to the loss of the fight; she was processing the terrifying scope of being comprehensively outmanaged.
"What... are you?" she asked.
It wasn’t an aggressive snarl.

It was a genuine, breathless question, the kind of sound a person makes when their entire worldview has just been shattered and they are desperately searching for a new framework to hold the pieces together.
"A student," Rex replied, his voice possessing the infuriatingly pleasant composure of a man delivering an answer he had rehearsed and thoroughly enjoyed giving.
"You know damn well," she spat, a small puff of smoke escaping her lips, FSSSSS, "that is not going to be enough."
"What you choose to accept does not change the reality of what I am," Rex countered, his gaze unwavering.
She sat back on her heels, her muscles aching with a deep, structural fatigue.
She turned her head to look at the city below the rooftop’s edge.
The district was a scarred mess of shattered masonry and smoldering ruins.

In the streets, the tiny, ant-like movements of people were beginning to shift; they were realizing the immediate terror of the dragon’s wrath had passed, and they were beginning the frantic, messy business of surviving a catastrophe they never expected to live through.
"The analysis was correct," Rex said, his voice cutting through the distant sounds of the city.
"The island’s foundational principle is real."
"The vulnerability point is real." He glanced up at the morning sky, where the secondary dragon was still circling at a lower altitude.
The beast’s behavior had shifted; it was no longer the coordinated, lethal weapon it had been under Ignivara’s command.
It was now just a restless, confused animal, searching for a rider who had fallen.
"And none of that is going to happen today."
Ignivara looked up at him, her golden eyes narrowing.
"Why are you telling me this?"
"Because the work you did was real work," Rex said, his tone dropping into something uncharacteristically solemn.
"And real work deserves an honest assessment of why it failed to produce the result it was designed for."
The silence that followed was heavy, pregnant with the tension of things unsaid.
"You want something," she said finally, her voice a low, dangerous vibration.
"I always want something," Rex admitted with a cocky, lopsided grin.

She saw the silhouette of the one that caused chaos in the underlayer with its mask and cape.
And the face of a man who looked far too calm for someone who had just survived a god-tier engagement.
She saw a man who was too depleted to perform any more grand gestures and was therefore performing nothing but the most brutal truth.
"You are..."

chapters.title: Chapter 749. The Rooftop Liquefied. We Moved The Meeting To The Stratosphere.
paragraphs: "You are going to keep doing this," she said.
It wasn’t a question; it was a condemnation. "Whatever this is... The Academy... The Underlayer... The masks you wear..."
"You are going to keep playing these games, and most people are never going to know what they are actually looking at."
"You’re still accusing me for all the things you said, huh?" Rex chuckled. "Well, it’s fine... I feel honored for you to think of that because that means I’m stronger than before."
"For your question, well yeah, most people," Rex said, his voice smooth as silk, "are not looking at all!"
"But you are the one who’s probably so keen about it, thanks to your Dragon’s nature, I guess... That is the only difference that matters."
"Is that meant to be a compliment?" she asked, her voice trembling with a mix of exhaustion and rising heat.
"It is an accurate observation," Rex said. "Whether it is a compliment depends on what you think looking clearly at things is worth."
"What do you think it is worth?"
Rex paused, choosing his words like a surgeon choosing a blade. "Everything. Eventually. The problem is the timeline."
"What happens now?" she demanded, her hands clenching into fists on the rooftop tiles.
CRACK.
Rex looked down at the plaza, at the chaotic skirmishes still raging between Apollo and Zane, at the circling dragon, and at the broken city.
"Now," Rex said, "I go deal with the rest."
He turned to walk away, his back turned to her, a gesture of supreme confidence, or supreme arrogance.
"DON’T YOU DARE!"
The roar didn’t come from her throat; it came from her soul.
RRRRRRRR AAAAAAGGHH!
The air around Ignivara suddenly ignited. It wasn’t the controlled, channeled fire of her dragon form but a raw, volcanic eruption of pure, unadulterated rage.
The temperature on the rooftop skyrocketed in a heartbeat.
FSSSSSSSSSS BOOOOOOOOOM!
A shockwave of heat slammed into Rex’s back, forcing him to halt. He turned just in time to see her rising, not with the grace of a dragon, but with the violent, jagged energy of a supernova.
Her eyes weren’t just gold anymore; they were bleeding light, the pupils slitting into vertical lines of pure white heat.
"You think you can just... analyze me?" she screamed, her voice cracking with a terrifying, primal power.
SKREEEEEEE!
"You think you can categorize my life, my work, and my fury into your little notebooks?!"
The rooftop beneath her began to liquefy, the tiles turning to glowing slag.
Ssssssssss...
"You want to deal with the rest?!" she roared, her energy flaring so violently that the very air began to scream in protest.
VREEEEEEE!
"Then deal with ME first!"
She didn’t transform back into the dragon; she did something far more dangerous. She pulled the dragon’s essence into her humanoid frame.

Her skin began to crack like cooling lava, revealing a blinding, molten core beneath. Her hair whipped around her head like a crown of white fire, and the sheer pressure of her aura sent cracks spider webbing across the entire roof.
KRA KOOOOOM!
She lunged. She didn’t fly; she exploded toward him, a streak of golden light and pure, vengeful heat, her fingers elongated into shimmering claws of solidified flame.
She wasn’t fighting to win anymore; she was fighting to burn the world and him to ash.
The impact was not a mere collision; it was a kinetic catastrophe. When Ignivara struck, she didn’t just hit Rex; she detonated against him.
BOOOOOOOOM!
The rooftop didn’t just crack; it disintegrated. The shockwave sent a plume of pulverized stone and molten tile screaming into the sky.

Rex, caught mid-turn, barely had time to snap a gravity Well around his body to prevent being flattened by the sheer momentum of her lunge. He felt the heat of her molten skin searing through his clothes, the smell of singed fabric and ozone filling his lungs.
"Then let’s see how much data you can process in a single second!" Rex grunted, his teeth gritting as he braced himself.
Ignivara didn’t give him the luxury of a breath. She was a whirlwind of incandescent fury.
Her fists, wreathed in white-hot dragon fire, became a blur of violent motion.
WHAP WHAP WHAP WHAP!
A barrage of strikes rained down on him, each one accompanied by the deafening CRACK of displaced air.
KRA KOOOOM!
A heavy hook caught him in the ribs, the sound of bone groaning under the pressure echoing through the air.
CRUNCH.
Rex felt a rib hairline fracture, a sharp spike of agony lancing through his side, but he didn’t retreat. He used the momentum of her strikes to propel them both upward.
"Higher!" he commanded himself, lashing out with a burst of telekinetic propulsion from his feet.
They tore through the clouds, a streak of golden light and silver shadow ascending toward the stratosphere. Ignivara was relentless.
She wasn’t just using physical force; she was venting her very soul.
FSSSSSS HAAAAAA!

She unleashed a continuous stream of concentrated dragon fire from her palms, a lancing beam of solar intensity. Rex spun in mid-air, the beam grazing his shoulder, the heat so intense it instantly cauterized the wound, leaving a blackened, smoking welt.
VREEEEEEE ZAP!
She followed the fire with a volley of magical projectiles, shards of solidified mana that looked like falling stars.
SHING! SHING! SHING!

Rex danced through the barrage, his eyes darting, his mind calculating trajectories in milliseconds. He raised a gravity shield, the shards slamming into the invisible barrier with the sound of heavy hammers hitting an anvil.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
"Is that all?!" Rex taunted, his voice strained but brimming with that maddening, cocky edge. "You’re fighting like a wounded animal, Ignivara!"
"Where is the precision? Where is the work?!"
That was the wrong thing to say.
"SHUT... UP!"
Her roar was a tectonic event.
RRRRRR AAAAAGGHH!
She surged forward, her body becoming a living comet. She caught Rex in a mid-air clinch, her arms wrapping around his waist like heated iron bands.
The heat was unbearable, melting the very air between them.
Ssssssssss!
KRA KOOOOOOM!

She slammed him upward, a massive, singular thrust of mana that sent them skyrocketing past the cloud layer. The sky turned from blue to a deep, bruising indigo. The air grew thin, cold, and silent, save for the violent, rhythmic HAAAAH... HAAAAH... of her desperate, burning lungs.
She began a frantic, brutal assault of close-quarters combat.
THUD! CRACK! SMASH!
Her knees slammed into his stomach, her elbows drove into his collarbone, and her palms struck his chest with the force of falling meteors. Each blow was a percussion of violence.
WHAM!
A palm strike to his jaw sent a spray of crimson blood from his lip, the red droplets freezing instantly into tiny rubies in the sub-zero air.
SPAT!

Rex was taking a beating that would have killed a lesser man. His vision was swimming, his lungs felt like they were filled with hot lead, and his left arm was a throbbing mess of bruised muscle and strained tendons.
But he was smiling. A bloody, manic, beautiful smile.
"There it is..." he gasped, coughing up a spray of red that hung in the void.
PHTOO!
"The... the raw... unrefined... power..."
He waited for the exact moment her momentum peaked, the moment her rage left a microscopic gap in her defense.
VREEEEEEEEE!
Rex didn’t push her away. He pulled her in.
He expanded a gravity singularity in the palm of his hand, right against her chest.
KRA BOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The sudden, massive increase in localized gravity acted like a vacuum, snapping her toward him and then violently repelling her as he inverted the field. The sudden shift in G-force was so violent it felt like their internal organs were being rearranged.
CRUNCH SPLATT!
The force of the sudden acceleration and deceleration sent a jolt through both of them. Ignivara’s head snapped back, her eyes wide with the sudden, disorienting shock.
Rex felt a rib finally give way, a sickening POP that he felt in his very teeth.
They tumbled through the thin atmosphere, a chaotic mess of limbs and fire, falling back toward the earth like a dying star.
FSSSSSSSSS!
As they plummeted, Ignivara recovered, her rage turning from a frantic fire into a cold, focused sun. She grabbed Rex by the throat, her fingers glowing with a lethal, white heat.
Sssssss!
"You want to see the end of the timeline, Rex?!" she screamed, her voice echoing through the heavens.
SKREEEEEEE!
"Then look at it!"
She gathered every ounce of her remaining energy, her entire body vibrating with the effort. The air around her began to warp and distort, a halo of golden destruction forming a sphere around her.
VREEEEEEEEEEEEE!
"DIE IN THE LIGHT!"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
She unleashed a point-blank explosion of pure draconic essence directly into his face, a supernova contained within the span of a heartbeat.
The explosion was absolute. A blinding, white gold supernova erupted from the point where Ignivara’s palms met Rex’s face.
KRA BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave was so violent it cleared the clouds for miles in every direction, leaving a hollowed-out void in the sky. Rex didn’t dodge.

He didn’t even attempt to shield himself. He took the full, unmitigated brunt of the draconic essence, the heat stripping the skin from his cheekbones and the pressure threatening to liquefy his very bones.
Sssssssssss!
As the light faded, Rex was a broken silhouette in the indigo sky. He was reeling, his body limp, trailing a long, shimmering ribbon of frozen blood and scorched essence.
His eyes were glazed, his breathing a shallow, rattling mess.
Haaa... huff... haaa...
Ignivara saw it. She saw the cracks in his composure.
She saw the man who had been an immovable mountain finally start to crumble. A primal, predatory triumph surged through her veins, overriding her exhaustion.
The rage wasn’t a wildfire anymore; it was a focused, laser-like intent to erase him from existence.
"Finally!" she shrieked, her voice a jagged tear in the atmosphere.
SKREEEEEEE!
"Finally, you’re breaking!"

chapters.title: Chapter 750. She Declared Victory Approximately Thirty Seconds Too Early.
paragraphs: She descended upon him like a falling star, her movements no longer just powerful but impossibly fast. She began a relentless, rhythmic execution of martial and magical fury.
WHAM!
A heavy, energy-infused kick caught him in the solar plexus.
OOF!
Rex’s body folded like parchment.
CRACK! THUD!
Before he could recover, she spun, her heel slamming into his jaw with the force of a wrecking ball.
KRA KOOM!
She didn’t stop. She became a blur of gold and white heat, a continuous loop of devastation.
WHAP WHAP WHAP WHAP!
A flurry of palm strikes rained down on his chest, each one sounding like a heavy mallet hitting wet clay.
SPLAT!
A punch to his gut sent a spray of crimson erupting from his mouth.
PHTOO!
VREEEEEEEEE!
She channeled her energy into her fingertips, firing rapid bolts of concentrated solar energy into his torso.
ZAP! ZAP! ZAP! ZAP!
Each bolt punched a smoking hole through his clothes and flesh, the smell of cauterized meat filling the air.
Sssssss!
She grabbed his head, her fingers digging into his temples, and slammed him downward with a telekinetic burst.
BOOM!
As he tumbled, she caught up to him, delivering a brutal knee to his spine.
CRUNCH!
The sound of his vertebrae grinding against each other was sickeningly loud in the thin air.
"Die!" she screamed, her voice a cacophony of divine fury. "Die! Die! DIE!"
KRA KOOOOM!

She unleashed a final, desperate combo: a spinning kick that shattered his ribs, followed by a double palm strike to his chest that shook his entire frame, and finally, a massive, overhead hammer fist aimed directly at his skull.
WHAM!
The impact was deafening.
THUD CRACK!
Rex was sent hurtling back toward the earth, a broken, bleeding wreck of a man, his body battered, bruised, and seemingly beyond the point of no return. He looked like a corpse caught in a hurricane.
Ignivara hovered in the air, her chest heaving, her hands trembling from the sheer output of her rage. She watched his descent, waiting for the final, silent impact.
She was ready to declare victory. She was ready to be done.
But the impact never came.
Midfall, Rex’s eyes snapped open.
They weren’t glazed anymore. They were piercing, cold, and terrifyingly lucid.
VREEEEEEEEEEE!
In a sudden, violent burst of telekinetic energy, Rex halted his descent, freezing in midair just meters above the rooftops.
Ignivara, still caught in the momentum of her final strike, lunged forward to finish him, her hands outstretched to crush his throat. But she didn’t hit soft, broken flesh.
She hit something that felt like solid granite.
CLACK!
With a movement so fast the human eye couldn’t even register it, Rex’s hands shot upward. He caught both of her wrists in a crushing grip.
CRUNCH.
Ignivara gasped, her eyes widening in shock. She tried to pull away, to flare her energy, to do anything, but she was anchored.
She was caught.
And then, she saw it.
The wounds were closing. The blackened, scorched flesh on his face was knitting itself back together in real time, the skin turning smooth and flawless as if the damage had never happened.
Sssssss...
The broken ribs snapped back into place with a series of wet, rhythmic pops.
POP! CRACK!
The massive bruises on his chest faded into nothingness, the blood that had been leaking from his mouth being reabsorbed into his body as his cells multiplied at an impossible, godlike rate.

His Supreme Healing and Infinite Regeneration were working with a terrifying, silent efficiency. Within seconds, the man who had been a broken wreck was once again the pristine, muscular titan she had first encountered.
Rex looked up at her. A slow, dark, and utterly predatory smile spread across his lips, a smile that promised a very different kind of end.
"You’ve had your fun, Ignivara," Rex said, his voice low, calm, and vibrating with a new, overwhelming power.
He tightened his grip on her wrists, his fingers feeling like unbreakable steel bands. "But the data is in."
"You’ve exhausted your variables."
He leaned in closer, his eyes glowing with an intense, terrifying light.
"This ends now..." he whispered, the air around him beginning to hum with a sudden, massive gravitational pressure. "...my turn."
Rex didn’t just move; he ceased to exist in one spot and materialized in another.
VWOOP!
Ignivara swung her claws at where he had been, but Rex was already behind her, his hand striking the back of her neck with the force of a falling building.
CLACK!
Her head snapped forward, and before she could recover, he was gone again.
VWOOP!
He reappeared at her flank, driving a concentrated burst of gravity into her side.
KRA BOOOOM!
The impact sent her spiraling, her body twisting violently in the thin air.
"What’s the matter?" Rex’s voice echoed from everywhere and nowhere. "Thought you had me figured out?"
VWOOP!
He was above her now. He fell like a stone, his knee crashing into her jaw with a sickening thud.
CRUNCH.
As she recoiled, he didn’t let up. He teleported again, appearing beneath her and delivering a precise kick to the small of her back.
THUD!
VWOOP!
He was in front of her again, his fingers digging into the pressure points of her shoulders.
SQUEEEEE!
Ignivara let out a sharp, agonizing shriek as he applied a crushing grip, a single, precise burst of telekinetic force that threatened to snap her clavicles.
"You’re out of time, Ignivara," Rex whispered, his voice cold and devoid of mercy. "This isn’t a fight anymore!"
"It’s an eviction!"
VWOOP!
He vanished and reappeared behind her, delivering a brutal, short-arc elbow to her kidney.
GURK!
She gasped, the air leaving her lungs in a ragged, bloody spray.
VWOOP! VWOOP! VWOOP!
He became a ghost of violence, a flicker of silver and steel.
WHACK!
A blow to the ear.
CRACK!
A palm strike to the bridge of her nose.
THUD!
A devastating knee to her stomach. Each time she tried to guard, he was already somewhere else, striking with a precision that turned her own momentum against her.
She was caught in a loop of endless, agonizing impacts, her body bouncing from one blow to the next like a pinball in a machine of pain.
"STOP IT!" she screamed, her voice a guttural, desperate sound.

In a final, desperate bid for survival, Ignivara’s body shuddered and expanded. With a deafening RRRRRRRUMBLE, she reverted to her massive dragon form in a split second, the sheer force of her transformation creating a shockwave that pushed Rex back.
FSSSSS BOOM!
Bellowing in primal rage, she lunged, her massive jaws snapping shut around Rex’s torso.
CHOMP!
Her teeth sank deep into his shoulder and chest, her powerful neck muscles tightening as she tried to crush him into oblivion.
Rex didn’t panic. He didn’t even flinch.
As the dragon’s teeth sank deeper, Rex reached up and slammed both palms against her upper and lower jaws.
CLANG!
His hands were like iron pylons, arresting her bite with a sudden, jarring halt.
SQUEEEEE!
The dragon’s eyes widened in shock; she had never encountered a mortal who could physically hold her maw open.
"Wrong move," Rex hissed, his eyes glowing with a lethal light.

He began to channel a massive, swirling vortex of energy in his palms, a fusion of gravity and telekinetic force. The air around them began to singe and warp, a high-pitched VREEEEEEEEEE that threatened to burst her eardrums.
"This is the end of the line."
KRA BOOOOOOOOOM!
He unleashed the fusion wave directly into her open maw. A beam of pure, blinding white energy roared down her throat, a concentrated pillar of destruction that bypassed all defenses.
Ignivara’s eyes rolled back as the energy surged through her, expanding and exploding from the inside.
BOOOOOMMMM!
The blast sent her reeling, her massive form convulsed by the internal detonation. But Rex wasn’t finished.
He surged forward, climbing her side, his fists becoming a blur of focused, brutal precision.
WHACK!
A right hook to her snout.
KRAK!
A left jab into her eye socket.
BOOM!
A double palm strike that shook her jaw.
CRACK! WHACK! SMASH!
He unleashed a devastating combo, his fists striking her face with the speed of a machine gun, each hit sounding like a thunderclap.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The dragon’s head whipped back and forth, blood spraying from her snout as her skull began to crack under the sheer pressure.
"Stay... down!"
Rex spun, gathering all his remaining momentum into one final, singular strike. He drove his fist deep into her soft underbelly, a punch that carried the weight of a mountain.
KRA BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The impact was catastrophic. The dragon’s eyes went blank as she was launched backward.
She became a golden streak, a falling star of flesh and scale, hurtling away from Aethelgard at impossible speeds.
VREEEEEEEEE!
She breached the sound barrier, a sonic boom echoing across the island.
BOOOOM!
She soared over the landscape, a doomed projectile, until she finally slammed into the uninhabited, desolate wasteland miles away from the city.
KRRRRRRRRRRAAAAAAAASH!!!
The ground shook as she crashed into a remote canyon, raising a massive plume of dust and debris. The impact crater was immense; the earth itself shattered by the force of her fall.
Rex stood alone in the sky, his chest heaving, his clothes tattered. He watched the distant plume of dust settle, his expression unreadable.
He had won, but the cost was written in the blood and bruises covering his body.
"Checkmate," he whispered to the wind.
